item.title: Campaign Organizer Elect Dan Osborn Flip The Senate
item.description: ampaign Organizer- Nebraska Location and Timeline: We are hiring a full-time Campaign Organizer to begin now and continue through Election Day. The locations are Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. This will expand over the program, so if you are a Nebraskan who lives further away or willing to relocate, please still apply! Who We Are: The Outreach Team is the national engine of campaigners and organizers building a fairer, cleaner, safer, and more peaceful world. We invest in people at every level with industry-leading pay/benefits, rigorous training and support and real paths to leadership. General Overview: Neighbor, it’s your time to step up for Nebraska. We need your love for our state and its people, your skills earned from years of hard work, and your ability to connect with other Nebraskans. Frankly, it’s the only way we are going to pry back our government and economy from the billionaires who have taken over. The good news is that there are more of us than there are of them. We just need to harness our power… conversation by conversation, on every porch, corner, driveway, sidewalk, field, and farm in Nebraska. And we need you to lead the charge. Join us on behalf of the Working Class Majority Pac. We are looking for Organizers to talk to voters about Dan Osborn’s run for Senate in Nebraska’s upcoming election. If you believe that real political power is built from the ground up through deep organizing and face-to-face conversations, we want you on our team in Scottsbluff, North Platte, Grand Island, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk. Organizers will be charged with recruiting, training, and working with a team of volunteers in key counties in Nebraska. The Organizer will start by building and recruiting a team of supporters and volunteers around canvassing. From there, Organizers will continue to engage volunteers through a series of campaign events and actions. Requirements: Valid driver's license and Insurance as well as a verifiable record of safe driving. Must be over 21 (in order to drive the rental car if needed) Must be available full-time. What You'll Do: Recruit and Train a Community of Volunteer Activists Call and text supporters and recruit them into grassroots actions. Identify new supporters and volunteers by knocking doors, gathering petitions, flyering, and conducting in-field recruitment efforts in the community and on local campuses. Run grassroots skills training to develop effective campaigners among volunteers. Keep meticulous track of a volunteer list so that no potential volunteer falls through the cracks. Represent the campaign through participation in community spaces and events, while engaging and uplifting coalition and partner organizations. Generate Campaign Actions Gather thousands of support cards from Dan Osborn supporters. Recruit and train volunteers to talk to voters. Recruit and engage with community leaders, organizational partners, and VIPs to build meaningful relationships while generating new supporters, volunteers, and event attendees. Knock on thousands of doors to educate voters about Dan Osborn and his platform. Manage Digital Campaign, Data Management, and Reporting Tools Demonstrate public support by recruiting volunteers to post on their own social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter. Use peer-to-peer texting services and relational organizing tools to communicate with community members. Write and send timely and compelling email campaigns to recruit activists to campaign activities. Track every interaction with detailed notes in order to report numbers daily and write weekly reports on the results of the campaign. Nail 100% of all messaging and legal requirements and ensure that volunteers do the same. Who You Are & Keys to Success (the must-haves): To be successful in this job, you will excel in these areas: Relationship Building: You develop and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with a diverse group of local and statewide community members. You are attentive and empathetic to the communities we serve, regardless of race, ethnicity, class, gender, or ability, and can identify shared values across communities for collective growth. You can build authentic relationships through authenticity and reliability, continuously uplifting others and their goals. You are comfortable and experienced in public speaking to a group about constituents around affordability and action opportunities. Inclusive and Collaborative Leadership: You approach leadership with a "power with" mindset that recognizes the impact power hierarchies have in different settings. You can learn from others, see and hear other perspectives, and step in or step back as necessary. You are reliable and accountable, always transparent about your abilities, capacities, and expectations. You honor the time and commitments of others while inspiring them to meet goals. Commitment to Equity and Inclusion: You have a proven ability to develop meaningful connections with diverse communities, including a wide range of community organizations, community leaders, and community members. You work with the community and within the workplace to identify areas of improvement for a more equitable environment. You take continued action and efforts to improve your REI knowledge, skills, and tools. Drive to Achieve Results: You have experience accomplishing ambitious goals and getting results, even when there are obstacles. You have the experience or ability to plan backwards to meet multiple goals timely and effectively. When there are unexpected changes, you bounce back and adjust quickly, learning and improving from any mistakes. Skills and Experiences we Expect of all Outreach Team employees: Commitment to equity and justice. Experience bringing a lens of inclusivity to all of your interactions with colleagues and community members. Passion for the role that your work plays in creating change in the world. Kindness and consideration for others. Drive to work collaboratively: learning from others; stepping-in or stepping-back when needed. Transparency: comfort admitting what you do and don't know, your capacity, and abilities. Task management: Able to adapt to the evolving needs of a project. Able to tackle big-picture projects and break them down into smaller pieces. Organized and efficient: Experience or demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects or goals at once in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment. Acute attention to detail: Track interactions and tasks with detailed notes. Plans ahead for roadblocks and bounces back quickly when problems arise. Effective communication skills (written or spoken) that are clear, concise and honest. Comfortable and excited to speak about the campaign publicly. Coach and learning mentality: successful experience or willingness to learn new things and pick up new skills on the job. Able to learn from mistakes and try again. Understanding of how your words and actions affect others, including an awareness of power language and communication accessibility. Ability to work weekends and weekday evenings, occasional holidays. Nice-to-Haves, but Not Required: Organizing experience in or around Grand Island, North Platte, Scottsbluff, Hastings, Alliance, Chadron, and Norfolk Nebraska. Experience working for nonprofits and issue campaigns. Data Management and Evaluation Experience: Experience working with various data management systems and tools, mainly Google Suite. Experience with Relevant Campaign Tools and Technologies: VAN, Action Network, ThruText, MailChimp, eCRMs like EveryAction, or social media tools (Twitter, Facebook, Instagram). Event or Project Planning & Management, Implementation or Evaluation. Knowledge or previous experience working in roles that support constituents around affordability and action opportunities is a plus If you were here right now, you would be: Recruiting, training, and developing volunteer leaders in your community to talk to their neighbors and community members about Dan Osborn. Completing your own shifts knocking doors to recruit volunteers and have in depth conversations about Dan Osborn for Senate. Engaging and expanding our support network through developing relationships with community leaders. Salary, Benefits and Perks: The salary for this position is $55,000 to $67,000 for full-time. We offer a generous benefits package, including paid vacation and sick leave, health insurance, and hands-on training. At the end of the campaign, there may be opportunities for advancement and bonuses. At The Outreach Team, we prioritize equity and inclusion. We are an equal opportunity employer and we strongly encourage Black, indigenous, people of color, women, people with previous felony convictions, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and others who identify with underrepresented groups to apply. To Apply: Visit: https://theoutreachteam.applytojob.com/apply

item.title: Summer Associate Internship Public Policy Assistant
item.description: Description The Summer Associate Program is a 12-week internship program beginning in May 2027 and ending in August 2027. Students will work on impactful projects and meaningful work during their internship. To qualify for this position, applicants must be currently pursuing a degree from an accredited college or university and have an anticipated graduation date of December 2027 or later. As part of Navy Federal's Military Affairs & Strategic Partnerships (MA&SP) department, GRPP collaborates closely with business units across the enterprise to assess policy implications, support strategic decision-making, and represent Navy Federal's interests before policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and other external stakeholders. The Public Policy Assistant Summer Associate will support the team's policy research, reporting, and operational activities. The associate will help maintain legislative, regulatory, stakeholder engagement, and project-tracking efforts that support the team's advocacy and strategic priorities. Responsibilities may include data analysis, reporting, process improvement, policy research, and the development of materials that help inform decision-making and increase visibility into GRPP activities across the enterprise. This role will provide exposure to public policy, government relations, stakeholder engagement, and cross-functional collaboration. Potential Projects Include: Support the collection, organization, and analysis of data related to legislative, regulatory, advocacy, stakeholder engagement, and project activities. Assist in preparing weekly, monthly, quarterly, and ad hoc reports, executive summaries, briefing materials, and presentations for senior leadership and internal stakeholders. Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations that provide insights into policy developments, advocacy activities, stakeholder engagement, and team performance metrics. Support the tracking and management of team projects, action items, external engagements, and strategic initiatives to improve visibility and operational efficiency. Conduct research on federal and state legislative proposals, regulatory actions, and emerging public policy issues affecting credit unions, financial services, and military-affiliated communities. Perform industry benchmarking and trend analysis to support advocacy priorities and strategic planning efforts. Assist with preparing background materials, stakeholder summaries, and briefing documents for meetings with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and internal business partners. Collaborate with business units across the enterprise to gather information and support policy-related initiatives and reporting. Complete a capstone project focused on improving GRPP's reporting, knowledge management, or operational processes, resulting in recommendations and tools that create long-term value for the team. Responsibilities Support the monitoring and tracking of legislative, regulatory, and public policy developments relevant to Navy Federal and the credit union industry. Conduct research and gather information from legislative, regulatory, industry, and internal sources to support policy analysis and advocacy efforts. Assist with maintaining records of team activities, stakeholder engagements, policy developments, and strategic initiatives. Compile, organize, and analyze data to support team reporting, metrics, and leadership updates. Prepare presentations, briefing materials, summaries, and reports for internal stakeholders and senior leadership. Support project management activities by tracking action items, milestones, and deliverables across multiple initiatives. Collaborate with business units and internal partners to collect information and support cross-functional projects. Help identify opportunities to improve team processes, reporting capabilities, and operational efficiency. Participate in team meetings, stakeholder engagements, and professional development activities to gain exposure to government relations and public policy functions. Qualifications Pursuing a degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, Law, or a related field. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to research, gather, and organize information from a variety of sources. Ability to manage multiple assignments and meet deadlines. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment. Demonstrated interest in public policy, government, financial services, advocacy, or related fields. Desired Qualifications Coursework or project experience in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Economics, Business, Communications, or a related field. Experience conducting research, analyzing information, or preparing reports and presentations through coursework, internships, student organizations, or other experiences. Familiarity with data analysis, reporting, data visualization, or business intelligence concepts. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Experience using Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint to organize information and communicate findings. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries and recommendations. Experience balancing multiple projects, priorities, or extracurricular commitments. Interest in legislative affairs, regulatory issues, government relations, military affairs, consumer financial services, or the credit union industry. Demonstrated leadership through student organizations, volunteer activities, community involvement, athletics, military service, or other experiences. Additional Information Hours: Monday – Friday, 8:00 AM – 4:30 PM Location: 820 Follin Ln SE, Vienna, VA 22180

item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Description GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES The Public Policy Team works to protect our state’s business climate and regional reputation by supporting key policies at the state and local levels that affect metro Atlanta's economy, talent, and community. The Coordinator role on the Government Affairs team will assist the Public Policy team with legislative tracking, research, administrative tasks, attending and summarizing legislative meetings, monitoring activities at various levels of government, attending and representing the chamber at various meetings, and other tasks as assigned. The Coordinator will report to the Manager of Government Affairs, while collaborating with all Public Policy team members and departments at the chamber. Preferred skills for this role include an understanding of the legislative process and an eagerness for continued growth, the ability to manage multiple responsibilities, strong attention to detail, and the ability to communicate professionally to ensure MAC's success in the public policy sphere. Our ideal candidate is a high-achiever, self-starter, and team player with an interest in deepening their understanding of Georgia’s political landscape and policy skills. Successful candidates will be organized, possess strong networking and communication skills, and demonstrate the ability to manage multiple projects without constant supervision. DAY-TO-DAY DUTIES INCLUDE: Legislative Develop a strong understanding of MAC’s legislative priorities, and work alongside team members to craft strategies and tactics to implement key priorities Monitor, research, and track in real-time legislative activity at the state and local government levels that could impact Georgia and the metro Atlanta region Assist with scheduling and executing meetings with elected officials, executive and legislative staff, business and civic community partners, coalitions, and key stakeholders Manage team-specific documents and resources that are critical to the team's operations and performance at the state capitol Conduct research and prepare policy summaries, briefing forms, talking points, letters of support, etc. Interact wit h federal, state, and local elected officials, department and agency leads, and their staff Assist with coalition building and stakeholder outreach around key legislative priorities Support and assist with the biennial development of the Metro Atlanta Chamber’s policy agenda and legislative priorities Build relationships with key campaign, fundraising, and political staff members Attend outside meetings, conferences, legislative functions, and other job-related events as directed. Administrative Manage accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, and reporting for Metro Atlanta Chamber Political Action Committee (MACPAC) Plan and execute administrative tasks for political entities including accounting, budgeting, financial oversight, ethics reporting, scheduling, communications, etc. Oversee operations of various entities, including fundraising, consultant management and oversight, board communications, ethics reporting, compliance, etc. Coordinate and execute the public policy team's state-mandated ethics reporting Event and Communications Support Assist with planning and execution of chamber events, meetings, initiatives, and other policy events attended by investors, elected officials, staff, and partners. Coordinate and draft internal and external updates on chamber priorities and key legislation Assist with creating department communications, social media, website/blog content, etc. External Foster relationships with MAC members, business community partners, lobbyists, government officials, and government staff Plan and execute meetings with elected officials and staff outside of the metro Atlanta region Perform other duties as assigned. QUALIFICATIONS: One to three years of experience preferred in government affairs, public policy, executive or legislative branch, community affairs, non-profit advocacy, regulatory affairs, or political campaigns Familiarity with the legislative process and Georgia’s political landscape, along with a continued eagerness to grow Ability to quickly synthesize legislation, regulations, data, and strategies, and to communicate them to team members and senior leaders Exceptional attention to detail, organizational skills, and verbal and written communication skills Excellent social and interpersonal skills; capacity to interact with a wide variety of people in government, politics, and civic and business leadership Ability to quickly identify barriers to success and devise strategies or tactics to remove or mitigate them Ability to maintain a non-partisan approach in all respects, work with all members of the executive departments and agencies, and the General Assembly and their staffs Self-starter, capable of working both independently and collaboratively with other team members to produce desired outcomes High energy, versatile, and able to multitask; flexible, able to adapt to changing priorities and plans Qualifications The Metro Atlanta Chamber (MAC) serves as a catalyst for a more prosperous and vibrant metro Atlanta. To advance economic growth and improve our quality of place, MAC is focused on starting, growing, and recruiting companies to our 29-county region. We're also focused on growing our innovation economy by promoting and strengthening connections to drive Atlanta's innovation and entrepreneurial culture. MAC is committed to being an active voice for the business community, serving as an advocate for a competitive business climate, advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion as economic imperatives, and telling Atlanta's story. Our Purpose, Principles, and Core Values MAC's purpose is to UNLEASH ATLANTA'S AMBITION, and in doing so we embody the following principles: Sit Down Together, Stand Up to Act Knock Down Walls, Open Doors Take the Lead, Share the Credit Sharpen the Focus, Expand the Reach At MAC, we naturally exhibit an unwavering commitment to three core values: to be relentless, smart, and all-in . This means every team member is: Relentless . MAC employees take pride in being relentless with an unwavering focus. Our partners trust us to deliver on our commitments. There isn't room for cutting corners, being aimless, or rejecting change. We are bold and persistent and execute with innovation and edge. Smart . Team members at MAC know that intense curiosity allows us to grow. We leverage instinct, integrity, and data to drive our strategy and achieve our purpose. As problem-solving idea generators, we have a natural advantage in any challenge. All-In. We're a greater force when we rally together. It doesn't matter what our title or position is: we trust each other and work as one to multiply our collective impact and achieve ambitious goals.

item.title: Congressional Affairs Specialist
item.description: Title: Congressional Affairs Specialist Location: Washington, DC 20004 Schedule: Full-time Pay: $160,000-$190,000 annually, commensurate with experience ROLE KMRG, LLC (KMRG) is a federal services company that hires talented professionals to support Government agencies and the communities they serve. We are hiring an experienced Congressional Affairs Specialist to support the Inter-American Foundation (IAF). In this role, you will provide senior-level subject matter expertise supporting congressional and interagency reporting, stakeholder engagement, legislative and appropriations analysis, and executive communications. You will advise and support IAF leadership while Government decisions and approvals remain with IAF. Applications will be reviewed as they are received. Apply today! RESPONSIBILITIES Congressional & Interagency Affairs Serve as a subject matter expert on federal and IAF reporting requirements and U.S. national security alignment Provide technical advice and assistance on IAF engagement with Congress and interagency stakeholders Track and communicate congressional and interagency updates, contacts, emerging issues, and stakeholder interests Monitor laws, legislative history, hearings, OMB circulars, regulations, and controls affecting IAF reporting and oversight Prepare and coordinate congressional RFIs, reports, and related materials for leadership review and approval Facilitate engagement with Congress, the Department of State, OMB, and other interagency stakeholders as needed Executive Communications, Planning & Reporting Advise IAF leadership on congressional and interagency matters Draft and edit executive briefings, talking points, memoranda, testimony, Q&A materials, and sensitive communications Coordinate with the Communications Team on external-facing publications and materials Develop an annual external-affairs workplan covering key reports, projects, and engagement milestones Prepare monthly status reports on projects, priorities, milestones, and completed tasks for IAF leadership Support congressional and interagency oversight travel and external-facing events when delegated and approved Prepare a final close-out report and transition memo covering completed work, key contacts, files, and ongoing tasks Participate in kick-off, orientation, routine check-ins, and other required meetings with staff and external stakeholders REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS U.S. citizenship Fluency in English and Spanish, oral and written Bachelor’s degree in political science, public administration, public policy, law, international relations, communications, or a related field Minimum 10 years of relevant experience working with Capitol Hill and U.S. executive agencies Strong understanding of legislative and executive branches, including appropriations, budgeting, congressional oversight Experience analyzing legislation, statutory language, and committee reports for operational, legal, or budgetary impacts Experience drafting sensitive executive briefings, testimony, and Q&A materials for congressional or interagency engagements Strong plain-language writing skills and ability to distill complex information into concise executive materials under tight deadlines Experience preparing and clearing responses to Congressional Letters of Inquiry, RFIs, and annual reporting requirements Ability to build effective relationships with cross-agency teams, congressional staff, White House liaisons, and interagency partners Ability to stay current on laws, hearings, OMB guidance, regulations, and controls affecting federal reporting and oversight Strong analytical judgment and the ability to provide timely technical guidance to senior leadership Strong computer skills, including word processing, spreadsheet programs, and contacts database management Ability to manage recurring reports, deadlines, meetings, and stakeholder requests with accuracy and continuity Ability to comply with IAF security, privacy, IT, and operational requirements PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Experience in the foreign assistance or international development space Regional familiarity with Latin America and the Caribbean LOCATION TRAVEL Local travel in the Washington, D.C. area is expected 1-2 times per week 2-3 week-long trips per year beyond local travel radius to support congressional and interagency oversight visits SECURITY & ACCESS REQUIREMENTS Must successfully complete, at minimum, a National Agency Check with Written Inquiries (NACI) Must complete required identity verification, fingerprinting, suitability screening, and PIV credentialing before receiving unsupervised access to IAF facilities or systems Must complete IAF IT Security Awareness Training before accessing IAF computers or networks IAF systems and data may only be accessed using authorized Government-furnished equipment (GFE) ****************** KMRG, LLC is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action (EEO/AA) employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, ancestry, national origin, age, marital or civil partnership status, mental disability, physical disability, medical condition, pregnancy, maternity status, political affiliation, military or veteran status, genetic information, traits historically associated with race, or any other basis prohibited by federal, state, and/or local law.

item.title: Legislative Affairs Coordinator
item.description: BATTERY COUNCIL INTERNATIONAL Legislative Affairs Coordinator Full-time · Washington, DC area required (work from home within the DC area) · Reports to the VP, Government Relations & Sustainability Salary range: $70,000–$90,000, plus bonus and benefits About BCI Battery Council International is the century-old trade association for the North American battery industry. We lead the industry’s federal and state advocacy on recycling, extended producer responsibility, transport, and safety, alongside our technical, data, and sustainability programs. We are a small, remote team, and we are building our state and federal advocacy capability in-house. The role This is the engine room of our advocacy program. You will track what is happening in legislatures across the country, flag what matters, and help BCI act on it. You will also assist with federal matters when state sessions quiet down in the second half of the year. It is a great role for someone early in a government-affairs career who wants real ownership and a national view of policy. What you’ll do Track fifty-state activity — monitor legislation and regulation affecting the battery industry across all states via BCI’s tracking database, and keep a current, reliable picture of what is moving. Watch the federal side — review the Federal Register daily for regulatory actions affecting the industry, follow federal legislation, and keep an eye on industry listservs. Summarize and report — turn developments into concise summaries and tracking reports, and maintain an ongoing issues-management report for the team and members. Write it up — draft articles and updates on policy issues for BCI’s digital publications and website. Support state outreach — help advance BCI’s policy priorities and coordinate with members and allied organizations. Back up federal advocacy — lend a hand on federal work as needed. What you bring A bachelor’s degree in political science, energy, public policy, related field, or equivalent experience. Roughly two to five years of experience in government affairs, legislative tracking, policy research, or a closely related field — strong internship experience considered for early-career candidates. Familiarity with how state (and ideally federal) legislative and regulatory processes work. Sharp research and writing, strong organization, and real attention to detail across a high volume of material. The self-direction to manage a broad workload well on a home-based, distributed team. Nice to have Exposure to environmental, recycling, product-stewardship, or manufacturing policy. Experience with a legislative-tracking platform (Bloomberg Government, Politico, or similar) and with coalition work. What we offer Competitive pay in the range above, plus an annual bonus. A 5% 401(k) match and medical, dental, and vision coverage. Paid time off and a work-from-home schedule based in the DC area, with occasional travel and in-person meetings. A national view of policy and genuine ownership of BCI’s state program, early in your career. Exposure to international policy and global battery-association work. How to apply Submit a resume and cover letter. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the position is open until filled. Please tell us where in the DC area you are based. Equal opportunity BCI is an equal-opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. We are committed to an inclusive hiring process and will provide reasonable accommodation to applicants with disabilities on request at any stage. Contact [email protected] to request accommodations. Battery Council International · batterycouncil.org · The salary range reflects the band for this role; the actual offer depends on experience and work location under BCI’s geographic pay framework.

item.title: Legislative Affairs Assistant
item.description: Job Requisition ID: 59213 BPIS #: 09236 Opening Date: 10/02/2026 Closing Date: 10/19/2026 Agency: Department of Healthcare and Family Services Class Title: ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT II - 00502 Skill Option: None Bilingual Option: None Salary: Anticipated starting salary range $6,500 -$8,000 monthly Job Type: Salaried Category: Full Time Number of Vacancies: 1 Bargaining Unit Code: None Merit Comp Code: Confidential (Management Bill) Exclusion from RC028 Collective Bargaining Coverage Work Hours: Monday - Friday 8:30am - 5:00pm Anticipated Hybrid Work Schedule Availability: It is required that a person reports to the headquarters on this job position as necessary (could be weekly, monthly, or other schedule) dependent on operational need Headquarter Location: 201 S Grand Ave E, Springfield, Illinois, 62704 Work County: Sangamon Agency Contact: HFS.DPASApps@illinois.gov A resume is highly encouraged to evaluate your qualifications and skills as part of your application. Please attach a DETAILED Resume/Curriculum Vitae (CV) to the MY DOCUMENTS section of your application if you decide to provide one. Why Work for Illinois? Working with the State of Illinois is a testament to the values of compassion, equity, and dedication that define our state. Whether you’re helping to improve schools, protect our natural resources, or support families in need, you’re part of something bigger—something that touches the lives of every person who calls Illinois home. No matter what state career you’re looking for, we offer jobs that fit your life and your schedule—flexible jobs that provide the gold standard of benefits. Our employees can take advantage of various avenues to advance their careers and realize their dreams. Our top-tier benefits and great retirement packages can help you build a rewarding career and lasting future with the State of Illinois. Position Overview The Department of Healthcare and Family Services is seeking to hire a motivated and courteous individual to serve as a Legislative Affairs Assistant for the Office of Legislative Affairs. The Staff Assistant will perform a variety of sensitive and controversial administrative duties to assist with the operations of the office. Additionally, this position will respond to inquiries from members of Congress, Illinois General Assembly and other parties along with organizing special projects for the manager. The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of the legislative process, excellent communication and research skills, and keen interest in public policy and government affairs. HFS values employees with different backgrounds, life experiences, and talents. Essential Functions Serves as Legislative Affairs Assistant to the Chief of the Office of Legislative Affairs Conducts controversial and/or sensitive studies and investigations of legislative issues concerning the agency’s programs Responds to a variety of sensitive and confidential inquiries from members of Congress, the Illinois General Assembly, recipients and/or their representatives, medical providers and the general public Serves as a management liaison for the Chief with department, Governor’s Office, legislative, and Department of Central Management Services’ staff and with other groups involved with the operations and activities of the agency Develops responses to constituent inquiries concerning agency programs and operations Plans, develops and organizes special projects for the Chief Compiles information and develops briefings for the Chief on issues affecting the agency Performs other duties as required or assigned which are reasonably within the scope of the duties enumerated above Minimum Qualifications Requires knowledge, skill, and mental development equivalent to completion of four (4) years of college preferably with courses in public or business administration Requires two (2) years of professional experience in a public or private organization Preferred Qualifications Two (2) years of professional experience serving as a staff assistant working for executive level management Two (2) years of professional experience conducting special projects and evaluating existing and/or proposed programs Two (2) years of professional experience working for a public or private organization maintaining confidentiality and handling sensitive information with professionalism Two (2) years of professional experience serving as a liaison for executive level management in meetings Two (2) years of professional experience coordinating assignments for executive level management Two (2) years of professional experience responding to program and operational inquiries from agency staff, other agencies, and the public Two (2) years of professional experience working with internal and external stakeholders Two (2) years of professional experience utilizing verbal and written communication skills Conditions of Employment Requires completion of a background check and self-disclosure of criminal history Requires the ability to utilize and maintain state issued equipment such as a laptop Requires ability to travel in the performance of duties, with overnight stays as appropriate Overtime is a condition of employment, and you may be requested or required/mandated to work overtime including scheduled, unscheduled, or last-minute overtime. This may require the ability to work evenings and weekends The conditions of employment listed here are incorporated and related to any of the job duties as listed in the job description About the Agency At the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS), we value staff as our greatest asset. We work in a spirit of teamwork to help millions of Illinoisans access high quality healthcare and fulfill child support obligations to advance their physical, mental, and financial well-being. We provide healthcare coverage for children and adults through Medicaid and other medical programs, and we help ensure that children receive financial resources from both their parents through Child Support Services. The HFS Office of the Inspector General investigates, audits and reviews program activity to ensure the integrity of our programs is maintained. HFS is committed to promoting and preserving a workplace culture that embraces diversity, equity, and inclusion. We welcome and value employees with different backgrounds, life experiences, and talents. It is the collective sum of our individual differences that provides a broad perspective, leading to greater innovation and achievement. In recruiting for our team, we recognize the unique contributions of each applicant regardless of culture, ethnicity, race, national origin, sex, gender identity and expression, age, religion, disability, and sexual orientation. HFS is an equal opportunity employer. Benefits Statement Employees receive a robust benefit package including: Monday-Friday work schedule Flexible work schedules are available in many program areas. (Remote work may be an option for certain positions.) Health, Life, Vision, and Dental Insurance Pension Plan Paid Maternity/Paternity Leave Deferred Compensation Program and other pre-tax benefit programs (Medical/Daycare) Employees earn (12) paid Sick Days annually. New Employees earn (10) paid Vacation Days their first year of service and can earn up to (25) paid Vacation Days annually. Employees earn (3) paid Personal Days annually. (13-14) paid holidays annually (based on start date) If you are seeking a new opportunity, and this position appeals to you, please apply today! ​ The main form of communication will be through email. Please check your “junk mail”, “spam”, or “other” folder for communication(s) regarding any submitted application(s). You may receive emails from the following addresses: donotreply@SIL-P1.ns2cloud.com systems@SIL-P1.ns2cloud.com

item.title: Co Op Government Affairs
item.description: California, US residents click here . The job details are as follows: Who We Are We are the first publicly-traded biotech or pharmaceutical company to take the form of a public benefit corporation. Our public benefit purpose is to provide a brighter future for patients through the development of novel pharmaceutical therapies; and technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs. United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) seeks to travel down the corridors of indifference to develop treatments for rare, deadly diseases. We were founded in 1996 by a family seeking a cure for their daughter’s pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Today, we have six FDA-approved therapies that treat PAH, pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and neuroblastoma, a rare pediatric cancer. Our near-term pipeline seeks to develop additional therapies for PAH and pulmonary fibrosis (PF). The cure for end-stage life-threatening diseases like PAH, PH-ILD, PF, and many others is an organ transplant, but only a small percentage of donated organs are available to address the vast need. For this reason, we are working to create manufactured organs to address the shortage of kidneys, hearts, lungs, and livers available for transplant. We believe an unlimited supply of tolerable, transplantable organs will eliminate the transplant waiting list and cure end-stage organ diseases for which transplant is not currently an option. Who You Are As a Fall 2026 Government Affairs Co-Op, you will work closely in collaboration with the Investor Relations, Strategic Operations, Risk Management and Corporate Real Estate departments at United Therapeutics Corporation (UT). In this role, you will support the Government Affairs department in their engagement with local, state, federal, and international governments, advancement of policy, and tackling regulatory issues. This co-op will allow you to prepare materials and attend meetings and briefings on the changing political environment and advance advocacy efforts. Throughout this co-op, you will be given the opportunity to develop strong communication skills (written and verbal), advanced people skills, and a working knowledge of government affairs and community outreach. This co-op is available in-person at our Silver Spring location on a six-month term. Due to the nature of government affairs, all co-ops will be primarily in-office. Research Research upcoming legislation that could affect United Therapeutics, our patients or our business. Maintain and expand UT’s use of legislation tracking software. Analyze legislation, then summarize the potential effects of that legislation on United Therapeutics, our patients, or our business. Travel to UT locations across the country to engage with lobbyists and local partners. Monitor and report on the evolving political and regulatory environment both for life sciences and regulatory decision making. Advocacy Advocate for United Therapeutics in relationship-building activities with government entities. Work to detail policy agendas to help propel United Therapeutics toward its advocacy goals. Attend meetings to gain insight from clients, local government officials, and relevant stakeholders. Travel to conferences and stakeholder gatherings across the country to represent the Government Affairs team in industry-specific policy settings. Reporting Update UT’s reporting obligations with local, state, and federal governments. Help support policy development in compliance with emerging regulatory requirements. Assist in the preparation of official documents (reports, memos, and other communication for both external and internal distribution). Minimum Requirements: Junior or Senior currently enrolled in an accredited undergraduate program; graduate students currently enrolled in accredited MPP, MPH, or JD programs are also welcome to apply. Interest in government affairs, policy, advocacy, and United Therapeutics’ mission. Interest in health policy, life sciences, and biotechnology with the pharmaceutical industry. Strong research and analytical skills. Good communication abilities (written and verbal). Proficiency in Microsoft Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Preferred Qualifications: Majoring in Natural Sciences, Economics, Public Policy, History, Pre-Law or Political Science preferred. Other majors are welcome to apply. Prior experience working in government affairs, campaigns, or a related field. ***Please include a cover letter with your application*** Job Location United Therapeutics requires this candidate to be on-site at our Silver Spring, MD location 100% of the time. This role will require a substantial amount of domestic travel. The salary for this position ranges from $22.50 to $26.50 per hour. The salary range is the range United Therapeutics Corporation in good faith believes is the range of possible compensation for this role at the time of this posting depending on the candidate’s experience, qualifications, geographic location, and other factors permitted by law. The Company may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range. This range may be modified in the future. No amount is considered to be wages or compensation until such amount is earned, vested, and determinable under the terms and conditions of the applicable policies and plans. The amount and availability of any bonus, commission, benefits, or any other form of compensation and benefits that are allocable to a particular employee remains in the Company's sole discretion unless and until paid and may be modified at the Company’s sole discretion, consistent with the law. At United Therapeutics, our mission and vision are one. We use our enthusiasm, creativity, and persistence to innovate for the unmet medical needs of our patients and to benefit our other stakeholders. We are bold and unconventional. We have fun, we do good. Eligible employees may participate in the Company’s comprehensive benefits suite of programs, including medical / dental / vision / prescription coverage, employee wellness resources, savings plans (401k and ESPP), paid time off & paid parental leave benefits, disability benefits, and more. For additional information on Company benefits, please visit https://www.unither.com/careers/benefits-and-amenities United Therapeutics Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer, including veterans and individuals with disabilities.

item.title: Political Science Faculty Member
item.description: $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly About Holyoke Community College: Holyoke Community College is housed on a multi-million-dollar, 135-acre campus, equipped with state-of-the art technology in specialized learning facilities. HCC serves over 9,000 students annually, and provides a variety of recreational and cultural activities, from sports programs to music festivals, for students and community members alike. The college's strongest assets continue to be an innovative spirit, a sincere concern for students and a commitment to strive for even greater success. These are the values which have created a tradition of excellence spanning more than six decades, and which are enabling Holyoke Community College to meet today's challenges. Mission : Educate. Inspire. Connect. Values: Kindness, Inclusion, Trust, Innovation & Collaboration Kindness, inclusion and trust are the foundation of the work that we do together. Innovation and collaboration enable us to explore and implement the ideas that will shape our future. The Critical Social Thought (CST) Department at Holyoke Community College seeks a full-time tenure-track faculty member to bring vision and innovation to Political Science courses within the department’s CST Option. We seek candidates who will bring a broad grounding in US Political Science to the department, and who can enhance our course offerings with specialized areas of expertise. Candidates with research or teaching in US National Politics, State and Local Politics, Civics, Civil Liberties, Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics are particularly encouraged to apply. Our ideal candidate will continue the department’s tradition of interdisciplinary teaching with colleagues across campus and engaging with the external community via community-based learning. As part of the college’s efforts to ensure equitable outcomes for all HCC students, candidates must bring a demonstrated commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in their teaching practice, as well as a record of excellence in college-level instruction. Primary responsibilities include: teaching lecture classes on general US Political Science topics as well as electives that serve the needs of students in our program as well as other degree programs; strengthening the ongoing development of our CST academic program via assessment and curriculum development; participating in college governance, recruitment and retention efforts; and professional development. In addition to teaching experience, candidates should also demonstrate a commitment to student-centered advising, and to building partnerships that will enhance students’ opportunities for career and transfer. Such partnerships may include internal collaborations with colleagues in the CST department and in the Latinx Studies program as well as external collaborations to expand career and transfer opportunities for students who major in CST and Latinx programs. Although hybrid teaching options may be available, this position will require a substantial amount of in-person, on-campus work with students, faculty, and community partners. Teaching US Political Science lecture courses, in particular general US National as well as State and Local Politics surveys, and courses that address specific subfields in Political Science relevant to the faculty member’s expertise. Ability to teach Immigration, Transnational Politics, and Latinx Politics is of particular interest. Working closely with colleagues in Critical Social Thought Department and across campus, develop innovative teaching methods; expand community-engaged learning initiatives; continue a commitment to innovative, inclusive, discovery-based and critically engaged curricula; incorporate technology in the classroom; develop and implement new courses as appropriate that serve the students’ academic needs, and strengthen the ongoing development of our CST academic program. Advising students in the CST program and related majors. Meeting with and assisting students during regular office hours. Actively participating in department, division, and professional staff meetings as well as other components of college governance. Maintaining professional expertise in areas of specialization. Participating in college programs and activities. Assisting the Dean, Associate Dean, and Chair of the Critical Social Thought Department to establish and maintain existing academic partnerships with related college programs as well as expand articulation agreements with external college and university programs. Providing college service as required by the MCCC contract, including participation in shared governance committees, sub-committees, or task forces. Minimum Qualifications: Master’s degree in Political Science or closely related field, with the ability to teach standard survey courses (US National, State and Local Government, Civil Liberties) as well as specialized courses within US Political Science and across disciplines; Teaching experience in higher education, specifically as instructor of record; Demonstrated excellent teaching skills including interactive teaching, varied pedagogical strategies, and culturally responsive pedagogies; Experience using instructional technology across teaching modalities (i.e. in physical, hybrid, and online classes) to enable student success; Experience working successfully with a diverse student body, staff, and faculty; Effective communication skills and ability to work collaboratively on projects and initiatives. Equivalency Statement: We welcome and encourage applicants who do not meet the qualifications as stated above, to put in writing precisely how their background and experience have prepared them for the responsibilities of this position. It is preferred that this document be uploaded separately from the resume, cover letter, and references. Preferred Qualifications: A record of teaching excellence in Political Science at a community college or at the first year/sophomore college level; Ph. D in Political Science or closely related field; Interest in promoting and participating in interdisciplinary learning; Ability to provide leadership within an academic department that will contribute to growth, innovation, and excellence in alignment with institutional goals; Bilingual (English/Spanish). Full-Time, Tenure-Track MCCC/MTA Position: Salary Range: $58,722.00 - $70,786.00. Actual salary will be commensurate with education and experience in accordance with MCCC/MTA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Full State benefits. Funding: State. Start Date: Fall, 2027. Additional Details: Applicants must include a CV, cover letter, and syllabus in one of the following areas: US National Government, State & Local Government, or Civil Liberties. A teaching demonstration is a required part of the interview process. Disability Accommodations: Holyoke Community College is committed to the full inclusion of individuals with disabilities and will ensure the availability of reasonable accommodations. If a reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact the Office of People and Talent at (413) 552-2554. Background Check: Employment is contingent upon the successful completion and review of a background check which will include CORI (Criminal Offender Record Information) and SORI (Sex Offender Registry Information). All candidates must have legal authorization to work in the United States. HCC is not sponsoring H1B Visa. Holyoke Community College is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, disability, religion, age, veteran status, genetic information, gender identity or sexual orientation in its programs and activities as required by Title IX of the Educational Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, and other applicable statutes and college policies. The College prohibits sexual harassment, including sexual violence. Inquiries or complaints concerning discrimination, harassment, retaliation or sexual violence shall be referred to the College’s Affirmative Action and/or Title IX Coordinator, the Massachusetts Commission Against Discrimination, the Equal Employment Opportunities Commission or the United States Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights. Holyoke, Massachusetts, United States $58,722 - $70,786 USD yearly

item.title: Federal Affairs Civil Commercial Lobbyist
item.description: Date Posted: 2026-10-05 Country: United States of America Location: US-VA-ARLINGTON-108 ~ 1100 Wilson Blvd ~ ROSSLYN HQ Position Role Type: Onsite U.S. Citizen, U.S. Person, or Immigration Status Requirements: Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the company’s immigration sponsorship now or in the future. The company will not offer immigration sponsorship for this position.​ The company will not seek an export authorization for this role. Security Clearance Type: None/Not Required Security Clearance Status: Not Required At RTX, the world's largest aerospace and defense company, 185,000 great minds are united by purpose and inspired to make a difference solving the world’s most complex problems. With our three market leading businesses, world-class operations and investments in research and development, we offer capabilities and opportunity no one else can. Together, we push the boundaries of known science and find new ways to connect and protect our world. Join us and help shape the future of aerospace and defense. RTX is looking for a talented Federal Affairs, Civil Commercial Lobbyist to join our corporate legal team. This position will lead a portfolio for the federal government relations lobbying team focused on civil space, energy & environment, oversight and investigations, research & development priorities in addition to Commerce, Justice, and Science (CJS) and Energy & Water Appropriations, for all three RTX businesses (Collins Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon). This lobbyist will foster relationships with U.S. government (Executive and Legislative Branches) and internal RTX business leaders while raising the RTX profile. This lobbyist will develop overall RTX government relations strategy in the assigned service/capability portfolio mentioned above policy areas across all three business areas, as well as promote and oversee RTX service legislative priorities specific to the Raytheon Technologies Research Center. What You Will Do: Develop and implement a comprehensive government relations strategy to successfully achieve RTX legislative priorities particularly related to civil space, energy, research & development, oversight & investigations and additional funding from the Appropriations Committees and relevant authorizing mechanisms of the House of Representatives and the Senate. Within this portfolio, lead government relations efforts by identifying and supporting policymaking opportunities and funding opportunities that advance the objectives and successful execution of the service/capability programs of all three business units. Advise the Presidents of the three RTX business units and other senior business leaders on all federal legislative matters that may affect the successful execution and funding of their programs. Develop and maintain relationships with key U.S. government customers/officials to identify opportunities of aligned interest, shape requirements & influence laws and regulations in support of all RTX related products and services. Collaborate with government affairs team leads to enhance RTX’s presence in Washington, DC with respect to assigned programs to create a national platform on which these programs positions, needs, and priorities can be articulated. Provide insight, guidance and support to RTX program managers, their direct reports, the Executive Vice President for Global Government Relations and key company leaders on program standing on budgetary, legislative and regulatory matters being considered by Members of Congress, their staffs, and the Appropriations Committees and authorizing committees of jurisdiction in the House of Representatives and the Senate. Coordinate internally with the Civil Commercial Team Lead and the Manager of RTXPAC to develop a strategy and attend events in support the company’s political action committee. Represent RTX interests on Capitol Hill at hearings, help prepare company leaders for Hill testimony when required, and provide briefings to Members of Congress, their staff and key Congressional committee professional staff on RTX programs. Qualifications You Must Have: Typically requires: A University Degree or equivalent experience and minimum 10 years prior relevant experience, or an Advanced Degree in a related field and minimum 7 years experience. Relevant experience working with Members of Congress and their staff, and committees (RTX considers several factors when extending an offer and determining grade including years of experience and advanced degrees). Knowledge of the legislative processes and associated funding mechanisms such as the annual appropriations bills. Previous experience working on Capitol Hill is required. Experience working with or on the portfolio’s committee jurisdiction a plus (CJS and/or Energy & Water Appropriations and/or House Energy & Commerce; House Science, Space, and Technology and/or Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation). Qualifications We Prefer: Ability to operate independently across a highly-matrixed organization, with strong research, writing and communication skills. Knowledgeable in U.S. military concepts, programs and terminology. What We Offer: Some of our competitive benefits package includes: Medical, dental, and vision insurance Three weeks of vacation for newly hired employees Generous 401(k) plan that includes employer matching funds and separate employer retirement contribution, including a Lifetime Income Strategy option Tuition reimbursement program Student Loan Repayment Program Life insurance and disability coverage Optional coverages you can buy pet insurance, home and auto insurance, additional life and accident insurance, critical illness insurance, group legal, ID theft protection Birth, adoption, parental leave benefits Ovia Health, fertility, and family planning Adoption Assistance Autism Benefit Employee Assistance Plan, including up to 10 free counseling sessions Healthy You Incentives, wellness rewards program Doctor on Demand, virtual doctor visits Bright Horizons, child and elder care services Teladoc Medical Experts, second opinion program This position may be eligible for relocation. And more! Learn More & Apply Now! *Please ensure the role type (defined below) is appropriate for your needs before applying to this role. Onsite: Employees who are working in Onsite roles will work primarily onsite. This includes all production and maintenance employees, as they are essential to the development of our products. Location Arlington, VA As part of our commitment to maintaining a secure hiring process, candidates may be asked to attend select steps of the interview process in-person at one of our office locations, regardless of whether the role is designated as on-site, hybrid or remote. The salary range for this role is 145,600 USD - 276,800 USD. The salary range provided is a good faith estimate representative of all experience levels. RTX considers several factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to, the role, function and associated responsibilities, a candidate’s work experience, location, education/training, and key skills. Hired applicants may be eligible for benefits, including but not limited to, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, short-term disability, long-term disability, 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts, flexible work schedules, employee assistance program, Employee Scholar Program, parental leave, paid time off, and holidays. Specific benefits are dependent upon the specific business unit as well as whether or not the position is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Hired applicants may be eligible for annual short-term and/or long-term incentive compensation programs depending on the level of the position and whether or not it is covered by a collective-bargaining agreement. Payments under these annual programs are not guaranteed and are dependent upon a variety of factors including, but not limited to, individual performance, business unit performance, and/or the company’s performance. This role is a U.S.-based role. If the successful candidate resides in a U.S. territory, the appropriate pay structure and benefits will apply. RTX anticipates the application window closing approximately 40 days from the date the notice was posted. However, factors such as candidate flow and business necessity may require RTX to shorten or extend the application window. RTX is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability or veteran status, or any other applicable state or federal protected class. RTX provides affirmative action in employment for qualified Individuals with a Disability and Protected Veterans in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and the Vietnam Era Veterans’ Readjustment Assistance Act. item.title: Vp Government Affairs
item.description: Tinker Federal Credit Union’s Risk department has an immediate opening for a Vice President of Government Affairs! This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the nation’s leading credit unions! We offer competitive pay, a robust benefits package, a “smart casual dress code” and much more! We want you to work and grow at TFCU, so there will be many opportunities for professional development and growth through training and continued education. We value you at TFCU! As a Vice President of Government Affairs, you will be responsible for the following: Manages TFCU’s Government Affairs function and is accountable for developing, recommending, and executing the organization’s legislative, regulatory, and political engagement strategy. Evaluates emerging public policy developments, advises leadership regarding organizational risks and opportunities, and manages the relationships, programs, resources, and external partners necessary to advance TFCU’s approved advocacy priorities. Salary Range: This is an exempt position. The starting salary range is $161,544-$201,930; however, actual placement within the range will be determined individually based on your experience relative to organizational needs and internal salary equity. Schedule: Normally works a weekday schedule, but may be required to work evenings, holidays, or weekends. Required to travel, including overnight travel, with or without advance notice Education/Experience: You must have a bachelor's degree in government, business, public policy, political science, or a related field. At least six years of progressively responsible experience in government affairs, lobbying, legislative affairs, regulatory policy, or public policy management is required, including experience managing significant programs, external partners, or cross-functional initiatives. Experience advising senior leadership and representing an organization before elected officials, regulators, or industry associations is required Certificates, Licenses, Registrations: Incumbent Bonding REQUIRED by TFCU’s chosen authority. Valid driver’s license, maintaining an acceptable Motor Vehicle Record. Registered federal lobbyist, or ability to register under the Lobbying Disclosure Act within 90 days of hire, is required. Ability and willingness to register as an Oklahoma state lobbyist is also required. Keys to success: In order to be successful as a Vice President of Government Affairs you must possess these qualifications: Ability to translate complex legislative and regulatory developments into concise organizational impact assessments and actionable recommendations. Ability to manage budgets, contracts, consultants, vendors, and multiple concurrent advocacy initiatives. Ability to exercise judgment and represent TFCU’s approved positions within established executive direction and delegated authority. Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and lead cross-functional work without direct reporting authority. Advanced knowledge of lobbying, ethics, disclosure, campaign-finance, PAC, and related compliance requirements. Ability to develop executive and board-level briefings regarding legislative, regulatory, and political developments. Proven ability to develop and maintain strong working relationships with national and state leaders, internal and external stakeholders, and employees at all organizational levels. Ability and willingness to travel for work assignments, including out-of-state travel, which may occur as frequently as quarterly or more often depending on business needs, and to work varied hours as needed. Proficiency in financial services, business, and project management software.

item.title: Public Policy Incentives Analyst
item.description: At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe. Job Title: Public Policy & Incentives Analyst Location: Based in St. Petersburg, FL, with consideration for remote candidates located in the Washington, DC area. The Public Policy & Incentives Analyst supports Jabil’s global public policy, government affairs, and economic development incentives activities. The role is responsible for monitoring and analyzing legislative, regulatory, trade, geopolitical, and economic development issues that may impact Jabil’s businesses, operations, customers, and global manufacturing footprint, while also supporting the administration and compliance of Jabil’s global portfolio of economic development incentives. The Analyst will conduct policy research, prepare executive briefings and issue summaries, track government actions and regulatory developments, and support engagement with government agencies, industry associations, consultants, and other external stakeholders. The role will also maintain accurate records of incentive commitments, monitor reporting deadlines and performance milestones, prepare reimbursement and compliance submissions, and support internal and external audits. The Analyst will work across Finance, Tax, Human Resources, Operations, Legal, Government Affairs, business units, and site leadership. This position requires strong analytical and writing skills, attention to detail, sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage multiple priorities across jurisdictions and subject areas. What can you expect to do? Monitor and analyze legislative, regulatory, trade, geopolitical, economic, and industrial policy developments affecting Jabil, its customers, manufacturing operations, supply chains, market access, and investments. Research emerging policy and regulatory issues and translate complex developments into concise executive updates, briefing materials, presentations, and actionable business analysis. Track legislation, regulations, executive actions, tariffs, trade restrictions, procurement requirements, government programs, and other U.S. and international policy developments relevant to Jabil. Support Government Affairs engagement with government officials, industry associations, economic development organizations, and other stakeholders through research, talking points, briefing materials, stakeholder mapping, and follow-up. Maintain Jabil’s centralized economic development incentives portfolio, including compliance requirements, reporting deadlines, contractual milestones, job and wage commitments, capital investment, training obligations, and reimbursement schedules. Coordinate with Finance, HR, Payroll, Operations, Tax, Legal, and site teams to collect, validate, and reconcile data required for incentive reporting, certifications, reimbursement requests, audits, and government inquiries. Identify and escalate policy, regulatory, geopolitical, and incentive compliance risks, including upcoming deadlines, performance gaps, missing information, and changes that may affect Jabil’s obligations or business strategy. Support new incentive opportunities, site expansions, project changes, and investment decisions through research, due diligence, financial and operational analysis, and government program evaluation. Develop and maintain standardized trackers, reports, templates, procedures, and audit-ready records for Public Policy, Government Affairs, and Incentives activities. Organize complex policy, financial, employment, operational, and government information into clear, fact-based recommendations for management and business leaders. What is the experience needed to be successful in this role? Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Economics, International Relations, Business, Finance, Public Administration, or a related field. 2+ years of experience in public policy, government affairs, economic development, incentives administration, compliance, research, finance, consulting, or a related analytical role. Experience researching and analyzing legislative, regulatory, trade, economic, or geopolitical developments and translating findings into business-focused recommendations. Strong written communication skills with experience preparing executive briefings, reports, presentations, or policy summaries. Experience collecting, validating, analyzing, and reporting data across multiple stakeholders and functions. Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and priorities in a fast-paced environment. Familiarity with economic development incentives, tax credits, grants, government programs, trade policy, tariffs, regulatory compliance, or public sector engagement is preferred. Benefits Package with Jabil Along with growth, stability, and the opportunity to be challenged, Jabil offers a competitive benefits package that includes: Competitive Base Salary Annual Bonus Medical, Dental, Prescription Drug, and Vision Insurance with HRA and HSA options 401K Match Employee Stock Purchase Plan Paid Time Off Tuition Reimbursement Life, AD&D, and Disability Insurance Commuter Benefits Employee Assistance Program Pet Insurance Adoption Assistance Annual Merit Increases Community Volunteer Opportunities BE AWARE OF FRAUD: When applying for a job at Jabil you will be contacted via correspondence through our official job portal with a jabil.com e-mail address; direct phone call from a member of the Jabil team; or direct e-mail with a jabil.com e-mail address. Jabil does not request payments for interviews or at any other point during the hiring process. Jabil will not ask for your personal identifying information such as a social security number, birth certificate, financial institution, driver’s license number or passport information over the phone or via e-mail. If you believe you are a victim of identity theft, contact the Federal Bureau of Investigations internet crime hotline (www.ic3.gov), the Federal Trade Commission identity theft hotline (www.identitytheft.gov) and/or your local police department. Any scam job listings should be reported to whatever website it was posted in. Jabil, including its subsidiaries, is an equal opportunity employer and considers qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Accessibility Accommodation If you are a qualified individual with a disability, you have the right to request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access Jabil.com/Careers site as a result of your disability. You can request a reasonable accommodation by sending an e-mail to Always_Accessible@Jabil.com or calling 727-803-7988 with the nature of your request and contact information. Please do not direct any other general employment related questions to this e-mail or phone number. Please note that only those inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to. #whereyoubelong #AWorldofPossibilities #EarlyCareer

item.title: Legislative Affairs Manager
item.description: Job Description Legislative Affairs Manager NRECA is a unique national trade association providing advocacy, financial services and business support services to over 900 consumer owned electric cooperatives across the country. NRECA employees are united by our mission, inclusive culture, collaborative workplace and commitment to service excellence. As a “best place to work” employer, we operate with integrity, transparency and a spirit of innovation. As a member of our Government Relations department, you will be joining a team that advocates on behalf of NRECA members on federal legislative and regulatory matters and in national policy forums and develops and trains our grassroots to impact policies at the federal, state and local level. NRECA has the top policy brand reputation among trade associations in Washington, D.C. for the last 4 consecutive years. Summary of Position The person in this role oversees government relations activities across a portfolio of legislative issues relevant to NRECA members. They will develop a deep understanding of assigned issue areas as well as the advocacy toolkit. They will promote and influence federal policies, legislation, and actions favorable to rural electric cooperatives and related programs and issues on assigned portfolio of issues. This position requires 5 full days in office with flexibility offered at the discretion of management. Key Responsibilities Establishes and maintains relationships with Members of Congress and their staff. Presents electric cooperative positions and priorities to inform and persuade stakeholders. Uses knowledge of various advocacy strategies and tools, including grassroots, grass tops, and leveraging member involvement, to advance legislation and policy goals related to issue portfolio. Develops subject matter expertise of policy and legislative issues and works closely with professionals across the association to advance legislative priorities that benefit the NRECA membership. Uses understanding of issues to engage, influence and inform lawmakers and NRECA stakeholders. Reviews, analyzes and summarizes pending legislation which may impact electric cooperative members on assigned policy areas. Prepares and hones messages to assist lawmakers and staff to understand NRECA’s policy priorities. Presents lawmakers and Directors with timely and concise updates related to pending legislation. Works with Directors to draft legislation in accordance with policy resolutions of the Association. Conducts advocacy efforts in support of policy resolutions and assists in the formulation of policy resolutions that guide strategies on assigned legislative issues. Prepares and hones messages to assist Members of Congress and their staffs to understand the policy priorities of NRECA and the impact of policy on electric cooperative members. Develops a deep understanding of co-op landscape and issues to leverage issue-area knowledge and advocacy skillset on behalf of NRECA members. Creates and cultivates relationships with member cooperatives, including statewide managers, G&T managers and distribution managers, providing legislative updates and guidance while channeling their active participation in NRECA’s advocacy efforts. Ability to report to the office when required Qualifications Required Qualifications and Skills 3 or more years of experience with congressional offices, political campaigns, or federal and/or state agency or industry relating to the assigned area of responsibility Bachelor's Degree in Government, Communications or related field Preferred Qualifications and Skills Experience on Capitol Hill or at a trade association, experience advocating on issues within the assigned area of responsibility Essential Physical Requirements The worker is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading. undefined Exerting up to 20 pounds of force occasionally, and/or up to 10 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg controls requires exertion of forces greater than that for sedentary work and the worker sits most of the time, the job is rated for light work. Salary Range: $114,000 - $140,000 Annual Salary Final compensation determined by individual qualifications, experience, and internal equity.
