item.title: Associate Full Professor And Department Head Political Science
item.description: Job Title Associate/Full Professor and Department Head (Political Science) Agency Prairie View A&M University Department College of Public Affairs & Societal Impact Proposed Minimum Salary Commensurate Job Location Prairie View, Texas Job Type Faculty Job Description Important Immigration information: A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a $100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025. Please be advised that Texas A&M University will NOT pay this fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your employment, we recommend that you consult with your private immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your current immigration status would make a potential offer of employment from Texas A&M University subject to this fee. In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status this moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be selected as the final candidate. __________________________________________________________________________ _ Prairie View A&M University seeks an accomplished, collaborative scholar-leader to serve as Associate or Full Professor and Department Head of Political Science, beginning Fall 2027. As the leader of the newly established Department of Political Science, the Department Head will shape its strategic vision and academic identity while advancing excellence in teaching, research, faculty and staff development, student recruitment and success, civic engagement, and public impact. The role also includes developing academic and interdisciplinary programs, expanding research and external funding, cultivating government and community partnerships, supporting experiential learning and career preparation, engaging alumni and advancement efforts, and strengthening the department’s regional and national visibility. The successful candidate must be tenure-eligible upon arrival. The salary is determined in accordance with the University’s compensation structure and will be commensurate with the candidates’ education and experience, within the assigned salary range for this position. Responsibilities: Strategic and Academic Leadership Lead an all-encompassing process for developing and implementing a shared strategic vision for the department. Establish departmental goals, priorities, performance indicators, and assessment processes aligned with the strategic plans of the College and University. Provide leadership for curriculum development, academic program review, assessment, and continuous improvement. Identify opportunities for new degree programs, minors, certificates, concentrations, micro credentials, and interdisciplinary initiatives. Ensure the quality, relevance, and integrity of the department’s academic programs and course offerings. Promote innovation in teaching, learning, civic engagement, experiential education, and the appropriate use of emerging technologies. Faculty Leadership and Development Recruit, retain, support, and mentor a high-performing faculty. Foster excellence in teaching, research, scholarship, service, and community engagement. Support faculty efforts to publish scholarly work, develop research collaborations, secure external funding, and increase their professional visibility. Administer faculty evaluation, promotion, tenure, and post-tenure review processes in accordance with University policies. Develop strategies for faculty succession, leadership development, and long-term departmental capacity. Student Success and Enrollment Management Lead strategies to strengthen student recruitment, enrollment, retention, academic progression, graduation, and post-graduation outcomes. Use enrollment, course-demand, academic-performance, and student-success data to inform decision-making. Expand opportunities for internships, undergraduate research, experiential learning, civic engagement, study away, conference participation, and career preparation. Strengthen pathways for transfer students and relationships with community colleges and other educational partners, as appropriate. Research and External Funding Maintain an active and externally funded research program aligned with the department’s mission and disciplinary standards. Publish regularly in peer-reviewed journals and present research at professional conferences. Mentor graduate and undergraduate students in research, scholarship, and creative activity. Advance a departmental research agenda that builds upon faculty expertise and addresses significant public, political, governmental, legal, and societal issues. Support faculty scholarship and encourage interdisciplinary research across the College and University. Encourage and support faculty efforts to secure grants, contracts, fellowships, and other forms of sponsored funding. Promote opportunities for faculty-student research collaboration. Identify opportunities for research partnerships with public agencies, nonprofit organizations, foundations, educational institutions, and community partners. Administration and Resource Management Provide effective and responsible oversight of the department’s budget, personnel, course schedule, and other resources. Develop annual budget requests and allocate departmental resources transparently and strategically. Ensure that faculty and staff assignments support academic priorities, student needs, and efficient departmental operations. Oversee departmental records, reports, assessments, reviews, and required institutional submissions. Collaborate with the Dean and other college leaders on budgeting, hiring, planning, assessment, and strategic initiatives. Evaluate progress toward departmental goals and make data-informed adjustments as needed. Partnerships, Advancement and Visibility Build productive relationships with alumni, donors, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, professional associations, and community partners. Collaborate with college and university advancement professionals to identify fundraising priorities and cultivate philanthropic support. Develop partnerships that create internships, research opportunities, employment pathways, and professional experiences for students. Raise the visibility of the department’s academic programs, faculty expertise, student achievements, research, and community contributions. Promote the department to prospective students, families, alumni, partners, and supporters. Other Duties Performs other duties as assigned. Required Education and Experience: An earned Ph.D. in Political Science or a closely related field from an accredited institution. At least three years of progressively responsible academic administrative experience, such as service as a department head or chair, program coordinator, center director, associate chair, associate dean, or in a comparable academic leadership role. At least 2 years of administrative experience. A record of teaching, research, scholarship, and service that meets the University’s requirements for appointment with tenure at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor. Evidence of effective leadership skills. Preferred Qualifications: Four or more years of progressively responsible academic administrative or comparable leadership experience, including roles such as department head/chair, associate chair, or academic program director. Experience leading the development, transformation, or strategic planning of an academic department, program, or organizational unit. Experience managing academic budgets and using data to guide planning, assessment, resource allocation, and continuous improvement. Experience leading curriculum development, academic program review, and the creation of new academic programs or credentials. Demonstrated success in student recruitment, retention, enrollment management, and degree completion. A record of securing or supporting external grants, contracts, philanthropic gifts, or other funding. Experience fostering interdisciplinary research and collaboration. item.title: Director Government Affairs
item.description: $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly Position Summary CFR’s Government Affairs operation is focused on actively engaging members of Congress and their staff, executive branch officials, and Washington, DC-based diplomats to provide timely, relevant, and useful analysis to further inform policymaking. Through discussion and examination of the critical challenges facing the United States and the international community, the program seeks to serve as both a direct resource and convener of leading thinkers and practitioners in a nonpartisan forum. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC at least four days per week. Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays are considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. CFR’s remote working schedule is subject to change. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Help craft and set strategy for outreach to members of Congress and congressional staff in innovative and policy relevant ways. Maintain a professional network on Capitol Hill and leverage that network to advance institutional priorities. Moderate and oversee some program events, roundtables, and briefings for policymakers and their staff. Coordinate private consultations for members of Congress and their staff to ensure CFR expertise and products are incorporated into the policymaking process. Develop and implement unique and custom outreach strategies for CFR initiatives and other bespoke institutional priorities. Invite and oversee relationships with outside experts participating in CFR programming. Develop strong working relationships with CFR fellows to promote their expertise and scholarship. Track international affairs developments on Capitol Hill. Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required. Minimum Qualifications Education and Experience 8+ years of related experience, with event planning experience required. Bachelor’s degree in international relations, government, public policy, or other related field is required; master’s degree preferred. Congressional or government relations experience required. Related Skills & Other Requirements Strong judgement, discretion, and strategic instincts to operate in high-level, dynamic, and confidential environment. Established relationships across significant segment of House or Senate environment. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills including with senior principles. Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to multi-task and problem solve independently. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment both independently and on a team. Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $145,000 – $155,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers an outstanding benefits package. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $145,000 - $155,000 USD yearly

item.title: Spring 2027 Research And Events Internship Talbott Center Foreign Policy Job Id 2026 3912
item.description: Spring 2027, Research and Events Internship, Talbott Center, Foreign Policy (Job ID 2026-3912) The Brookings Institution Washington, District of Columbia, United States Internship 3 days ago $18.40 - $18.40 USD hourly Overview Thinking about a career in public policy? Committed to improving the world we live in? Think Brookings - one of the most influential, most quoted and most trusted think tanks! Interns spend approximately 12 weeks working alongside leading experts in government and academia from all over the world . Brookings also offers students the opportunity to intern in departments such as communications, human resources and central operations management. The mission of the Internship Program is to provide students with a pre-professional learning experience that offers meaningful, practical work experience related to their field of study or career interest. Students engage in career exploration and development as well as learn new skills. Interns will have the opportunity to attend meetings, think tank events, professional development workshops, and public Brookings events. In addition, interns will have the opportunity to network with other interns throughout the Institution. This internship is an opportunity for undergraduate students in their junior or senior year and graduate students with an interest in international affairs, foreign policy, history, political science, international law, international political economy, or related fields to apply principles and theory learned in the classroom in a professional environment. PhD students are not eligible for internships; please visit our Careers page for current open positions.This internship pays an hourly rate of $18.40, and applicants must be willing to commit to a minimum number of hours per week (no less than 24 hours per week, during regular business hours), with some flexibility around an academic course schedule. This internship requires regular in-person presence each week at our Washington, DC office with the option of at some work-from-home time. English fluency is required. To learn more about Brookings research programs, click here . Position Location : This internship requires you to be located in the U.S. for the duration of the internship. This is a hybrid opportunity. Hybrid positions combine regular in-person presence at our Washington, DC, office with the option of remote work. Work location cannot be in any of the following states: Alaska, California, Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Michigan, Oregon, Rhode Island, and Washington. Please only apply if you can live and work in states other than those listed above for the duration of the internship . Responsibilities This in-person internship will focus on a broad range of foreign policy and national security issues, including U.S. defense modernization and innovation, nonstate armed actors (militants/terrorists), nuclear issues, global governance, and security cooperation. Candidates should also be prepared to conduct research on additional security issues. This internship requires regular in-person presence each week at our Washington, DC office with the option of at some work-from-home time. Interns will learn how to apply theoretical knowledge learned in the classroom to a professional public policy institution and environment. They will monitor current developments in relevant research areas, conduct qualitative/quantitative research, produce written briefings and memos, brief support staff and senior fellows, summarize and synthesize documents, edit publications, help staff Brookings events, attend additional external think tank events, maintain databases, conduct additional administrative tasks related to web-postings, and logistical tasks related to events featuring guest speakers. Depending on an intern's foreign language abilities, they may also help translate documents. Interns should leave the internship with a better understanding of how to conduct high quality research and impartial analysis, additional subject matter knowledge on a broad range of national security and foreign policy issues, and experience interacting with top scholars in the field. Please be advised that Brookings is currently implementing a multi-year strategic plan that includes changes to our organizational structure. As this work continues, the program associated with this internship may change between the time of application and the internship start date. While the program may change, the work/research area described in this posting and the team associated with that work are expected to remain the same. Candidates will be informed of any relevant updates during the recruitment process and prior to the start of the internship. Qualifications Education/Knowledge/Skills: This internship is an opportunity for undergraduate students in their junior or senior year and graduate students pursuing a masters degree with an interest in international affairs, foreign policy, history, political science, international law, international political economy, or related fields to apply principles and theory learned in the classroom in a professional environment. Applicants should have a demonstrated interest in one or more of the following research areas: national security, U.S. foreign policy, U.S. defense policy, nuclear policy, maritime security, or nonstate armed actors (insurgencies, militant/extremist groups, terrorist organizations). Additional Information: This internship requires you to be located in the U.S. for the duration of the internship. Successful completion of a background investigation is required for interning at Brookings. Brookings requires that all applicants submit a cover letter and resume. Please submit your resume as instructed and add your cover letter as an attachment when you apply. You are required to submit/attach a separate cover letter for each internship application. Your cover letter should highlight your educational experience and skills, along with an explanation of how this internship will contribute to your professional goals. Please address your cover letter to Hiring Manager. If selected as a finalist for the internship, you will be required to submit two letters of recommendation or provide two professional references . Applications will be accepted until November 7, 2026. Applications not completed and submitted by the application deadline date will not be considered. Your application is considered complete when you receive an email confirming that your application was successfully submitted. As you are applying, please be sure to click here to learn more about the Brookings Internship Program, deadlines, and directions on how to successfully submit your internship application(s). Brookings welcomes and celebrates diversity in all its forms. We welcome applications that reflect a variety of backgrounds based on ideology, race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status, first generation college goers , and other factors protected by law . Brookings is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer that is committed to promoting a diverse and inclusive workplace. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $18.40 - $18.40 USD hourly

item.title: Research Associate U S Foreign Policy
item.description: $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly Overview Founded in 1921, the Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is a leading nonprofit membership organization, research center, and publisher, with headquarters in New York, an office in Washington, DC, and programs nationwide. It is dedicated to increasing America's understanding of the world and contributing ideas to U.S. foreign policy. CFR's 5,000+ members are leaders in international affairs and foreign policy. CFR also publishes Foreign Affairs , the preeminent magazine on global issues, and provides up-to-date information about the world and U.S. foreign policy on its award-winning website, CFR.org. Position Summary CFR’s David Rockefeller Studies Program is one of the country’s largest foreign policy think tanks with a widely respected and influential research staff. The Studies Program’s aim is to advance the discussion of U.S. foreign policy and international affairs through its writing, publications, public outreach, and discussions. As part of the Studies Program, the research associate will support a variety of fellows and programs, including a senior fellow whose work focuses on international relations, foreign policy, and diplomatic history. This role encompasses both administrative and research support, with the balance between the two fluctuating based on fellow and program needs. This position is based in CFR’s Washington, DC, office on a hybrid basis. CFR defines hybrid status as working at least four days a week onsite, with Tuesday through Thursday considered institutional anchor days where all staff are required to be onsite. Essential Functions/Responsibilities Provide logistical and administrative support to fellows, including scheduling and calendar management, handling phone calls, and media requests, making travel arrangements, and drafting correspondence Coordinate events, including preparing invitations, making travel arrangements, corresponding with speakers, presiders, and participants, and providing logistical support for the event Conduct research and editing for articles, book chapters, and other publications Assist with budgeting, including tracking monthly income statements, monitoring grant information, potentially drafting grant reports and proposals, creating and updating Excel spreadsheets, and preparing vouchers for reimbursement Assist fellows with social media outreach, including website maintenance and posting and/or using social media platforms, as needed Support other fellows and departments, upon request Perform any other duties or tasks as assigned or required Minimum Qualifications Experience and Education Bachelor’s degree in a related field such as political science, history, or international relations or other related fields. Demonstrated interest in foreign policy studies, diplomatic history, or related fields Master’s degree preferred, but not required One or more years of related administrative and/or internship experience preferred Related Skills & Other Requirements Excellent research, writing, editing, and communication skills Strong organizational and time management skills, with exceptional attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. Ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with others Ability to exercise sound judgment, maintain confidentiality, and manage sensitive information with discretion. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and other digital productivity tools, with strong online research and information-management skills Required Application Materials Please submit a résumé and cover letter stating your interest in the position. Compensation and Benefits The full-time annual compensation range for this position is $55,000 – $58,000, depending on experience. In addition to competitive salaries, the Council on Foreign Relations offers a benefits package that is among the best offered by nonprofit institutions today, including an award-winning health and wellness program, an on-site fitness center, and generous leave policies and health insurance programs. About CFR The Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) is committed to fostering a foreign policy community in the United States that is more representative of American society, recognizing that diverse backgrounds and perspectives contribute to broader, more informed participation in the foreign policy debate and lead to an enhanced understanding of the world and the United States’ role therein. To that end, CFR is dedicated to continuing to advance diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout its work and workplace by building a more diverse membership and staff, producing and dispensing thoughtful analysis on a broad range of foreign policy issues, and developing relevant, wide-reaching programming that also serves to expand the foreign policy talent pipeline to underrepresented populations. Washington, District of Columbia, United States $55,000 - $58,000 USD yearly

item.description: Elections Specialist Eaton County Charlotte, Michigan, United States Full-time 3 days ago $42,078 - $54,704 USD yearly General Summary Under the supervision of the Elections Administrator, receives, processes and corrects Qualified Voter files. Serves as Chief Assistant to the Elections Administrator on election activities for the County. Assists customers at the counter and by telephone by responding to inquiries related to election records and the election procedures of the Clerk's Office. Essential Functions Pre-Election Activities Reviews, monitors, verifies petition signatures, for both candidate and ballot petitions, and prepares receipt as proof of transaction for candidate filings, and other documents. Assists with the development and delivery of training to precinct inspectors and local election officials, regarding election operations and standards. This includes assisting the Election Administrator in reviewing updates to election laws, regulations that may require an update to County Clerk’s election procedures and training materials for maintaining compliance. Assists the Election Administrator with election activities such as forwarding voter registrations, ballot requests, absentee ballot applications, and absentee ballots to local clerks. Assists the Election Administrator by providing administrative assistance in preparation for 9 days of Early Voting. This includes providing logic and accuracy testing of the County Early Voting equipment, as required by law. Assists the Election Administrator with election activities by organizing materials to be mailed to candidates, proofreading ballots, maintaining and ordering election supplies, and performing related election activities. Week of Election Activities Assists the Election Administrator with day-to-day elections operations, including ordering supplies, using voting equipment, ballot programming and printing, prepares printing order, testing ballots and voting equipment, preparing forms, training materials, voter education, reimbursement claims, post-election audits, and handling of Election Administrator Committee meetings for in-county school and library districts. Assists with Election Night Reporting of election results, compilation of election returns, and the preparation of the election returns for certification. Assists the Election Administrator and participating municipalities by providing for the administration of a central polling place and conducting the 9 days of Early Voting on behalf of local units. Campaign Finance Assists the Election Administrator with campaign filing administration. Receives and reviews campaign finance and filing documents. Notifies candidates of errors, omissions, required corrections, and filing deadlines. Collects filing fees, fines, and additional charges. OTHER FUNCTIONS : Assists citizens, candidates, and other interested parties with questions and concerns regarding the election process and related department operations. This includes but is not limited to reviewing, responding, processing other such inquiries. This may include directing inquiries to the proper agency, local unit of government, group or individual. Responsible for retrieving election records from storage area, may entail locating and moving boxes of stored files, as well as moving certain permanent records into long-term storage as directed. Responsible for updating the elections web pages as needed. This list may not be inclusive of the total scope of job functions to be performed; duties and responsibilities may be added, deleted, or modified at any time Minimum Qualifications Must meet at least one of the following combinations of education and/or experience, and meet the other criteria: Associate’s degree with one year of experience in a clerical and data processing environment at a similar level, or a closely related field. One year of college in political science, event planning, business administration/management, or a closely related field. Two years of experience in a clerical and data processing environment at a similar level. High school degree or GED with four years of experience in a clerical and data processing environment at a similar level. Other Requirements Must be able to become commissioned by the State of Michigan as a Notary Public within 6 months of employment. Must be able to achieve accreditation through the Michigan Bureau of Elections Clerk within 12 months of employment. Valid State of Michigan Driver’s License. Working knowledge of MS Office Suite and must be an accurate typist with high proficiency. Preferred Education, Certification, or Experience Preferred college coursework in political science, event planning, business administration/management, or a closely related field. Preferred experience in a municipal setting working with elections. The qualifications listed above are intended to represent the minimum skills and experience levels associated with performing the duties and responsibilities contained in this job description. The qualifications should not be viewed as expressing absolute employment or promotional standards, but rather as general guidelines to be considered alongside other job-related selection or promotional criteria. Physical Requirements/Working Conditions Physical Requirements : [This job requires the ability to perform the essential functions contained in this description. Have the ability to operate a copy machine, fax machine, calculator, computer and other office equipment. Ability to access office files. Ability to retrieve and move books and indexes weighing up to 20 lbs. Ability to attend evening meetings. Have the ability to stoop, kneel, crouch and stretch to retrieve and store files and other documents in the office and basement storage vault. item.title: Legislative Director
item.description: Legislative Director Sierra Club Atlanta, Georgia, United States Full-time 3 days ago $86,000 - $86,000 USD yearly Job Title: Legislative Director Department: Georgia Chapter Location: Hybrid; must be able to travel to Atlanta daily Reports To: Chapter Director Supervises : Legislative Interns and Contract Lobbyists Context : At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 700 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees. Scope: The Legislative Director builds the Chapter’s power and influence through delivery of legislative advocacy efforts. Maintains governmental and political contacts, evaluates legislation, makes strategic recommendations related to legislation, and lobbies at the state and local level. This is a hybrid position that requires frequent in-person meetings as well as in-state travel. Job activities include but are not limited to: Legislative Strategy. Plans, coordinates, and implements the Chapter’s legislative strategies as approved by the Chapter Legislative Committee. Writes and implements work plans for legislative campaigns and coordinates with staff and volunteers to develop campaign goals and tactics that will deliver policy wins in alignment with the Chapter’s priorities. Collects and maintains legislative data, evaluates legislative strategies, reports campaign outcomes to the Chapter Director, and makes recommendations on adjusting organizing strategy as needed. Legislative Lobbying. Builds and maintains relationships with elected officials and legislative staff. Coordinates with groups and partners in order to rally support/opposition for bills, initiatives, laws, or resolutions. Monitors, studies, and researches proposed legislation to determine possible effects on the environment and makes appropriate recommendations to the Legislative Committee. Confers with legislators and officials to emphasize merits or weaknesses of specific bills to influence passage, defeat, or amendment of measure, or introduction of legislation that defend and advance environmental protection. In consultation with the Legislative Chair and contract lobbyist, prepares for legislative hearings and meetings. Ensures compliance with state and federal law and files lobbyist reports. Policy Messaging & Communications. Works with Sierra Club staff and coalition partners to develop a consistent, clear state policy and legislative message that is being communicated to the public, relevant communities, and stakeholders. Tracks legislative proceedings to ensure proper messaging and leads rapid response strategy. Write legislative briefs and works with communications staff to develop one-pagers, talking points, and policy toolkits. Grassroots Mobilization. Manages and implements legislative mobilization efforts including but not limited to: indirect lobbying, direct-to-target messaging, coalition events, SMS, and phonebanking. Designs and facilitates legislative training for volunteers and manages in-district lobbying volunteer programs. Plans and coordinates meetings between members and elected officials to discuss legislative issues and proposals and allow for officials to hear and consider member concerns. Convenes coalition spaces, meetings, and events in coordination with partners to plan mobilization opportunities, activations, and events Representation. Represents Sierra Club to elected officials, the public, in coalition meetings, legislative meetings, and events. Serves as Sierra Club spokesperson to media outlets and promotes volunteer and partner organization media exposure as needed. Collaboration with Committees. Writes legislative scorecard with Legislative Committee, works with Political Committee on endorsements, and serves as staff lead for Coordinated Campaign work. Is staff support on committees (Legislative, Clean Energy, Transportation, Wildlands, and Political) Manage Legislative Staff. Hires, manages and supports legislative staff, including: contract lobbyists and legislative interns. Manages hiring processes and executes contracts in alignment with the chapter's budget and priorities. Establishes performance objectives and expectations, and evaluates accomplishments and effectiveness. Tracks grant deliverables, progress and performance and, when necessary, helps course correct and respond to challenges. Advance Georgia Chapter’s Cultural Transformation Goals. Supports implementation of the Chapter's efforts to cultivate an environment that benefits from a broad coalition of identities reflecting the richness of cultures across Georgia. Seeks and creates opportunities to affirm the belonging of partners and members through political and legislative work. Miscellaneous. Travel is required for staff meetings, volunteer group meetings, statewide legislative functions, and other meetings and events deemed relevant to the duties of the job. Meetings and other work outside of regular business hours, including weekends and evenings is required. Heavier workloads may occur as a result of deadlines and during peak activity periods. The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies: Subject matter expertise. Substantial subject matter expertise in environmental policy, political science, or both. Prior experience and effectiveness in lobbying. Clear understanding and knowledge of the legislative and political process. Team Leadership. Prior experience and/or demonstrated ability in developing, training, and coaching teams of staff and volunteers in achieving shared goals. Experience in organizational conflict resolution and committed communication skills. Ability to address and resolve conflicts within the organization effectively, fostering a positive and collaborative work environment. Relevant experience. Must have experience working as a lobbyist. Must have experience with Georgia state-wide and/or local politics. Strong analytical skills. Ability and willingness to conduct strategic outreach. Successful candidates will show a strong desire to engage in collaboration, conduct outreach, and build networks throughout the organization and the state. Strong communication skills, both verbal and written. Successful candidates will demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively and clearly both verbally and in writing. Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate. Uplifting and additive . You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go. The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies: A deep knowledge and understanding of Georgia’s unique legislative and political landscape. Experience and a deep understanding of the rules, laws, and guidelines as they relate to political and lobbying work in Georgia, both advocacy and electoral. Can recognize where work needs to be done and fill the gaps. Self-motivated; can work independently as well as part of a team. Working knowledge of operations, budget management, and grant funding. Fast learner who can quickly absorb, distill, and communicate to diverse audiences new and often complex information $86,000 - $86,000 a year Compensation and Benefits The salary for this position is $86,000 annually. The Sierra Club offers a competitive salary package commensurate with skills and experience plus excellent benefits that include medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a retirement savings 401(k) plan. This is a category 4, exempt, non-represented, supervisory position. Sierra Club values the expertise and talents of foreign nationals. Sierra Club sponsors both nonimmigrant and immigrant visas when certain criteria are met, based on immigration laws and organizational needs. Such sponsorship is at the discretion of the Department Head and Sierra Club People Department in consultation with the employee’s manager. The Sierra Club cannot guarantee the approval of a visa petition. The Sierra Club is an equal opportunity employer committed to workforce belonging. item.title: Chief Legislative Affairs Division
item.description: Duties This position is located under the Office of Public and Governmental Affairs, Legislative Affairs Division in Washington, DC. The major duties of the Chief, Legislative Affairs Division position include, but are not limited to, the following: Ensure that congressional inquiries are responded to timely and accurately while always keeping their sights on the frequent sensitivities surrounding these and the associated requirements that may come from the Department Advise Bureau executives on a legislative strategy to accomplish Bureau goals and objectives and develops and promotes a legislative liaison program to accomplish those goals. Developing and implement nationwide legislative affairs strategies, activities, policies and programs and representing the Bureau in meetings and discussions with the member of Congress, their staff and top level offices from the Department of Justice and ATF. Stay aboard of newly proposed or enacted legislation affecting Bureau programs and servs as technical advisor to the AD and DAD, PGA and the Bureau Director and Deputy Director, providing authoriative analysis regarding new or revised legislatoin and intiatives having natioal or internatonal implications. Develop and maintain effective working relationships with other top Deparment and Bureau officials and keeps abreast of problems of a politcally sensiteve nature, areas of special or urgent Congressional interest, and any developments or problems relating to Bureau programs and budgetary needs Summary The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the Chief of the Legislative Affairs Division, Office of Public and Governmental Affairs (PGA) for the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives(ATF) and is responsible for developing, implementing, and directing the legislative affairs program, ensuring harmonious relationships with officials from the Department of Justice, Members of Congress, their staffs, and those committees that oversee the work and resources of the Bureau. Requirements Conditions of employment The requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement. Must be U.S. Citizen or National Selective Service registration is required for males born on, or after, December 31st 1959. Those not registered should have an approved exemption on file. May be required to serve a one-year probationary period. Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation. You must meet all applicable time-in-grade requirements by the closing of this announcement. Financial Disclosure: If selected, you may be required to disclose financial information in accordance with DOJ and Federal ethics guidelines. MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of ATF's mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process. This is a non-bargaining unit position. Qualifications To qualify for this position at the GS-15 grade level, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-14 by the closing date of this announcement. Specialized experience is demonstrated experience, which has equipped the applicant with the particular knowledge, skills and abilities to perform successfully the duties of this position. Experience must be in the normal line of progression or must be related to the work of the position advertised and must be reflected in resume. Specialized experience must include all of: Apply laws and regulations governing law enforcement, industry operations and other local, state and federal statutes; AND Develops and implements a federal legislative affairs strategies, activities, policies and programs; AND Prepares and provides official material to Congress regarding Bureau goals, objectives, and the effectiveness of programs; AND Establish parameters for assuring timely and quality completion of work assignments related to legislative affairs activities; AND Responds to congressional inquiries. item.description: Current University of Arkansas System employees, including student employees and graduate assistants, need to log in to Workday via MyApps.Microsoft.com, then access Find Jobs from the Workday search bar to view and apply for open positions. Students at all University of Arkansas institutions will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Jobs for Students.” University of Arkansas, Fayetteville students will view open positions and apply within Workday by searching for “Find Student Jobs at UAF.” All Job Postings will close at 12:01 a.m. CT on the specified Closing Date (if designated). If you close the browser or exit your application prior to submitting, the application process will be saved as a draft. You will be able to access and complete the application through “My Draft Applications” located on your Candidate Home page. Closing Date: Type of Position: Faculty - Tenure/Tenure Track No Job Type: Regular Yes Institution Name: University of Arkansas, Fayetteville Founded in 1871, the University of Arkansas is a land grant institution, classified by the Carnegie Foundation among the nation’s top 2 percent of universities with the highest level of research activity. The University of Arkansas works to advance the state and build a better world through education, research, and outreach by providing transformational opportunities and skills, fostering a welcoming climate, and nurturing creativity, discovery, and the spread of new ideas and innovations. The University of Arkansas campus is located in Fayetteville, a welcoming community ranked as one of the best places to live in the U.S. The growing region surrounding Fayetteville is home to numerous Fortune 500 companies and one of the nation’s strongest economies. Northwest Arkansas is also quickly gaining a national reputation for its focus on the arts and overall quality of life. As an employer, the University of Arkansas offers a vibrant work environment and a workplace culture that promotes a healthy work-life balance. The benefits package includes university contributions to health, dental, life and disability insurance, tuition waivers for employees and their families, 12 official holidays, immediate leave accrual, and a choice of retirement programs with university contributions ranging from 5 to 10% of employee salary. Below you will find the details for the position including any supplementary documentation and questions, you should review before applying for the opening. If you have a disability and need assistance with the hiring process, please submit a request via the Disability Accommodations | OEOC | University of Arkansas (uark.edu) : Request an Accommodation. Appli­cants are required to submit a request for each position of which they have applied. For general application assistance or if you have questions about a job posting, please contact Human Resources at 479.575.5351. Department: Department of Political Sciences Summary of Job Duties: The Department of Political Science in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in public administration, public policy, and nonprofit studies, beginning in August 2027. This is a standard nine-month faculty appointment. The successful candidate will serve as a core faculty member in the Master of Public Administration and Nonprofit Studies (MPA) program. The department’s standard teaching load is two courses per semester, for a total of four courses per academic year. The successful candidate will be expected to teach graduate courses that support the MPA program and introductory level undergraduate courses. This is an in-person position. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. About the Department: The Department of Political Science consists of 22 full-time faculty. For more information about our department, please visit https://fulbright.uark.edu/departments/political-science. Duties will include: • 40% Teaching or Professional Performance • 40% Research/Scholarly and/or Creative Activities • 20% Academic Service Activities Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: A Ph.D. in political science, public administration, public policy, nonprofit studies, or a closely related field conferred by the start date of employment from an accredited institution of higher education Potential to contribute to high-quality scholarship in public administration, public policy, nonprofit studies, or a closely related area Ability to teach at least one graduate course in public administration, public policy, or nonprofit studies that supports the MPA program Ability to teach introductory level undergraduate courses in the Department of Political Science Preferred Qualifications: Evidence of a coherent and productive research agenda, including peer-reviewed publications or a strong pipeline of scholarly work Evidence of effective college-level teaching Ability to teach two or more of the MPA course areas identified above Experience or demonstrated ability to mentor students Research and teaching interests that complement and broaden the strengths of the Department of Political Science and the MPA program Qualification Equivalencies: Additional Information: This position is a Designated Research Position and is regulated by the Arkansas Research Education Protection Act of 2025 . Prior to issuance of an offer of employment, the University is required to request and obtain additional information about an applicant’s background and, if required, conduct an additional review of that background information. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Required Documents to Apply: Cover Letter/Letter of Application, Curriculum Vitae, List of three Professional References (name, email, business title), Other (see special instructions for details) Proof of Veteran Status Recruitment Contact Information: Dr. Geoboo Song, gbsong@uark.edu All application materials must be uploaded to the University of Arkansas System Career Site https://uasys.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/UASYS Please do not send to listed recruitment contact. Special Instructions to Applicants: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Completed applications received by October 8, 2026, will be assured full consideration. Late applications will be reviewed as necessary to fill the position. For additional inquiries, please contact the search committee chair, Dr. Geoboo Song, at gbsong@uark.edu. Applicants must submit: 1) A curriculum vitae; 2) A cover letter explaining their interest in the position and how their research and teaching meet the advertised qualifications; 3) A research statement; a teaching statement that identifies the MPA courses and an appropriate 20000-level undergraduate course they would be prepared to teach and includes evidence of teaching effectiveness; 4) One representative writing sample; 5) A list of three professional references (name, title, institutional affiliation, email address, and phone number). Letters of recommendation will not be required as part of the initial application and will be requested only for candidates selected for interviews. Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Pre-employment Screening Requirements: Criminal Background Check, Sex Offender Registry The University of Arkansas is committed to providing a safe campus community. We conduct background checks for applicants being considered for employment. Background checks include a criminal background check and a sex offender registry check. For certain positions, there may also be a financial (credit) background check, a Motor Vehicle Registry (MVR) check, and/or drug screening. Required checks are identified in the position listing. A criminal conviction or arrest pending adjudication or adverse financial history information alone shall not disqualify an applicant in the absence of a relationship to the requirements of the position. Background check information will be used in a confidential, non-discriminatory manner consistent with state and federal law. The University of Arkansas seeks to attract, develop and retain high quality faculty, staff and administrators that consistently display practices and behaviors to advance a culture that embeds equal opportunity, educational excellence and unparalleled access for all. The University of Arkansas is an equal opportunity institution. The University does not discriminate in its education programs or activities (including in admission and employment) on the basis of any category or status protected by law, including age, race, color, national origin, disability, religion, protected veteran status, military service, genetic information, sex, sexual preference, or pregnancy. Questions or concerns about the application of Title IX, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex, may be sent to the University’s Title IX Coordinator and to the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights. Persons must have proof of legal authority to work in the United States on the first day of employment. All Application information is subject to public disclosure under the Arkansas Freedom of Information Act. Constant Physical Activity: N/A Frequent Physical Activity: N/A Occasional Physical Activity: N/A Benefits Eligible: Yes

item.title: Federal Government Affairs Manager Rise
item.description: Federal Government Affairs Manager (RISE) Croplife America Arlington, Virginia, United States Full-time 1 day ago Location: Arlington, Virginia Position Type: Full-Time Travel: Some travel is required for industry conferences and other stakeholder engagements. Reports To: Executive Director RISE (Responsible Industry for a Sound Environment), a trade association representing the specialty (non-agricultural) pesticide and fertilizer industry, is seeking a full-time Federal Government Affairs Manager based in Arlington, Virginia, near our nation’s capital. The successful candidate must register as a federal lobbyist. As a member of the public affairs team, this position will strengthen RISE’s federal advocacy presence on Capitol Hill and help ensure the association is a force multiplier for the industry. This role offers direct exposure to congressional policymaking and the opportunity to help shape advocacy outcomes for an industry with a broad national footprint. Responsibilities include supporting federal advocacy strategies that integrate grassroots engagement and communications to engage members, allies, congressional offices, policymakers, and other stakeholders. Responsibilities: Coordinate with the RISE team to develop and implement effective grassroots engagement strategies that mobilize members and allies on federal issues. With the Executive Director, help lead RISE’s congressional advocacy initiatives by cultivating relationships with national partner associations, key congressional offices, and committee staff, and positioning RISE as a subject matter expert on issues affecting its membership. Help lead educational meetings with congressional staff on behalf of the Pesticide Policy Coalition, focusing on foundational pesticide regulation education and the benefits of specialty pesticides and fertilizers. Support the development and execution of RISE’s federal appropriations strategy, including building congressional resource materials, identifying key House and Senate targets, and supporting a national campaign. Track congressional developments, hearings, markups, member priorities, committee activity, and relevant political dynamics to help inform RISE’s advocacy strategy. Assist in the development and delivery of public policy presentations and updates on behalf of RISE at industry conferences. Assist in composing and distributing informative and compelling correspondence, testimony, policy positions, grassroots alerts, congressional briefing materials, meeting notes, follow-up summaries, reports, toolkits, and background materials to support engagement on priority issues. Prepare for, participate in, and follow up on meetings with Members of Congress, congressional staff, committee staff, coalition partners, and member company representatives. Assist with planning and execution of RISE fly-ins, including member preparation, scheduling, materials development, congressional meeting logistics, and follow-up. Collaborate closely with RISE colleagues and members to advance federal advocacy, grassroots engagement, and communications initiatives. Participate in political fundraisers, industry events, coalition meetings, and other stakeholder engagements outside normal business hours, as needed. Other responsibilities as assigned. Education and Work Experience: Minimum of a BA/BS degree in political science, communications, public relations, environmental science, or a similar field. Minimum of 3 years of experience in public policy, legislative affairs, government affairs, or advocacy is required; at least 1 year of experience working in Congress, with a congressional committee, or in a congressional-facing advocacy role is preferred Additional Qualifications: Ability to self-start projects and independently manage assignments while meeting established timelines. Drive to become a subject matter expert on legislation and regulations broadly impacting the specialty pesticide and fertilizer industry. Ability to monitor federal legislative activity, identify emerging congressional trends, and summarize implications for members and internal stakeholders. Ability to proactively develop and maintain key relationships with congressional offices, committee staff, members, allies, RISE contract lobbyists, coalitions, grassroots stakeholders, teammates, and other stakeholders. Ability to build trust and work effectively with congressional offices, committee staff, coalition partners, and stakeholders across the political spectrum. Ability to exercise political acumen in assessing congressional dynamics, stakeholder interests, and opportunities for effective Hill engagement. Embodies flexibility, sound judgment, and discretion. Excellent written and oral communication skills, including strong writing, proofreading, editing, and the ability to distill complex or technical information into concise, effective, and influential materials. Experience tracking legislation and summarizing policy proposals. Familiarity with the U.S. pesticide regulatory system and current policy issues is preferred but not required. Proficiency in Microsoft Office and legislative tracking tools. Arlington, Virginia, United States

item.title: Usa Director Government Affairs And Public Policy
item.description: Position Summary... What you'll do... Role summary: The (USA) Director, Government Affairs and Public Policy leads strategic engagement to align and execute public policy initiatives with organizational objectives. This role shapes high-impact messaging, manages complex reputational risks, and fosters collaborative partnerships across markets and industries. By integrating policy insights with business strategy, the director advises leadership on emerging risks and opportunities, drives proactive external storytelling, and guides cross-functional teams through scenario planning and decision-making processes. The position requires expertise in advocacy, public policy and public affairs to influence outcomes and support long-term organizational goals. About the team: The State & Local Government Relations team represents Walmart before state and local governments, advancing public policy priorities and managing emerging issues. Collaborating across the business, the team monitors and shapes legislation and regulations impacting stores, associates, customers, and operations. They engage with governors, legislators, local officials, and stakeholders to develop state-specific strategies and clear advocacy. Team members anticipate risks and opportunities, exercise sound political judgment, and build strong relationships that support Walmart’s mission to serve customers and communities effectively. This position will be based in New York state, with a preference to be located in Albany. What you'll do: Develop and execute Walmart’s state government affairs strategy in New York and an additional state, advancing legislative, regulatory, and public policy priorities. Represent Walmart before governors’ offices, legislatures, attorneys general, regulatory and economic development agencies, and local officials. Build trusted relationships with policymakers, regulators, trade associations, and key stakeholders. Monitor and engage on legislation, regulations, and emerging political issues affecting Walmart’s business. Lead advocacy strategies, coalition efforts, and direct policymaker engagement. Anticipate political and policy risks and provide strategic counsel to leadership. Translate complex business issues into compelling policy arguments, briefings, testimony, and executive recommendations What you'll bring: At least 10 years experience in policy analysis, public policy advocacy, and regulatory compliance within complex environments. Proven ability to lead strategic communication and public affairs initiatives across multiple stakeholder groups. Strong skills in stakeholder engagement, coalition building, and influencing decision-making at senior levels. Expertise in developing and executing comprehensive communication and crisis response plans. Demonstrated capability to manage projects, including budgeting, scheduling, and risk mitigation. Proficiency in coaching teams on negotiation, storytelling, and conflict resolution in public policy contexts. Ability to integrate strategic foresight and business insights to shape policy and reputational outcomes. At Walmart, we offer competitive pay as well as performance-based bonus awards and other great benefits for a happier mind, body, and wallet. Health benefits include medical, vision and dental coverage. Financial benefits include 401(k), stock purchase and company-paid life insurance. Paid time off benefits include PTO (including sick leave), parental leave, family care leave, bereavement, jury duty, and voting. Other benefits include short-term and long-term disability, company discounts, Military Leave Pay, adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, and more. You will also receive PTO and/or PPTO that can be used for vacation, sick leave, holidays, or other purposes. The amount you receive depends on your job classification and length of employment. It will meet or exceed the requirements of paid sick leave laws, where applicable. For information about PTO, see https://one.walmart.com/notices . Live Better U is a Walmart-paid education benefit program for full-time and part-time associates in Walmart and Sam's Club facilities. Programs range from high school completion to bachelor's degrees, including English Language Learning and short-form certificates. Tuition, books, and fees are completely paid for by Walmart. Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to a specific plan or program terms. For information about benefits and eligibility, see One.Walmart . The annual salary range for this position is $110,000.00 - $220,000.00 Additional compensation includes annual or quarterly performance bonuses. Additional compensation for certain positions may also include : - Stock ㅤ ㅤ ㅤ ㅤ ‎ Minimum Qualifications... Outlined below are the required minimum qualifications for this position. If none are listed, there are no minimum qualifications. Bachelor’s degree in Political Science, Public Policy, Economics, Communications, or related area and 8 years’ experience in government relations, public policy research, legislative affairs, regulatory analysis, or related area OR 10 years’ experience in government relations, public policy research, legislative affairs, regulatory analysis, or related area Preferred Qualifications... Outlined below are the optional preferred qualifications for this position. If none are listed, there are no preferred qualifications. Advanced graduate degree; experience leading large-scale/national or multi‑market government affairs initiatives within the region or area of expertise., People management experience. Primary Location... 141 WASHINGTON AVE EXTENSION, WALMART ALBANY, NY 12205-0000, United States of America Walmart and its subsidiaries are committed to maintaining a drug-free workplace and has a no tolerance policy regarding the use of illegal drugs and alcohol on the job. This policy applies to all employees and aims to create a safe and productive work environment.

item.title: U S Public Policy Advocacy Intern
item.description: Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today! The U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy Summer Intern will support the U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy team through policy research, advocacy project support, project coordination, knowledge management, and development of reusable team materials. This internship is designed as a structured, development-focused 10-week experience that provides exposure to healthcare policy, federal and state government affairs, legislative and regulatory processes, advocacy strategy, corporate stakeholder engagement, and the pharmaceutical supply chain. This role will support meaningful, project-based work aligned to real team priorities while building the intern's skills in research, writing, synthesis, professional communication, organization, data validation, project tracking, and cross-functional collaboration. The role is intended to support Cencora's early talent pipeline and align with future workforce planning and talent development opportunities. The intern will contribute to discrete, supervised projects involving advocacy resources, state-level footprint materials, shared resource organization, policy research, meeting preparation, and team infrastructure initiatives. Projects will be designed to encourage critical thinking, problem solving, collaboration, and development of tangible deliverables that support business objectives. The intern will maintain a project and accomplishment log throughout the internship and prepare a final presentation summarizing completed work, key deliverables, skills developed, and overall business impact. Job Requirements The Summer Intern, U.S. Public Policy & Advocacy will be responsible for: Conducting research on federal and state policy issues, healthcare legislation, regulatory developments, congressional activity, trade association activity, and industry trends relevant to Cencora's policy and advocacy priorities. Drafting concise internal summaries, background documents, one-pagers, biographies, briefing materials, meeting preparation documents, and presentation content for internal stakeholders under manager guidance. Supporting state-level advocacy resource development by validating data, organizing information, identifying gaps or inconsistencies, and coordinating with internal stakeholders as needed. Assisting with maintenance of team trackers, shared resources, project logs, templates, repositories, meeting materials, and process documentation. Supporting organization and maintenance of shared team folders, onboarding materials, project resources, knowledge repositories, and other business-critical documentation. Attending selected congressional hearings, industry briefings, internal meetings, team calls, and advocacy-related events, and preparing concise summaries of key takeaways. Supporting planning and coordination for meetings, office visits, fly-ins, briefings, advocacy activities, and special projects as assigned. Collaborating with colleagues across Public Policy, Federal Advocacy, State Advocacy, PAC, Corporate Responsibility, Marketing, and other business functions on assigned initiatives. Maintaining a task and project log that documents assignments, deliverables, accomplishments, and skills developed throughout the internship. Completing a final presentation summarizing project outcomes, business impact, professional development experiences, and recommendations for future work. Required Knowledge Basic understanding of U.S. government, public policy, political processes, legislative affairs, healthcare policy, business, communications, or related subject matter. Interest in healthcare, government affairs, advocacy, public policy, legislative affairs, stakeholder engagement, or the pharmaceutical supply chain. Ability to conduct research, analyze information, and synthesize findings into clear, concise written materials. Understanding of professional written and verbal communication, including proofreading, accuracy, and audience awareness. Strong attention to detail and commitment to producing high-quality work products. Understanding of confidentiality, professionalism, discretion, and appropriate handling of sensitive information. Familiarity with Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, and SharePoint. Ability to organize information in a clear and accessible manner. Ability to work independently on assigned projects while collaborating effectively with team members. Ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and communicate proactively regarding workload and project status. Required Experience / Relevant Coursework Candidates should be currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to: Political Science Public Policy Government Public Administration Health Policy Healthcare Administration Communications Journalism Business Administration Economics International Affairs Law or Pre-Law Data Analytics Public Affairs Related liberal arts, policy, business, or healthcare fields Preferred Coursework or Experience Coursework in U.S. government, legislative process, public policy, healthcare policy, political science, economics, communications, business, research methods, public administration, law, or data analysis. Experience conducting research, writing summaries, preparing presentations, organizing data, drafting reports, or supporting team projects. Experience using Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, or SharePoint through academic, volunteer, internship, work, or student organization activities. Experience in policy, advocacy, government, communications, nonprofit, healthcare, business, legal, administrative, or research-related settings preferred but not required. Experience collaborating in team environments, managing deadlines, organizing information, and communicating updates effectively. Demonstrated interest in healthcare policy, government affairs, public affairs, advocacy, legislative processes, political systems, community impact, or the healthcare supply chain. What Cencora offers We provide compensation, benefits, and resources that enable a highly inclusive culture and support our team members’ ability to live with purpose every day. In addition to traditional offerings like medical, dental, and vision care, we also provide a comprehensive suite of benefits that focus on the physical, emotional, financial, and social aspects of wellness. This encompasses support for working families, which may include backup dependent care, adoption assistance, infertility coverage, family building support, behavioral health solutions, paid parental leave, and paid caregiver leave. To encourage your personal growth, we also offer a variety of training programs, professional development resources, and opportunities to participate in mentorship programs, employee resource groups, volunteer activities, and much more. For details, visit https://www.virtualfairhub.com/cencora Full time $37,752 - 56,650 *This Salary Range reflects a National Average for this job. The actual range may vary based on your locale. Ranges in Colorado/California/Washington/New York/Hawaii/Vermont/Minnesota/Massachusetts/Illinois State-specific locations may be up to 10% lower than the minimum salary range, and 12% higher than the maximum salary range. The company’s continued success depends on the full and effective utilization of qualified individuals.
