Below you will find the details for the position including any supplementary documentation and questions, you should review before applying for the opening. If you have a disability and need assistance with the hiring process, please submit a request via the Disability Accommodations | OEOC | University of Arkansas (uark.edu) : Request an Accommodation. Appli­cants are required to submit a request for each position of which they have applied. For general application assistance or if you have questions about a job posting, please contact Human Resources at 479.575.5351. Department: Department of Political Sciences https://politicalscience.uark.edu Summary of Job Duties: The Department of Political Science in the Fulbright College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Arkansas invites applications for a tenure-track assistant professor position in Political Science to start in August 2027. We are particularly interested in candidates whose research and teaching interests lie in the field of public law, with preferred specializations in jurisprudence, immigration law, family law, environmental law, or political theory. The expected teaching load for the position will be two courses per semester. Duties will include teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, performing research in their area of expertise, and contributing to the service needs of the department. Faculty hired in this position will have an opportunity to be a part of Fulbright College’s multidisciplinary Democracy as a Public Good cluster hire at the University of Arkansas. Through its Democracy as a Public Good Initiative, the College will advance the University’s land-grant mission by expanding capacity to generate knowledge that informs public understanding, contributes to policy and practice, and connects Arkansas to national and international conversations about societal good. Building on existing campus expertise in issues ranging from norms of democratic communication, free speech, media ethics and literacy, humanitarian governance and civil society, risks that AI poses to democratic governance, immigration, and public law, new faculty members participating in the cluster will advance their research agendas through mentoring and opportunities for collaboration—both with other scholars and with communities in the state—that may result in peer-reviewed publications, external funding, and new approaches to the pressing challenges that democracy faces. The successful candidate for this position will have an opportunity to join a community of scholars committed to confronting major issues, generating new knowledge, and providing research-based solutions that investigate and strengthen democratic culture for people living in Arkansas and beyond. This is an in-person position. Most university classes are offered face-to-face, and extensive in-person engagement in such activities as office hours, student advising, and departmental, college, and university committee meetings is essential to advancing student success and departmental effectiveness. Regular, reliable, and non-disruptive attendance is an essential job duty, as is the ability to create and maintain collegial, harmonious working relationships with others. About the Department: The Department of Political Science currently consists of 22 full-time faculty and is committed to strengthening its faculty, student body, and curriculum. For more information about our department, please visit https://fulbright.uark.edu/departments/political-science. Duties will include: • 40% Teaching or Professional Performance • 40% Research/Scholarly and/or Creative Activities • 20% Academic Service Activities Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: A Ph.D. degree in Political Science or a closely related field from an accredited institution of higher education conferred by August 2027 from an accredited institution of higher education A record of publication or submission of research in reputable scholarly outlets Demonstrated evidence of effective teaching in teaching evaluations, sample syllabi, or a teaching portfolio Demonstrated ability to teach an undergraduate Introduction to American Government course Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate coursework in at least two areas of public law A well-defined and coherent research agenda Preferred Qualifications: A strong and active research agenda that is well-grounded in political or legal theory, backed by advanced analytical, methodological, and empirical skills and focuses on some aspects of public law Demonstrated potential for publishing in top-tier outlets Demonstrated commitment to undergraduate and graduate education and a willingness to contribute to the department’s existing strengths in teaching and research Demonstrated ability to teach undergraduate coursework in political theory Demonstrated potential to secure external grant funding Demonstrated potential for national and international scholarly reputation Qualification Equivalencies: Additional Information: This position is a Designated Research Position and is regulated by the Arkansas Research Education Protection Act of 2025 . Prior to issuance of an offer of employment, the University is required to request and obtain additional information about an applicant’s background and, if required, conduct an additional review of that background information. Salary is commensurate with experience and qualifications. Required Documents to Apply: Cover Letter/Letter of Application, Curriculum Vitae, List of three Professional References (name, email, business title), Other (see special instructions for details) Proof of Veteran Status Recruitment Contact Information: Dr. Andrew Dowdle, professor, adowdle@uark.edu All application materials must be uploaded to the University of Arkansas System Career Site https://uasys.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/UASYS Please do not send to listed recruitment contact. Special Instructions to Applicants: Completed applications received by October 12, 2026, will be assured full consideration. Late applications will be reviewed as necessary to fill the position. For additional inquiries, please contact the search committee chair, Andrew Dowdle, at adowdle@uark.edu. To complete the application, candidates will need to submit: (1) a cover letter indicating interest and qualifications; (2) a current curriculum vita; (3) a research statement; (4) a teaching statement describing approach to instruction, assessment of learning, and means of including students from different backgrounds and with different learning abilities; (5) evidence of teaching effectiveness, including teaching evaluations (when available) demonstrating excellence in instruction; (6) unofficial graduate transcripts; (7) one single-authored writing sample; and (8) names of three academic references (only finalists will be asked to submit letters of recommendation). Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. Pre-employment Screening Requirements: Criminal Background Check, Sex Offender Registry The University of Arkansas is committed to providing a safe campus community. We conduct background checks for applicants being considered for employment. Background checks include a criminal background check and a sex offender registry check. For certain positions, there may also be a financial (credit) background check, a Motor Vehicle Registry (MVR) check, and/or drug screening. Required checks are identified in the position listing. item.title: Public Policy Researcher Entry Level Reston Va
item.description: Are you looking to work on current and emerging policy issues? Do you want to apply your education and experience to help government agencies improve the way they develop and implement regulations, policies, and programs? Our Regulatory, Policy, and Economics Portfolio has over 30 years of experience supporting the design, implementation, and improvement of federal programs for key clients including the Environmental Protection Agency, Department of Transportation, Department of Homeland Security, Department of Labor, Department of Interior, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Join our multidisciplinary team of regulatory specialists, policy analysts, economists, and attorneys. We combine legal, policy, economic, and scientific research and analysis to solve unique public policy challenges through innovative, accurate, timely, and high-quality products and services. Our dynamic work environment involves working on multiple projects simultaneously, supporting a variety of federal clients, and providing a wide range of support services. This entry-level full-time position will be hybrid from our Reston, VA headquarters. Job Responsibilities: Participating in short- and long-term engagements to support federal clients whose responsibilities are to develop policies and craft regulations that implement the desired policy, explain the rationale of the rulemaking to interested parties; and implement the regulatory requirements Supporting federal agency efforts to transparently manage and analyze public comments received on proposed agency rules Assist in drafting and editing documents related to federal agency rulemakings Immersing oneself rapidly in varied projects for multiple clients Providing verbal and written progress updates to project staff Synthesizing information from rulemaking documents, literature, and other technical reports Assist in developing recommendations through collecting and analyzing both qualitative and quantitative data Drafting reports and presentations Interacting with clients to discuss ICF’s analysis Basic Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in public policy, government, environmental science, natural or physical science, political science, or related subjects U.S. Citizenship is required per federal contract requirements Ability to obtain and maintain a government security clearance Preferred Qualifications: Understanding of the federal rulemaking process Ability to obtain and maintain a moderate-level government security clearance Strong analytical and organizational skills are essential Ability to prioritize and work on multiple projects under strict deadlines in a fast-paced environment Excellent written and oral communications skills Detail-oriented and team-oriented approach Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint) and Adobe; and Time management strategies Bot and Third-Party Applications Please note that this application must be submitted directly by the applicant for consideration. Failure to do so may result in the application being excluded for consideration . Applicants needing an accommodation for disability or religious purposes in connection with the application process should contact Candidateaccommodation@icf.com for assistance. Working at ICF ICF is a global advisory and technology services provider, but we’re not your typical consultants. We combine unmatched expertise with cutting-edge technology to help clients solve their most complex challenges, navigate change, and shape the future. We can only solve the world's toughest challenges by building a workplace that allows everyone to thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer . Together, our employees are empowered to share their expertise and collaborate with others to achieve personal and professional goals. For more information, please read our EEO policy. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. Reasonable Accommodations are available, including, but not limited to, for disabled veterans, individuals with disabilities, and individuals with sincerely held religious beliefs, in all phases of the application and employment process. To request an accommodation, please email Candidateaccommodation@icf.com and we will be happy to assist . All information you provide will be kept confidential and will be used only to the extent to provide needed reasonable accommodations. Candidate AI Usage Policy At ICF, we are committed to ensuring a fair interview process for all candidates based on their own skills and knowledge. As part of this commitment, the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to generate or assist with responses during interviews (whether in-person or virtual) is not permitted . item.title: Head Of Spectrum Management Government Affairs
item.description: Our client is developing a fully commercial next-generation GPS/PNT system to provide significant performance, security and reliability improvements for its users. The system will provide users with better accuracy, faster Time to First Fix (TTFF), solid anti-jam and anti-spoof capabilities, and will support US Government position and timing service resiliency along with next-generation commercial applications like drone delivery, self-driving cars, urban air mobility, and augmented reality. The $260B annual GNSS Hardware, Software and Data Services market is ripe for disruption and improvement, and the company intends to lead that revolution with its commercial infrastructure and services. The Position Our client is currently seeking a Full-Time Head of Spectrum Management & Government Affairs at its Herndon, Virginia location to secure and protect the spectrum its constellation depends on, lead its engagement with U.S. Government stakeholders, and advance the company’s role in ensuring resilient Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) for critical infrastructure and national security. Spectrum is the company’s wireless real estate, and this role owns it. You will own, build out and execute the roadmap that secures its radionavigation-satellite service (RNSS) and supporting allocations across domestic and international regulators, coordinate with incumbent GNSS and other operators to avoid harmful interference, and defend its rights over the life of the constellation. The work is both technical and political: you will be as comfortable in an interference analysis or an ITU coordination meeting as in a conversation with an agency lead or a Congressional office. Alongside spectrum, this senior role will drive the company’s broader regulatory and policy strategy, guide export control compliance, and build coalitions across federal agencies, Congress, industry, and international forums. As a pivotal leader in a fast-growing venture, you will directly shape how its commercial PNT system integrates with national security priorities and commercial markets. The position is hybrid, based in Herndon with regular access to Washington, DC, and includes occasional domestic and international travel as required. We’ll Expect You To… Lead Spectrum Management (75%) Own the company’s spectrum strategy and multi-year roadmap, securing, protecting, and expanding its RNSS, TT&C, feeder link, and inter-satellite link spectrum across domestic and international bodies. Lead ITU satellite network filings and coordination under the Radio Regulations, including advance publication, coordination requests, notification, bringing into use, and NGSO milestone obligations, working through the responsible notifying administrations. Negotiate and document coordination agreements with incumbent GNSS system operators, other satellite networks, and terrestrial users, and resolve interference concerns before they become disputes. Lead or direct interference and compatibility analyses (PFD, EPFD, aggregate interference, and protection criteria) that support filings, coordination positions, and regulatory submissions. Manage FCC satellite licensing and U.S. market access (Part 25 applications, modifications, and related filings) and coordinate with NTIA and the IRAC on federal band sharing. Secure earth station licensing and landing rights for the company’s ground network and service markets, country by country. Represent the company in World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC) preparation, ITU-R study groups and working parties, and U.S. preparatory processes, shaping agenda items that affect RNSS and PNT. Partner with Space Systems and Signals engineering so payload, emission, and system design decisions stay consistent with filed and coordinated parameters. Monitor for harmful interference, and manage outside spectrum counsel, consultants, and filing budgets. Lead Government Affairs & Policy (25%) Serve as the company’s primary liaison to the civil PNT policy community, including the National Coordination Office (NCO) for PNT, DOT, DHS/CISA, NIST, NASA, and the policy offices of the FCC and NTIA, to position commercial LEO PNT as a recognized complement to GPS. Participate in interagency working groups, federal advisory bodies, and public-private forums shaping civil PNT resilience and complementary PNT policy, and provide technical input to National PNT Strategy updates, Federal Radionavigation Plan revisions, and related civil policy processes. Represent the company in a focused set of standards bodies, trade associations, and industry coalitions where participation directly supports its spectrum and regulatory objectives. Track federal policy and regulatory developments affecting civil PNT, critical infrastructure timing, and commercial space, and translate them into concise internal guidance for the executive team and engineering. Oversee regulatory compliance for space operations and exports, including launch licensing, UN space object registration, and ITAR/EAR compliance (TAAs, DSP-5s, and company-wide export training), in coordination with outside counsel.

item.title: Manager Associate Director Director Public Policy
item.description: The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is seeking a new team member to join its Public Policy team who is passionate about American agriculture and the policies that affect the agricultural industry. This position serves as NASDA's lead federal policy advocate for food systems and nutrition. The role converts member priorities into coordinated legislative, regulatory, and funding strategies; leads the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee; and builds the relationships needed to elevate the voice of state departments of agriculture food systems and nutrition policy. Depending on qualifications, experience, and capacity demonstrated, the portfolio may expand to include leadership of the Marketing and International Trade Committee and associated policy issues, providing a defined opportunity to take on broader responsibility over time. This position will have the opportunity to travel across the U.S. for meetings and conferences with the possibility of international travel. The candidate will be able to build relationships and collaborate with leaders from state departments of agriculture from all 50 states and four U.S. territories, congressional and government entities, and agricultural partnerships and coalitions. Members of the Public Policy team earn a competitive salary and enjoy an excellent work culture at an organization with exceptional perks, including a flexible schedule and an incredible mission. ABOUT NASDA The National Association of State Departments of Agriculture is a nonpartisan, nonprofit association representing the 50 elected and appointed commissioners, secretaries, and directors of the state departments of agriculture, and four U.S. territories. NASDA grows and enhances American agriculture through policy, partnerships, and public engagement. We recognize that to achieve our goals, we need employees as passionate about agriculture as we are. We strive to create a positive work environment that our employees can be proud of and where they can build their careers. ABOUT THE POSITION The essential functions include, but are not limited to, the following: Lead the development, implementation, and communication of NASDA's federal policy portfolio for food systems and nutrition, with primary emphasis on funding and implementation of state led farm-to-table programs; additional priorities may include food safety (e.g., FSMA and food safety inspection), in close coordination with and support of NASDA's Food Safety team, as well as food labeling, nutrition, food waste, food access and security, and food supply chain issues. Serve as staff lead for the Food Systems and Nutrition Committee, coordinating priorities with the committee's Chair and Vice-Chair, preparing meeting agendas, policy materials, recommendations, and follow-up actions. Translate member priorities into legislative, regulatory, and appropriations strategies and advocate those positions before Congress and federal agencies. Monitor and analyze federal legislation, regulations, funding opportunities, and emerging issues; provide timely, concise, decision-ready guidance to NASDA members and leadership. Build trusted relationships with commissioners, secretaries, directors, and staff of state departments of agriculture and facilitate consensus across diverse state interests. Develop and sustain partnerships and coalitions with agricultural, food systems and nutrition stakeholders to advance NASDA priorities and elevate the roles of state departments of agriculture in those spaces. Draft high-quality policy briefs, testimony, comment letters, talking points, presentations, and member communications. Manage projects, timelines, deliverables, and reporting with sound and strategic judgment. Demonstrate readiness for increasing responsibility by building subject matter knowledge, independently managing assigned issues, and developing the judgment and stakeholder relationships needed to assume additional committee and policy leadership. Collaborate across NASDA's policy, communications, trade, partnerships, and other key teams and represent NASDA at meetings and events, including travel as required. QUALIFICATIONS Candidates may be considered at the Manager, Associate Director, or Director level based on the depth, scope, and relevance of their experience. Manager, Public Policy: At least two years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to support policy analysis and advocacy, manage defined issues and projects, cultivate stakeholder relationships, and produce clear, accurate written materials with appropriate guidance. The Manager is expected to grow toward greater independence and may assume additional policy or committee leadership based on demonstrated readiness, performance, and organizational needs. Associate Director, Public Policy: At least four years of relevant experience, with demonstrated ability to manage policy issues, relationships, and projects with increasing independence. Director, Public Policy: At least six years of relevant experience, including demonstrated ownership of complex policy strategy, senior level external representation, and independent committee or portfolio leadership. PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE Congressional and federal policy expertise: Relevant federal agricultural policy experience with Congress or federal agencies (primarily USDA and FDA), including legislative, appropriations, or regulatory policy, as well as an understanding of the roles of Congress, federal agencies, and state departments of agriculture. Relevant government affairs work in these areas is also acceptable. Policy analysis and strategic judgment: Ability to track and analyze legislation, regulations, program guidance, funding proposals, and emerging issues; identify implications for states; and recommend and execute practical courses of action. Advocacy and communication: Demonstrated ability to translate complex issues into concise, audience-appropriate briefs, testimony, letters, talking points, presentations, and oral advocacy. Relationship building and diplomacy: Ability to establish credibility with NASDA members, congressional and government officials, partners, and coalitions; navigate differing state perspectives; and build consensus without relying on formal authority. Project management: Experience managing multiple priorities, deadlines, deliverables, or related responsibilities with accuracy, accountability, and follow-through. Collaboration, adaptability, and integrity: Ability to work effectively across teams, respond productively to changing priorities, learn new issues quickly, and represent NASDA with sound judgment, discretion, and nonpartisanship. Education: A bachelor's degree is required. Desired area of study in agricultural policy, food policy, political science, public policy, economics, law, or related agriculture, food, or nutrition field. An advanced degree may substitute for a portion of relevant experience where appropriate. WORK SCHEDULE This is a full-time (40hrs/week), exempt position at the NASDA headquarters at 4350 N Fairfax Drive, Arlington, VA. We offer a hybrid work schedule, with three days in the office and two days working from home. Working hours are generally Monday - Friday, 9 am - 5 pm local time. Benefits: PTO for vacation, sick leave, and volunteer hours Tuition reimbursement Professional development 401k - 100% match up to 4% SALARY The hiring range is $65,000 - $100,000 annually based on experience. We understand your time is valuable, so we have a rapid and easy application process. Please complete our initial 3-minute, mobile-friendly application and attach your cover letter and resume to your application . Applications without a cover letter and resume will not be considered. We look forward to meeting you! - If you have issues attaching your cover letter to the application, please email it to careers@nasda.org. NASDA does not discriminate in employment practices or programs on the basis of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, disability, age, marital status, family/parental status, income derived from a public assistance program, political beliefs, or reprisal or retaliation for prior civil rights activity. You will have to pass a background check

item.title: Senate Reporter
item.description: Bloomberg Government is seeking an ambitious reporter to lead our Senate coverage. The reporter will work with the rest of our Congress Team to break news out the Senate, quickly and authoritatively cover action on the Senate floor and from behind-closed-door caucus meetings and write enterprise and analysis that connect the dots for our readers about the power players and politics shaping the chamber. The position includes working on our flagship newsletter Congress Tracker and collaborating with other reporters and legislative analysts. There are also opportunities to travel and cover Senate campaigns. What you will do: Demonstrated ability to report and write news stories and features with minimal editing under deadline. Working knowledge of journalism principles and techniques. Demonstrated ability to develop and cover a beat, including developing sources, developing story ideas, and conducting interviews. Knowledge of federal and state legislative, regulatory, and judicial processes. Ability to attend outside meetings, hearings, news events, etc., and to report on them clearly and accurately for deadline. Proficiency in MS Office. Ability to use Bloomberg Industry Group publishing tools and other technology effectively with Bloomberg Industry Group training. Excellent proofreading skills. You need to have: Bachelor’s degree with coursework in English or journalism preferred. 5 - 7 years’ experience in journalism, including at least one year reporting on subject areas covered by assigned publications. Compensation Range: $85,000.00-$105,000.00 Placement in the salary range will be decided upon completion of the interview process. Salary determination will be determined based on factors including but not limited to relevant experience, demonstrated skills related to the requirements of the role, education, certifications, and geographic location. Equal Opportunity Bloomberg Industry Group maintains a continuing policy of non-discrimination in employment. It is Bloomberg Industry Group’s policy to provide equal opportunity and access for all persons, and the Company is committed to attracting, retaining, developing, and promoting the most qualified individuals without regard to age, ancestry, color, gender identity or expression, genetic predisposition or carrier status, marital status, national or ethnic origin, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation, sexual and other reproductive health decisions, parental or caring status, physical or mental disability, pregnancy or maternity/parental leave, protected veteran status, status as a victim of domestic violence, or any other classification protected by applicable law (“Protected Characteristic”). item.title: Public Policy Coordinator Program And Data Support
item.description: Description Pay Range - $50,939.20 - $55,016.00 (Median Pay $52,510,00) I. Purpose & Summary of Position: The Texas Council on Family Violence is the only 501(c)(3) nonprofit coalition in Texas dedicated solely to creating safer communities and freedom from family violence. With a state-wide reach and direct local impact, TCFV, with the collective strength of more than 1000 members, shapes public policy, equips service providers, and initiates strategic prevention efforts. Using TCFV’s strategic plan as a guide, the Public Policy Coordinator, Program and Data Support is responsible for strengthening and expanding the capacity of family violence programs and community partners working to create system change in support of survivors of family violence. The Public Policy Coordinator , Program and Data Support works on the Program Policy Focus Area of the Policy Team within TCFV, reporting to the Public Policy Manager (Programmatic Focus Area) and/or the Director of Public Policy. The Public Policy Coordinator will focus on supporting the agency and programs by focusing on the following areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety. They will also provide support, training, and technical assistance to agencies and professionals that directly advocate for survivors of family violence, including state and federal laws around service provision to survivors of family violence. II. Priority functions / Accountabilities: A. Training Development and Coordination – 15% Coordinate, develop and offer trainings on issues related to the areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety for a wide variety of audiences. Create, develop and update written materials and protocols for use by survivors, family violence programs, and allied professionals, with particular emphasis on building knowledge and skills related to areas of data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety . Utilize effective, current, innovative methods to strengthen and expand the capacity of family violence service providers. B. Technical Assistance and Consultation – 35% Provide technical assistance to advocates, family violence programs, and other entities with a focus on data science and analytics, funder regulations and program data reporting, data storytelling, allocations, privacy rights, confidentiality, and technology safety . Support relevant TCFV listservs and respond to relevant email accounts to support program staff across the state via training and technical assistance. Ensures that calls and requests for technical assistance are responded to in a supportive, timely manner. C. Systems Advocacy Efforts– 35% Assist in TCFV’s Allocations committee processes with a focus on leading data and analytics. Support evaluation efforts related to the Texas State Plan. Assist policy team in a variety of data analysis and analytics as requested. Develop and maintain expertise on state and federal laws pertaining to confidentiality and privilege for survivors of family violence. Research, track, and provide recommendations about bills during legislative session, including TCFV’s priorities and other proposals that would impact family violence survivors and the allies who serve them. Other projects and responsibilities may be added and/or changed at the discretion of the Managers and Directors. D. Administrative- 15% Ensures timely and accurate reporting of grant activities, including contributing information for the agency’s funding applications. Ensures timely and accurate submission of evaluations, reports, and other required or requested documentation. Actively participate in team efforts to deepen our practices of relationship building, learning, and leadership development. Leads policy team efforts around Tableau. Qualifications III. Minimum Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Sought: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below represent the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Required: Texas residency required. This role is a hybrid remote job and requires in-office responsibilities, in Austin, on a periodic basis. If not directly located in Austin, successful applicants must maintain an ability and availability to attend in-person team activities, necessary Policy, or TCFV-wide activities, and attend in-person meetings and other responsibilities, as requested by the Policy Manager or Policy Directors. Hybrid staff are also expected to travel and attend in person activities associated with their job descriptions and duties. Outside of these expectations, hybrid staff work remotely within the state of Texas. Experience incorporating the perspectives of multiple communities, including BIPOC survivors, advocates, and stakeholders in the consideration of impacts and outcomes of a decision-making process. Experience in data science, data analytics, or other data analysis. Strong team building and leadership skills to effectively manage Coalition activities through vision, strategic planning, and expertise. Self-driven to work independently with minimal supervision and use disciplined time management skills. Thorough knowledge of domestic violence issues and the circumstances faced by those experiencing it. Critical analytical skills to understand the political, social, financial, and external issues affecting service providers; to foresee and interpret trends and dynamics changing needs of TCFV constituents; and to develop process and resources to respond effectively and in a timely manner. Communication skills suitable for presentation and written publication, for internal and external distribution. Self-driven to manage time and complete multiple activities and grant deliverables within deadlines. Working experience with Microsoft Office applications and can adeptly navigate new software and technology. Ability to work collaboratively in a team, providing support and constructive feedback in interpersonal interaction with staff, board, and members. Must be proactive, communicative, responsive, creative, flexible, to accomplish agency and program goals; and possess mission of service attitude with a strong commitment to and knowledge of constituent service and relations. Ability to work within a team to offer support and collaborate on team projects. Ability to maintain strict confidentiality of employee, donor, funder, survivor, and case information. Preferred: Bachelor’s Degree. We will consider a combination of education and related experience. (Equivalency formula: two years of experience is equal to one year of education.) Bi-lingual English/Spanish language a plus as is any bi-lingual / bi-cultural lived experience. Experience providing direct services to individuals affected by domestic violence preferred. IV. Working Conditions and Environment/Physical Demands: Ability to communicate and converse in English. Travel up to 25% during non-legislative session times. Ability to frequently tolerate prolonged stationary positions and frequently move about a large public building. Ability to engage in frequent public contact. Professional attire may be required for most public-facing work. Ability to work in or from a remote location or from a home-based office. Must possess the emotional and physical stamina to deal with a variety of high-pressure situations, such as: responding to urgent legislative issues, handling difficult internal and external interactions, and effectively working long and, at times, odd hours which could exceed 40 hours or include weekends as necessary. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and minimum level of work being performed. They are not intended to be construed as exhaustive of all duties, responsibilities, and skills required for the position. The employee will be required to perform any other job-related duties as required by the job objectives, the CEO and mission and philosophy of TCFV.

item.title: Election Specialist I
item.description: Functional Statement Under general supervision of the Election Operations Team Lead, assists with certification of ballots and handling inquires; acts as contributor to Board publications; provides general interpretations of various election laws to election authorities, election judges, and the general public; provides oral and written answers related to questions regarding various statutes; conducts election judge training classes for election authorities. Essential Function 1 Assists in providing general interpretation of various election laws; advises local election authorities and officials concerning necessary implementation, abolishment or revision of procedures resulting from changes in statutes and/or rules and regulations. Essential Function 2 Assists in the preparation and writing of various agency publications to be used for in-house reference and election authority distribution; conducts training sessions for various election authorities as assigned. Essential Function 3 Assists in providing written answers related to questions arising out of the Illinois Election Code to election officials and authorities, legislative staff and members of the general public; refers obscure or novel inquiries to senior personnel. Essential Function 4 At the request of the director/operations lead, assists in all activities of candidate nomination filing. This includes, but is not limited to, the following: petition filing, objection filing, service of notice for objections, electoral board meeting support, candidate withdrawals, and ballot certification. Essential Function 5 Performs other duties as assigned or required which are reasonably within the scope of duties enumerated above. Minimum Qualifications 1 Requires skill, knowledge, and mental development equivalent to completion of four years college with courses in public administration, government or communications, or other related field. Minimum Qualifications 2 A four-year degree may be substituted with one year of professional elections experience such as might be acquired working in election administration. Minimum Qualifications 3 Requires ability to travel extensively throughout the state to monitor elections and conduct election judge training seminars. The State Board of Elections welcomes all and promotes workplace diversity. It is our individual traits, character, and experiences that make each of us special and unique. It is only when we bring that individualism together and work as a diverse team that we thrive. There is no place for discrimination based on race, religion, culture, sexual identity or orientation, age, or disability at the State Board of Elections. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Use the “Apply” button at the top right or bottom right of this posting to begin the application process. If you are not already signed in, you will be prompted to do so. State employees should sign in to the career portal for State of Illinois employees – a link is available at the top left of the Illinois.jobs2web.com homepage in the blue ribbon. item.title: Policy And Legislative Affairs Coordinator
item.description: Position: Policy and Legislative Affairs Coordinator Classification: Full-time, Exempt Reports to: Director, Special Projects Company: Texans Together Location: Houston, TX Position Description: The Policy and Legislative Affairs Coordinator serves as the organization's lead resource for legislative affairs, policy analysis, advocacy strategy, and government relations. This position monitors legislative and regulatory developments, analyzes their impact on organizational priorities, and provides recommendations to executive leadership regarding advocacy efforts and implementation strategies. Working closely with the Director of Special Projects, the Coordinator will help develop and execute legislative engagement strategies, build relationships with policymakers and stakeholders, coordinate advocacy activities, and support organizational readiness for policy and regulatory changes. Primary Responsibilities: Monitor legislation, regulatory activity, and policy developments at the local, state, and federal levels. Track bills and legislative initiatives relevant to the organization's mission and strategic priorities. Analyze proposed legislation and assess potential impacts on operations, programs, and stakeholders. Develop policy summaries, legislative reports, issue briefs, and executive-level recommendations. Provide strategic guidance regarding emerging policy issues. Assist in the development and implementation of the organization's advocacy agenda and legislative priorities. Execute advocacy strategies and activities aligned with organizational goals. Prepare policy positions, talking points, briefing documents, and stakeholder communications. Recommend advocacy approaches and engagement opportunities based on legislative developments. Coordinate organizational responses to policy proposals and legislative initiatives. Support the cultivation and maintenance of relationships with members of the Texas Legislature, legislative staff, state agencies, and key stakeholders. Support leadership engagement with elected officials and policy influencers. Coordinate legislative meetings, site visits, presentations, and informational briefings. Represent the organization at legislative hearings, stakeholder meetings, conferences, and public forums. Serve as a liaison between the organization and governmental entities. Support legislative engagement efforts during legislative sessions and interim periods. Track committee hearings, legislative deadlines, policy proposals, and stakeholder activities. Identify opportunities for strategic engagement and advocacy. Prepare leadership for legislative meetings, testimony, and policy discussions. Lead policy-focused projects and strategic initiatives. Research emerging trends, best practices, and policy innovations relevant to child welfare and community-based care. Develop reports, presentations, dashboards, and briefing materials for executive leadership and board members. Required Qualifications: Bachelor's degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Government, Public Administration, Social Work, Communications, or a related field. Minimum two (2) years’ experience in government affairs, public policy, legislative affairs, advocacy, child welfare, public administration, communications, or a related field. Experience working with the Texas Legislature, legislative offices, state agencies, or governmental entities. Experience in child welfare, community-based care, human services, education, healthcare, or nonprofit advocacy. Preferred Qualifications: Master’s degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Law, Social Work, or a related field preferred. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge of Texas legislative processes and policymaking. Strong writing and communication skills. Ability to synthesize complex information into concise summaries. Strong project management and organizational skills. Ability to independently manage multiple projects and competing priorities. Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities. Ability to translate strategic direction into actionable plans and measurable outcomes. Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills. Ability to influence and coordinate work across teams without formal authority. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment. Sound judgment, initiative, and a willingness to take ownership of projects and results. Work Conditions: Environment: Office Work Schedule: Monday – Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Travel: Occasional (Must have reliable transportation, valid Texas Driver License and current Auto Insurance) DePelchin is Proud to be an Equal Opportunity Workplace. DePelchin is committed to selecting and employing the best and most qualified person available for each job opening without unlawful discrimination of any kind. Additionally, DePelchin is committed to providing a work environment free of discrimination and harassment on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation and gender identity), marital or parental status, veteran status, religion, national origin, age, disability, family medical history, genetic information, or political affiliation.

item.title: Director Federal Government Affairs
item.description: Job Description Summary The Director, Federal Government Affairs serves as a key representative and advocate for Novartis at the federal level, building and maintaining strategic relationships across Congress, the Administration, federal agencies, industry associations, and the broader healthcare policy community. The Director will develop and execute advocacy strategies that advance enterprise priorities, shape policy outcomes, and support the company's business objectives. The role provides strategic counsel to senior leadership on legislative and regulatory developments, drives engagement with external stakeholders and trade organizations, and helps strengthen Novartis' reputation as a trusted, innovative, and influential voice in healthcare policy. This role is based out of our Washington D.C. office 3x/week. Job Description Key responsibilities: Provide respected, credible and active day-to-day representation of Novartis in Washington, D.C. by establishing and maintaining a strong, sophisticated network of relationships on Capitol Hill, within the Executive Branch, and relevant agencies and across the broader healthcare/policy community. Proactively support the company’s enterprise priorities through strategic alignment of business priorities with the company’s advocacy and political agenda, including healthcare, tax, and workforce issues. Lead the creation and execution of specific government affairs strategies to ensure an in-creased understanding of the company with respect to its strategic positioning in the industry, and build the company’s reputation for high integrity, competitive leadership and sustained performance. Develop a strategic direction as it relates to the company’s outreach and engagement with federal government officials, issue management, and third parties. Analyze legislative language; prepare and provide executive summaries of complex legislation and assist other NVS functions with issues involving federal officials. Drive federal advocacy agenda and provide input/recommendations at key associations such as PhRMA, BIO, and others that impact policy development and strategy. Manage expectation of Public Affairs leadership – keeping all relevant stakeholders informed on existent and upcoming federal legislative issues, delivering strategies for success and executing against those strategies. Essential Requirements: 10+ years of experience with federal legislative, executive and public policy-making activities preferred. Understanding of the healthcare and pharmaceutical industries and/or tax preferred. In-depth knowledge of the U.S. legislative process, including an under-standing of the roles and decision-making processes of the Executive Agencies, the U.S. Senate, and U.S. House of Representatives. Strong background in analyzing legislative language and providing strategic insights to support company functions involving federal officials. Excellent communication skills to effectively represent the company in meetings and discussions with federal policymakers and stakeholders. Proficiency in utilizing data-driven impact assessments to inform decision-making and policy development. Benefits & Rewards The salary for this position is expected to range between $176,400 and $327,600 per year. The final salary offered is determined based on factors like, but not limited to, relevant skills and experience, and upon joining Novartis will be reviewed periodically. Novartis may change the published salary range based on company and market factors. Your compensation will include a performance-based cash incentive and, depending on the level of the role, eligibility to be considered for annual equity awards. US-based eligible employees will receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, life and disability benefits, a 401(k) with company contribution and match, and a variety of other benefits. In addition, employees are eligible for a generous time off package including vacation, personal days, holidays and other leaves. Why Novartis: Helping people with disease and their families takes more than innovative science. It takes a community of smart, passionate people like you. Collaborating, supporting and inspiring each other. Combining to achieve breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. Ready to create a brighter future together? https://www.novartis.com/about/strategy/people-and-culture Join our Novartis Network: Not the right Novartis role for you? Sign up to our talent community to stay connected and learn about suitable career opportunities as soon as they come up: https://talentnetwork.novartis.com/network Benefits and Rewards: Read our handbook to learn about all the ways we’ll help you thrive personally and professionally: https://www.novartis.com/careers/benefits-rewards EEO Statement: The Novartis Group of Companies are Equal Opportunity Employers. We do not discriminate in recruitment, hiring, training, promotion or other employment practices for reasons of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital or veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. Accessibility and reasonable accommodations The Novartis Group of Companies are committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application process, or to perform the essential functions of a position, please send an e-mail to us.reasonableaccommodations@novartis.com or call +1(877)395-2339 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. Please include the job requisition number in your message. Salary Range $176,400.00 - $327,600.00 Skills Desired Affiliate Marketing, Communication Methods, Influencing Skills, Job Interviews, Leadership, Marketing, Microsoft Access, Photography, Policy Development, Political Analysis, Press Releases, Prioritization, Public Affairs, Social Media, Stakeholder Management

item.title: Lead Legislative Specialist
item.description: Summary Serves as the Lead Legislative Analyst for the Officer of the Assistant Secretary of War for Legislative Affairs. Responsibilities include serving as the technical expert and authority on all legislative activities in support of the annual legislative program surrounding the annual National Defense Authorization Act and Appropriations Bills. Duties Incumbent typical work assignments may include the following: Leads the Legislative Analysis team members to achieve specific tasks, produce work products and services to meet program and production goals. Ensures that the organization's strategic plan, mission, vision and values are communicated to the team and integrated into the team's strategies, goals, objectives, work plans and work products and services. Manages the congressional reporting requirements process for the Office of the Secretary of War. Manages the Department of War (DoW) Congressional Hearings process. Requirements Conditions of employment U.S. Citizenship is required Males born after 12-31-59 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service (see https://www.sss.gov/Home/Registration) May be required to successfully complete a probationary/trial period Must be determined suitable for federal employment Required to participate in the direct deposit program This position is subject to pre-employment and random drug testing (See Additional Information) This position is subject to the DoD Priority Placement Program The incumbent must be able to obtain and maintain a Top Secret security clearance with SCI and SAP components. A Special Background Investigation (SBI) is required with favorable adjudication by a determining authority. This position may require occasional travel away from your normal duty station for official business on military or commercial aircraft. Travel may be up to 25% The incumbent may be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and/or holidays and/or overtime. Qualifications In order to qualify for this position, you must meet the requirements described below. You may qualify at the GS-14 level, if you fulfill the following qualification requirement: One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service (experience may have been gained in the private sector) that demonstrates your ability to 1) Managing the congressional reporting requirements process to ensure all submissions meet substantive sufficiency standards; 2) Analyzing hearing summaries and transcripts to support assigned components in addressing congressional hearing conclusions and 3) Preparing reports, maintaining records of work accomplishments and administrative information. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. All qualifications and education requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Your resume may not exceed two (2) pages . For qualifications determinations, it is recommended that applicants include their months and hours worked per week for each employment listed on their resume. If a determination is not able to be made about the duration of your creditable experience for qualification requirements, you will be removed from consideration. Read more about what should I include in my federal resume at https://help.usajobs.gov/faq/application/documents/resume/what-to-include ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: Federal agencies treat active duty service member as veterans, disabled veterans, and preference eligible, when they submit, as part of their application package, a "certification" of active service in lieu of a DD-214, indicating the service member is otherwise eligible and will be discharged or released within 120 days from the date of submission. A "certification" letter should be on letterhead of the appropriate military branch of the service and contain (1) the military service dates including the expected discharge or release date; and (2) the character of service. This "certification" must include your rank, dates of active duty service, type of discharge and character of service (i.e. honorable), and date any terminal leave will begin. It must be signed by, or by direction of, the adjutant, personnel officer, or commander of your unit or higher headquarters. Active duty members that fail to provide a valid "certification" of service with their initial application will be found "not eligible". Members may be appointed before the effective date of their military retirement/separation if they are on terminal leave. Current or Former Political Appointees: Agencies must seek prior approval from OPM before they can appoint a current or recent political appointee to a competitive or non-political excepted service position at any level. If you are currently or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, or Non-career SES employee in the executive branch, you MUST disclose that to the Human Resources Office. Time-in-grade requirements must be met by the closing date of this announcement and clearly documented in your resume. Education Education cannot be substituted for experience. Additional information Condition of Employment: This position is designated as a Testing Designated Position (TDP) under the civilian drug-testing program. As a mandatory requirement for employment in this TDP, the incumbent is to (a) refrain from the use of illegal drugs and (b) if required, submit to urinalysis testing. The selectee must sign statements acknowledging the position is identified as a TDP. Probationary Periods: As a condition of employment for accepting this position, you will be required to serve a 1-year probationary period during which we will evaluate your fitness and whether your continued employment advances the public interest. In determining if your employment advances the public interest, we may consider: - your performance and conduct; - the needs and interests of the agency; - whether your continued employment would advance organizational goals of the agency or the Government; and - whether your continued employment would advance the efficiency of the Federal service. Upon completion of your probationary period your employment will be terminated unless you receive certification, in writing, that your continued employment advances the public interest. Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP): This program applies to employees who have been involuntarily separated from a Federal service position within the competitive service or Federal service employees whose positions have been deemed surplus or no longer needed. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: (1) meet ICTAP eligibility criteria; (2) be rated well-qualified for the position; and, (3) submit the appropriate documentation to support your ICTAP eligibility. For more information visit: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/ Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing an online application, you may request an alternative application. Please send an email to the following address for information on how to obtain an alternative application: whs.job.application.assistance@mail.mil Reemployed Annuitants: Applicants in receipt of an annuity based on civilian employment in the Federal Service are subject to the DoD Policy on The Employment of Annuitants (DODI 1400.25, volume 300). http://www.esd.whs.mil/DD/DoD-Issuances/140025/ Nepotism : Under the provisions of 5 USC 3110, an individual may not be appointed into a position if the position is under the supervisory chain of command of a relative. Additional vacancies may be filled by this announcement. Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. A career with the U.S. government provides employees with a comprehensive benefits package. As a federal employee, you and your family will have access to a range of benefits that are designed to make your federal career very rewarding. Opens in a new window Learn more about federal benefits . Review our benefits Eligibility for benefits depends on the type of position you hold and whether your position is full-time, part-time or intermittent. Contact the hiring agency for more information on the specific benefits offered.

item.title: Multimedia Coordinator Outreach Government Affairs
item.description: About Houston-Galveston Area Council The Houston-Galveston Area Council is one of the largest regional planning commissions in the country with a diverse service area of 13 counties and more than 7 million people. We are the pulse of our region addressing issues that cross city limits and county lines every single day. We make decisions that affect our transportation system, ensure the safety and well-being of our seniors, connect people to jobs, help families recover from natural disasters, preserve water quality for our children, and so much more. We work to make the region a great place to live, work, and thrive. What will I be doing? The Multimedia Coordinator is a strategic communicator who will connect H-GAC’s programs, priorities, and regional impact with the people and organizations the agency serves. As part of the Outreach & Government Affairs team, this position will create clear, compelling, and visually engaging communications for residents, member governments, elected officials, community partners, media, and other stakeholders. The coordinator will support strategic communications, graphic design, digital marketing, social media, media relations, and intergovernmental relations. This position will also monitor governmental developments, assess their relevance to H-GAC, and help align communications activities with organizational strategy. The successful candidate will be an excellent writer and strong graphic designer with sound judgment, audience awareness, and an interest in the governmental environment in which H-GAC operates. Strategic Communications & Content Development Help develop public affairs and communications strategies that advance H-GAC’s mission, programs, and regional priorities. Work with leadership and program staff to identify audiences, messages, communications needs, and appropriate outreach channels. Write and edit content for websites, newsletters, reports, presentations, social media, talking points, and outreach materials. Translate technical, governmental, and policy information into clear, audience-focused content. Maintain editorial calendars, communications standards, and project workflows while ensuring materials are accurate and consistent. Graphic Design & Multimedia Communications Create polished print and digital materials, including reports, infographics, presentations, newsletters, advertisements, event materials, and social media graphics. Transform regional data, policies, and technical subjects into accessible and visually engaging stories. Apply strong design judgment in typography, layout, imagery, branding, and information hierarchy. Maintain brand consistency, develop reusable templates, and prepare files for print and digital production. Coordinate with creative vendors and support photography, video, and other multimedia projects as needed. Digital Marketing & Social Media Plan and create digital content that builds awareness of H-GAC programs, services, events, and regional initiatives. Develop copy, graphics, short-form video, and multimedia content for social media, websites, email, newsletters, and digital campaigns. Manage content calendars and coordinate approvals, publishing, and monitoring. Monitor online conversations and news for communications opportunities or reputational concerns. Use analytics and digital best practices to improve audience reach and engagement. Project Coordination Manage multiple communications and public affairs projects from concept through delivery. Coordinate schedules, requirements, reviews, approvals, and final production. Support public meetings, conferences, board-related activities, community events, and outreach campaigns. Explore emerging communications tools and responsible uses of artificial intelligence to improve quality and efficiency. Key Qualifications Excellent writing, editing, visual communication, and verbal presentation skills. Strong graphic design capabilities and a portfolio demonstrating expertise in layout, typography, branding, information design, and digital content. Ability to interpret governmental, policy, and technical information for different audiences. Understanding of how communications, government relations, media relations, and stakeholder engagement support organizational strategy. Proficiency with Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop. Experience developing content for print, websites, email, social media, and presentations. Strong project-management skills and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Sound judgment and the ability to work effectively with executives, elected officials, government staff, media, vendors, and community partners. Commitment to accessible communications, nonpartisan public service, and regional cooperation. Do you have… Bachelor’s degree in an applicable academic discipline or related field of study 3 years of experience working with local government, nonprofit programs, school, or in job-related duties Preferred 3+ years of progressively responsible experience in public affairs, strategic communications, government relations, or public-sector communications. Experience working for a government, regional organization, public agency, nonprofit, association, news organization, legislative office, or public-sector consulting firm. Experience communicating with elected officials, government staff, media, and community stakeholders. Knowledge of the Houston-Galveston region and issues affecting local governments. Experience monitoring governmental activity and connecting developments to organizational strategy. Familiarity with media relations, digital advertising, photography, video, data visualization, or web content. Knowledge of the Texas Open Meetings Act, public-information practices, or public-sector accessibility requirements. Working knowledge of Spanish or experience developing multilingual materials. Salary range: $70,000.00 - $77,000.00 All employees of H-GAC are required to reside within the agency’s region of service to support our commitment to excellence in service of our region. H-GAC is an equal opportunity/ADA employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, or protected veteran status.

item.title: Student Senate Co Advisor 2 Vacancies Internal Posting
item.description: Job Description Central Carolina Community College is committed to being an employer of choice, grounded in excellence, integrity, respect, collaboration, innovation, and leadership. We provide a supportive, growth-focused workplace where professionals can thrive while helping students access first-class educational and workforce opportunities. Join us in shaping futures, strengthening our region, and contributing to a mission-driven culture rooted in service and opportunity. Central Carolina Community College is seeking two faculty or staff members to serve as Co-Advisors for the College’s Student Senate. Student Senate is not a student club or general student organization. It serves as a representative student leadership body for the College and provides students with opportunities to participate in college life, shared governance, leadership development, campus events, and statewide student leadership experiences. The Director of Student Engagement serves as the lead advisor for the Student Senate. Co-Advisors work in close collaboration with the Director, with responsibility for advising and supporting Student Senators shared among the three individuals. Together, the advising team supports Student Senators, coordinates Senate operations, facilitates leadership development, maintains regular meeting structure and accountability, and connects student leaders with meaningful opportunities to serve the College community. This is an internal posting open to all CCCC employees (full-time, part-time and adjunct). Time Commitment This is a year-round stipend assignment requiring shared responsibility for advising the Student Senate. The position requires an average commitment of approximately 10-15 hours per month per advisor, with additional time required during elections, onboarding, conference preparation, leadership programming, major college events, and requested mascot appearances. Advisors should expect responsibilities outside of normal work hours, including evenings and weekends. Typical responsibilities include: Monthly Student Senate meetings. Student mentoring and advising. Election and onboarding support. Event planning and Student Senate administration. Student leadership development. Campus event support. Coordination of Student Senator participation in college events. Coordination of Charlee the Mascot coverage at requested events. Budget, travel, and administrative documentation. Conference preparation and student travel support. Travel Expectations This assignment requires travel throughout the year. Co-Advisors share responsibility for traveling with and supervising students at approved Student Senate events and leadership experiences in accordance with College policies and in coordination with the Director of Student Engagement. Typical travel includes: Four Student Senate or student leadership conferences across North Carolina each year. Statewide student leadership meetings, training, or conferences as approved. College-sponsored leadership experiences and student engagement activities. Other approved Student Senate travel or leadership development opportunities. Reporting Relationship For purposes of this stipend assignment, the Student Senate Co-Advisors will work collaboratively with the Director of Student Engagement, campus partners, and other College departments to support Student Senate operations, student leadership, student voice, and student success. Performance Expectations The Co-Advisors will work collaboratively to: Maintain an active, visible, and accountable Student Senate. Support Student Senators in fulfilling their responsibilities with professionalism, integrity, and dedication. Foster meaningful student engagement, leadership development, civic engagement, and student representation. Ensure regular monthly Student Senate meetings and appropriate documentation of attendance, participation, and action items. Support Student Senate participation in college events and student engagement initiatives. Ensure appropriate coverage and coordination for Charlee the Mascot at requested college events. Increase Student Senate visibility, participation, and connection with the broader student body. Successfully coordinate elections, onboarding, meetings, leadership activities, conferences, travel, and campus engagement opportunities. Collaborate with College departments to elevate student voice and support student-centered initiatives. Represent Central Carolina Community College with professionalism while supporting students at on-campus and off-campus events. Essential Duties Working collaboratively with the Director of Student Engagement, the Co-Advisors will: Serve as Co-Advisors to the Student Senate under the leadership of the Director of Student Engagement, who serves as the lead advisor. Share responsibility equally with the Director of Student Engagement for the direct advising, mentoring, and support of Student Senators, including providing consistent guidance, communication, accountability, and leadership development. Recruit, mentor, and support Student Senators. Collaborate with the Director of Student Engagement to coordinate Student Senate elections, appointments, leadership development, onboarding, and succession planning. Collaborate with the Director of Student Engagement to plan and facilitate monthly Student Senate meetings and additional officer or leadership meetings as needed, with meeting responsibilities shared across the advising team. Support Student Senators in understanding and fulfilling the expectations outlined in the Student Senate Bylaws and Student Senate Commitment Contract. Guide Student Senators in representing the student body with professionalism, integrity, and accountability. Support Student Senators in developing leadership, communication, collaboration, advocacy, and civic engagement skills. Assist Student Senators in identifying student needs, concerns, and opportunities for improved student engagement and campus connection. Coordinate Student Senate involvement in college events, campus activities, student engagement initiatives, and leadership opportunities. Ensure appropriate Student Senate representation and support at requested college events. Coordinate coverage for Charlee the Mascot at requested college events, including communication, scheduling, student support, and coordination with event organizers. Collaborate with Student Engagement, Student Services, Academic Affairs, Marketing and Communications, campus partners, and other College departments to support student involvement and representation. Support the management of Student Senate budgets, expenditures, travel, and related documentation in accordance with College policies. Maintain Student Senate records, attendance, meeting notes, rosters, event participation records, and other administrative documentation. Support communication between Student Senators, College leadership, campus partners, and the broader student body. Coordinate Student Senate participation in conferences, leadership experiences, recognition events, college activities, and other approved programming. Maintain regular communication and coordination with the Director of Student Engagement and fellow Co-Advisor to ensure consistent guidance, expectations, communication, and support for Student Senators. Represent Central Carolina Community College with professionalism while supporting students at on-campus and off-campus events. Recognizing and respecting the variety of experiences and contributions represented by all of our students, employees, and community, the Student Senate Co-Advisor will encourage a learning environment where everyone is supported and valued for their unique perspectives and experiences and will foster and promote the participation of all members of our diverse communities. Minimum Requirements Full-time faculty or staff member at Central Carolina Community College. Demonstrated commitment to student success, leadership development, student engagement, and student voice. Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills. Ability to supervise students and represent the College during off-campus activities and travel. Ability to support student leaders in a professional, inclusive, and student-centered manner. Preferred Requirements Experience advising student government, student leadership programs, student organizations, or student leaders. Experience supporting student events, leadership development, civic engagement, or campus programming. Experience coordinating meetings, budgets, travel, event logistics, or student programming. Familiarity with shared governance, student advocacy, parliamentary procedure, or student leadership development. Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and campuses.
