item.title: Voter Outreach Specialist Public Outreach Specialist
item.description: Description Pay range: $46,441 - $74,769 This vacancy is in the Voter Registration & Elections department. The purpose of this position is to: •Educate, inform, and empower all DeKalb County residents on voter registration and election-related subject matters. •Assist voters with completing registration and absentee ballot applications. •Participate in discussion panels, to make presentations at town hall and community meetings, speak at secondary schools, colleges and universities. •Develop printed collateral and web content for translation and design. Essential Functions: Receives and responds to citizen inquiries, concerns, requests, problems, and complaints; actively listens to callers and visitors; conveys understanding and willingness to resolve issues; promotes and establishes goodwill; exercises tact and discretion; remains composed with rude or irate constituents; addresses or routes concerns based on knowledge of County services; provides information and assistance; and follows-up with citizens. Assists citizens with resolution of problems and complaints; communicates with County departments to identify, research, and resolve issues; connects constituents with resources, referrals, and support; and refers complex or sensitive problems to appropriate staff for resolution. Attends community or homeowner meetings; represents County; makes presentations; answers questions; provides information; and advises appropriate staff of issues and concerns. Prepares correspondence, emails, and written replies; composes, proofreads, and edits letters, emails and other responses to constituent questions and concerns; and sends replies to constituents. Maintains outreach records and files; compiles and tracks data related to inquiries and complaints and the disposition thereof; maintains notes and records to facilitate follow-up and problem resolution; and prepares related reports. Functions specific to Voter Registration & Elections: Develops and executes outreach and community relations strategies. Maintains and updates all departmental voter education and public information materials. Creates, designs, composes and edits brochures, fact sheets, surveys, news releases, and public service announcements for department. Researches voter information and current laws through state, federal and outside county websites. Engages with other county departments and counterparts in other counties to share and learn best practices. Conveys understanding and willingness to resolve issues. Promotes and establishes goodwill. Exercises tact and discretion. Contacts organizations, churches, senior centers, schools, etc. with requests to present information and answer questions regarding upcoming elections and new laws throughout DeKalb County. Prepares applicable voter information packets. Conducts voter registration drives. Assists voters with completing registration and absentee ballot applications. Participates at events and meetings, registers voters, reviews application for completeness, and answers questions. Provides pertinent information on voter registration, upcoming elections, and new laws that have passed. Advises appropriate staff of issues and concerns. Organizes and leads public meetings and voter education and outreach efforts. Measures performance of public meetings and events, including participant feedback and partnering with community leaders, civic organizations, churches, schools and colleges. Designs and maintains database to enter comments and ratings from voter surveys. Designs and maintain database of community contacts and participation at events. Provides monthly statistical voter data and reports from databases. Prepares correspondence, emails, and written replies; composes, proofreads, and edits letters, emails and other responses to constituent questions and concerns; and sends replies to constituents. Determines and assists in creation of appropriate information to present to community groups. Minimum Qualifications: Associate degree in Public Administration, Public Relations, Communications, or related field required; three years of experience in communications, customer service, or a related field; or any equivalent combination of education, training, and experience which provides the requisite knowledge, skills, and abilities for this job. Preferred: Three years of experience in elections or public outreach

item.title: Legislative Analyst
item.description: Under general direction, the legislative analyst is responsible for providing legislative research and analysis on a wide and diverse number of subject matter issues associated with municipal roles, including policy committees and other stakeholders. The position requires that the individual has the ability to help develop and implement strategies and tactics in order to influence the development of laws, policies, budgets, and regulations for state and local programs that affect cities. RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES Assist in identifying, analyzing and developing recommendations for the League on state and federal policy issues that affect municipalities. Research legislative issues and compile data to support the League’s lobbying efforts on proposed legislation and rulemaking. Monitor state and federal legislation that may affect Florida’s municipalities. Follow trends in municipal budgets and monitor revenue sources. Analyze the state budget and report relevant changes that affect municipalities. Assist lobbyists in following state agency activities and meetings as directed. Develop, coordinate and promote the legislative department’s research activities, including assisting with conducting short term studies and research projects, developing research reports on a variety of topics, collecting and disseminating information and data. Respond to requests for information from city officials, state agencies, state cabinet officials and staff, and others. Respond to inquiries from League members, and state agency and legislative staff regarding subject matter issues. Establish and maintain relationships with other state municipal leagues. Including, but not limited to, coordinating informal quarterly meetings with legislative staff. Assist lobbyists with presentations of issues to Legislature, League members and staff. Strategize legislative fixes through amendments or maneuvers to support lobbying efforts. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES Ability to manage multiple tasks, with a high attention to detail, including organizing and coordinating complex projects. Capacity to foresee needs and take initiative. Knowledge and understanding of local and state government structures. Knowledge of the techniques and procedures used in research and analysis, possessing strong analytical and writing skills. Strong oral and written communication skills. Ability to work effectively as a member of a team both internally and with outside parties. Dynamic thinker with the ability to work independently with minimal guidance. TRAINING AND EXPERIENCE Degree from an accredited college, university, or equivalent in Business, Political Science, or a related field. Experience working in local or state government operations is preferred, or association-related experience. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. **PLEASE DO NOT APPLY IF YOU ARE A SMOKER**

item.title: Coordinator Government Affairs
item.description: Who We Are: It all starts with purpose. We are a purpose-driven nonprofit with a dynamic staff culture. With a meaningful purpose, motivated staff, and excellent benefits, working here will definitely have you smiling! The ADA’s headquarters is located in one of Chicago’s most iconic buildings, designed by a world-renowned architectural firm, and is close to public transportation. With more than 350 colleagues, the ADA Staff are some of the most talented people in the Chicago, Washington D.C., and Boston area. We were named a 2024 Best-in-Class Employer by Gallagher and Top Workplace by the Chicago Tribune in 2019 and 2021! Come join our team! Job Responsibilities: The Coordinator of Government Affairs will provide administrative, operational, financial, compliance, and communications support to the Government Affairs division. Responsibilities include coordinating daily operations; tracking projects and deadlines; scheduling meetings and conference calls; preparing agendas, reports, and other materials; monitoring and reporting financial activity; processing invoices; administering contracts and purchase orders; coordinating vendors; supporting compliance reporting and records management; managing website content; coordinating event logistics; and assisting with communications and public affairs activities. The Coordinator serves as a central administrative resource for CGA, Lobby Day, the State Lobbyist Conference, divisional meetings, and other Government Affairs activities. The position also provides backup support to the Manager of Government Affairs and assists with divisional operations, compliance activities, and special projects. Must Have: Bachelor's degree or experience in lieu of degree 3 years (or 7 years in lieu of a degree) experience coordinating projects, meetings, and administrative operations across cross-functional teams in administrative, operations, communications, public affairs, government affairs, legislative offices, trade associations, nonprofit organization, or executive support environments Knowledge of administrative and office operations, project coordination, records management, and the legislative, regulatory, advocacy, or association management environment Excellent written and verbal communication skills Ability to draft correspondence, format policy documents, manage website content, coordinate communications projects, and support public affairs and advocacy initiatives Ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain confidentiality, and work effectively with staff, vendors, consultants, government officials, and external stakeholders Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite Travel twice per year, 1-3 nights per trip, to attend meetings Position may require more than the standard number of hours of work within a work week, before or after hours work, and/or weekend work Nice to Have: Knowledge of meeting and event coordination, compliance reporting, and stakeholder communications Experience in a government affairs, public affairs, congressional, legislative, advocacy, association management, nonprofit, communications or executive office environment Just a few of the benefits offered to employees: Promotes Work/Life Balance Hybrid Work Schedule (2-3 days from home) Health insurance/ dental reimbursement plan Ample Paid time off 401(k) Flexible Spending Account Life insurance Tuition reimbursement Paid Parental Leave Pet Insurance Student Loan Refinance 2 days off to work at a charity event of your choice The ADA values a variety of backgrounds and experiences and is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to qualified job candidates. The ADA is an equal opportunity employer of protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment in open positions without regard to race, ethnicity, gender, color, religion, sex, age, marital status, ancestry, citizenship, physical or mental disability, medical condition, veteran status or any other characteristic. The American Dental Association is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities in our recruiting process. If you need any assistance or accommodations due to a disability, please let us know at recruiting@ada.org Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities.

item.title: Government Affairs Lead
item.description: WHO WE ARE: The National Multiple Sclerosis Society mobilizes people and resources to drive research for a cure and to address the challenges of everyone affected by MS. To fulfill this mission, the Society funds cutting-edge research, drives change through advocacy, facilitates professional education, collaborates with MS organizations around the world, and provides programs and services designed to help people with MS and their families move their lives forward. We partner with volunteers to accomplish our work. Staff members engage volunteers through effective and timely communications, facilitating meaningful opportunities, and continually seeking and providing feedback for reciprocal growth and learning. Job Summary: The AVP, Government Affairs (Government Affairs Lead) is responsible for leading the implementation of the Society's federal advocacy strategy and advancing legislative and regulatory priorities through direct engagement with policymakers, regulators, and key stakeholders. This role serves as the primary liaison to federal government entities and works in close partnership with Policy, Healthcare Access, and Mission leadership to execute coordinated advocacy efforts. This role collaborates closely with state government affairs colleagues and contracted lobbyists/ consultants to support alignment of federal and state advocacy efforts and identify opportunities for coordinated engagement. This position focuses on external engagement, relationship management, and advocacy execution, in close partnership with the advocacy and healthcare access leadership team and Mission leadership. Further, the Lead also contributes to the achievement of the Society's four strategic pillars by aligning work, decisions, and partnerships with enterprise priorities and actively collaborating across teams to advance mission outcomes. Location Requirements Remote - Flexible Location ​Work is primarily performed remotely, however, when possible and necessary, teams meet in person to conduct the business of the organization and build team relationships. Compensation | Benefits: The estimated hiring compensation range for this role is $100,000 - $120,000. Final offers will be based on the candidate's geographic location, consider career experience, and may vary from this range due to these and other factors. You will have the opportunity for a highly competitive, comprehensive benefit package that the Society provides to employees. Your benefits include: Considerable Paid Time Off Plan Paid Holidays 401k Retirement Savings Plan with Society match Commuter Benefit Plan Comprehensive Health & Welfare benefits including: Medical Dental Vision Flex Spending Accounts Life Insurance Disability Coverage Spring Health Membership offering free therapy and professional coaching, as well as additional voluntary benefit offerings. Not to mention, you will join an incredible mission focused team of people! Main Responsibilities: Federal Advocacy/ Legislative Strategy & Execution (60 %) Implement and advance federal government affairs strategies aligned with the Society's policy priorities, access principles, and strategic goals. Lead federal appropriations work through contracted lobbyist. Build and maintain relationships with Members of Congress, congressional staff, and key committees. Represent the organization in meetings, briefings, and advocacy events on Capitol Hill. Identify opportunities to advance legislative and regulatory priorities. Plan and execute advocacy initiatives such as: Capitol Hill days Legislative briefings Stakeholder roundtables Support grassroots and grass-tops engagement and strategies to amplify the voices of people with lived experience. Advocate for policy implementation that supports patient access and organizational priorities. Coordinate responses to federal rulemaking in partnership with the Policy team. Relationship Management & External Representation (20%) Build and manage relationships with advocacy partners, trade associations, and coalitions. Represent the organization at conferences, policy forums, and stakeholder convenings. Provide timely updates and strategic insights to internal stakeholders. Assess political landscape and implications for advocacy priorities. Partner closely with the VP, Policy to translate policy positions into actionable advocacy strategies. Collaborate with Communications to support advocacy campaigns and messaging. Support executive leadership with briefing materials, talking points, and meeting preparation. Federal-State Coordination (10%) Partner with state government affairs colleagues to promote alignment between federal and state advocacy priorities and messaging. Facilitate information sharing across federal and state advocacy teams regarding legislative and regulatory developments. Support cross-functional planning efforts related to advocacy campaigns, grassroots engagement initiatives, and key events. Identify opportunities to leverage federal advocacy activities in support of state priorities and vice versa. Contribute to planning and execution of major advocacy initiatives, including the Public Policy Conference and MS Activist engagement activities. Contribute to development of the advocacy budget. Lead the Federal Advocacy Team, providing strategic direction, coaching, and prioritization to maximize policy influence and resource allocation. Partner across the advocacy and healthcare access leadership team and across mission, marketing and communications and development to translate complex policy issues into accessible messages for diverse audiences, leveraging traditional and digital media, personal stories, and advocacy content to drive impact. Scope of Role: Team Responsibilities (10%) Attend/actively engage in training, professional development, conferences, and staff meetings. Share information, lessons learned, and stakeholder insights to support organizational objectives. Participate in cross-functional initiatives and contribute to team success. Collaborate across mission and contribute to the integrated mission operations plan, including working with regional Programs & Support team members to identify emerging issues. Develop a strong working knowledge of all Society and relevant 3rd party (e.g., Komodo) information systems including Salesforce or other Society CRMs. Maintain knowledge of MS, current treatments, disease and symptom management. Stay up to date on advances in MS through publications and research. Implement and follow National MS Society risk management policies and procedures. Participate in professional development activities to improve knowledge and understanding of healthcare systems and provider needs. Contribute to team meetings, provide support and feedback to colleagues. Other duties as assigned. What We're Looking For: 8–12 years of experience in federal government affairs, lobbying, congressional relations, or public policy advocacy. Strong understanding of federal legislative and regulatory processes. Demonstrated success engaging Congress, congressional staff, and federal agencies. Experience building coalitions and managing stakeholder relationships. Ability to translate complex policy issues into effective advocacy strategies and communications. Preferred qualifications Experience in healthcare, patient advocacy, nonprofit advocacy, or life sciences. Experience working within national associations or mission-driven organizations. Advanced degree (MPP, MPH, JD, or related field). We’re committed to supporting the growth of every employee through a structured and transparent approach to career development . We use Talent Portraits to define clear expectations, development opportunities, and advancement paths — whether you're growing as a people leader or deepening your expertise as an individual contributor. Each role is thoughtfully placed within one of these pathways (Leadership or Partner) to help you understand how it fits into our broader organization and your potential career journey. This position is classified as Leader - Leading Others. The National MS Society is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. We strive to create a workforce that reflects the communities we serve and where everyone feels empowered to bring their authentic selves to work. We need you and your unique talents and perspectives to help us write the last chapter on MS. APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: We appreciate your consideration of our job opportunities and strive to make it as effortless as possible to apply for our positions. With only a few required sections and the option to use our resume parsing tool, we aim to streamline the application experience, saving you time and effort. Additionally, if you wish to include a cover letter with your application, please feel free to attach it along with your resume , and any other documents required, to the Resume/CV document upload section at the bottom of the My Experience page. We appreciate your interest in joining our team and look forward to receiving your application! Important : You will not be able to modify your application after you submit it. The "My Experience" page is the only opportunity to add your cover letter and supporting document attachments. If you experience any trouble submitting your materials, please check out our FAQ & Contact Us page .

item.description: About Us: Consertus is an AI-native global capital program management and advisory firm that combines deep industry expertise with advanced digital capabilities to deliver smarter, faster, and more sustainable outcomes. Headquartered in Miami, Florida, and supported by a team of more than 1,500 professionals, we help clients plan, deliver, and optimize complex capital programs across the full project lifecycle. Our integrated capabilities span advisory, digital solutions, engineering and design, and program delivery, enabling organizations to navigate complexity, mitigate risk, and achieve strategic objectives. We serve a diverse range of industries, including aviation, transportation, transit, water, healthcare, energy, education, government, commercial real estate, life sciences, and technology. At Consertus, we believe our people are our greatest strength. We foster a collaborative, flexible, and inclusive environment where individuals can grow, develop their skills, and make a meaningful impact. Together, we’re transforming the way the world is planned, built, and delivered. Learn more about how Consertus is creating lasting value for clients, communities, and our people at www.consertus.com . About this Role: We are seeking a detail-oriented Professional Selection Analyst to supervise and coordinate the selection process of Architects, Engineers, and other professional consultants in accordance with school board policies and procedures and Florida State Statutes. Key Responsibilities: Manages and coordinates the review and evaluation process of proposals received in response to the Districts Request for Qaulifications/Proposals for professional services Reviews projects scope, schedules, and budgets as part of research to develop appropriate professional fee caps, terms, and conditions. Negotiates contract for professional services following established procedures and guidelines Prepares preliminary and final recommendations for approval, as well as negotiated terms and conditions, to the School Board for commissioning of design and construction of professional firms, and related services. Qualifications/Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in engineering, architecture, or construction management or equivalent required Minimum of 10 years of design, project management, and negotiating contracts for large public agencies Registration as an architect, professional engineer, or licensed general contract preferred Previous experience organizing groups and gathering information Working proficiency with MS Office Suite, particularly Word and Excel (intermediate level skills) Knowledge of computer software and technology relevant to the role, and motivation to learn new applications (e.g., SharePoint, SAP) Demonstrated ability to communicate effectively in both oral and written forms Proven ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously Additional Requirements Must be able to pass a background check in accordance with client and project requirements What’s In It For You: Comprehensive health coverage (medical, dental, and vision) Company-paid life and disability insurance Optional benefits like pet insurance, legal, and supplemental health plans 401(k) with day-one eligibility, 3% safe harbor, plus up to 2.5% company match Generous time off: 10 paid holidays and PTO starting at 15 days, growing up to 25 Access to Consertus Academy for continuous learning and development Equal Employment Opportunity Statement: Consertus is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. item.title: Us Congressional Lead Global Affairs
item.description: About the Team OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and - in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders - seek to further regulation, industry standards, and safe and beneficial development of AI tools. About the Role As a US Congressional Lead on the Global Affairs team, you will help develop strategies and advance OpenAI’s engagement with the U.S. Congress, including developing and managing relationships with House and Senate lawmakers and staff. You will support OpenAI’s U.S. Global Affairs team in meetings, briefings, hearings and other engagements with Congress. You will also facilitate collaboration with civil society and industry partners relevant to Congressional engagement and in alignment with OpenAI’s mission. OpenAI releases industry-leading research and tools. You will face new challenges as the impact of cutting edge generative AI technologies continues to be explored and as the needs of the organization evolve. Day-to-day work may encompass anything from helping to shape strategic initiatives and policy documents to preparing our leaders for engagements with government officials or representing OpenAI in private and public forums. We are looking for a self-directed and creative individual with Capitol Hill experience, experience managing private sector and civil society relationships, plus an understanding of AI-related legislative and regulatory issues and processes. This role is based in Washington, DC and may require frequent travel to participate in meetings and events with key stakeholders. We offer relocation assistance to new employees. You should thrive in this role if you: Are well versed in the issues around emerging AI technologies, especially in the U.S. Congressional context. Are an enthusiastic and effective coalition builder who thrives as a member of a high performing, peer-led global team. Are highly organized, and are used to working as an accountable individual contributor as well as a team player. Are passionate about the promise of technology and the future of artificial intelligence but thoughtful about its potential risks. We're looking for a blend of: Demonstrated experience (8+ years) and credibility in working with Republicans in the U.S. federal government, particularly the legislative branch. Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of the U.S. government, institutions, and processes, and the key policy issues and debates related to AI. Extensive experience in technology policy, with experience working with the Commerce, Judiciary, and/or Appropriations Committees. Track record of effectively working with cross-functional teams, especially communications, policy and legal teams, and aligning a diverse range of internal and external partners Sound judgment and outstanding personal integrity Ability to execute in fast and flexible environments through rapid cycles of analysis, decision, and action Excellent communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical and policy concepts to diverse audiences Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and project management skills Genuine care and knowledge about the impact of technology on society About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement . Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. For unincorporated Los Angeles County workers: we reasonably believe that criminal history may have a direct, adverse and negative relationship with the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment: protect computer hardware entrusted to you from theft, loss or damage; return all computer hardware in your possession (including the data contained therein) upon termination of employment or end of assignment; and maintain the confidentiality of proprietary, confidential, and non-public information. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. To notify OpenAI that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form . No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this link . OpenAI Global Applicant Privacy Policy At OpenAI, we believe artificial intelligence has the potential to help people solve immense global challenges, and we want the upside of AI to be widely shared. Join us in shaping the future of technology.

item.title: Director Public Policy
item.description: About Perplexity Perplexity helps people find answers, explore ideas and get things done with AI. As we grow, we want policymakers around the world to understand what we're building and how it works. Overview We're hiring a Director, Public Policy as a founding member of our policy team. Based in Washington, D.C., this role will help build and scale our engagement with governments, regulators and policy communities worldwide. Ideal candidates have built this function before, not only operated within an established team. The role requires hands-on coordination and will help set policy priorities with company leadership. We will prioritize candidates who can demonstrate resourcefulness, persistence, and a willingness to work through the details to get things done. This role reports to the Senior Director, Product, Privacy & Regulatory Legal and will operationalize our public positions set by Comms and executive leadership. What you'll do Build the program. Turn company priorities into a global engagement plan, with clear market priorities, owners and measures of progress. Scale how we work. Establish stakeholder tracking, policy monitoring and briefing standards that keep a growing team coordinated across regions. Build relationships across markets. Engage policymakers, regulators, trade associations, think tanks and civil society in the U.S. and key international markets. Anticipate change. Listen closely to policymakers to understand current priorities and emerging debates. Use expertise and trusted relationships to identify risks and raise opportunities the company may not yet see. Lead advocacy. Advance approved company positions through direct engagement and coalitions, adapting to local contexts and applicable lobbying and ethics requirements. Advise leadership. Translate political and regulatory developments into business implications and recommendations. Bring intelligence back to Legal, Comms, Product and executives. Connect policy and communications. Inform and execute the strategy Comms and executive leadership set, with clear messages and coordinated engagement across markets. Build regional capacity. Coordinate external advisers and partners, recommend future hiring priorities, and develop colleagues as the team and its reach grow. Make engagement effective. Prepare leaders for government meetings and run briefings, roundtables and product demonstrations, with clear objectives and follow-through. What we're looking for At least 10 years of relevant experience in public policy, government affairs or legislative advocacy. A record of building and scaling a policy function, program or team, ideally at a growing technology company. Experience managing policy engagement across multiple jurisdictions, including the U.S. and at least one other major market. Experience representing a company, association or clients before government. Government service is strongly preferred. A network you've built yourself, and evidence that you can establish credibility and relationships in new markets. Strong writing and judgment. You can explain complex issues plainly, advise senior leaders and know when to escalate. A hands-on approach. You can write the brief, take the meeting and handle details while building for the next stage of growth. Experience coordinating internal teams and external advisers across regions, with clear priorities and accountability. Bonus Experience hiring, managing or developing policy professionals. Experience with AI, privacy, competition, copyright or other technology policy issues. Experience on Capitol Hill, in the executive branch, or in a comparable government role outside the U.S. Registered lobbying experience and familiarity with lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements.

item.title: Texas Newsroom Legislative Reporting Intern Spring 2027
item.description: TEXAS NEWSROOM LEGISLATIVE REPORTING INTERN, SPRING 2027 WHO WE ARE: Serving the country’s fourth-largest media market, KERA reaches more than 5 million people monthly through KERA TV , KERA News , KXT , WRR and The Denton Record-Chronicle as well as through national shows Think and From the Top . For more than 65 years, North Texans have turned to KERA as a destination for community engagement and lifelong learning. As we seek to recognize and reflect our audience and communities, we encourage applicants from all backgrounds and points of view to consider employment opportunities at KERA. ABOUT THE TEXAS NEWSROOM: The Texas Newsroom is the collaboration among NPR and public radio stations in Texas, including KUT Austin, KERA North Texas, Houston Public Media and Texas Public Radio in San Antonio. We air six daily statewide newscasts, and our stations partner to produce the radio newsmagazine Texas Standard, “the national daily news show of Texas.” POSITION SUMMARY We're looking for a curious and motivated college student or recent graduate in the Austin area to join our statewide reporting team. You'll work alongside veteran journalists to cover the people, policies and debates shaping Texas. Stories you produce for radio and digital platforms will reach audiences across Texas — and potentially nationwide via NPR. This is a hands-on reporting internship where you'll develop story ideas, cover important hearings, interview lawmakers and everyday Texans, and learn how to break down complicated policy debates into engaging and accessible stories. This intern will also be paired with a veteran journalist who will serve as a mentor throughout the legislative session. Our previous interns have reported on everything from abortion legislation to the state's school voucher debate to profiles of new lawmakers navigating their first weeks at the Capitol. This is an FLSA classified non-exempt position and will report to the Managing Editor, The Texas Newsroom. WHAT YOU WILL DO: Report in person at the Texas Capitol at committee hearings, on the House and Senate floor and at press conferences and rallies. Record audio and produce newscast spots and audio features. Equipment will be provided. Write news stories and features for digital audiences. Pitch stories. Respond quickly to breaking news. C onduct research and interviews to provide context and explain the potential impact of legislation. Occasionally dive into topics outside the Legislature as assigned. As a KERA employee: Work in a manner that is consistent with KERA’s mission, vision and values; and maintain compliance with all company policies and procedures Perform additional duties as assigned This list of job duties is not exhaustive and is subject to regular reviews and updates. WHAT WILL MAKE YOU SUCCESSFUL: Qualified applicants must be current students (in an accredited degree program) or have graduated no more than 12 months prior to the start of the internship. We believe a strong organization includes employees from a range of backgrounds, with different skills, experiences, and passions. If you don't meet every job qualification but have some of these skills and think you’re the right person for the job, we'd like to hear from you. Please apply and tell us more about yourself. Strong writing and editing skills Solid understanding of AP style Knowledge of public radio BONUS IF YOU BRING: Audio editing experience Previous experience working for a daily news organization Knowledge of social media practices SALARY $16 per hour paid on a bi-weekly pay period. Interns can expect to work 15-20 hours per week. LOCATION AND SCHEDULE: The internship is in-person and based in Austin, TX. Interns should have some availability between 9am and 5pm (M-F). Hours are flexible, and we will work with you to accommodate class schedules. The internship will begin around January 11, 2027, and end June 4, 2027. There may be opportunities to extend the internship into the Summer 2027 term. HOW TO APPLY: Complete the application on KERA’s employment page and attach a resume. Add a cover letter explaining why you are interested in this internship. Include a link to an online portfolio that includes at least 3 work samples, such as audio or digital news stories for a campus publication or class assignment. APPLICATION TIMELINE: We generally close roles 2-4 weeks after posting. The hiring process may continue for several weeks after the closing of the role depending on the number of applicants. KERA is an Equal Opportunity Employer KERA believes that diversity is important to our success. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, religion, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by law.

item.title: Chief Government Affairs Officer
item.description: AAAS is one of the world’s largest multidisciplinary scientific societies and a leading publisher of cutting-edge research through its Science family of journals. Its mission is to advance science, engineering, and innovation throughout the world for the benefit of all. To fulfill this mission, AAAS has the following strategic goals: Advance scientific excellence and achievement. AAAS recognizes, inspires, and enables a robust research ecosystem that drives discovery and innovation and prepares future scientists and engineers. Foster inclusivity for scientific excellence. AAAS fosters the open and inclusive scientific enterprise that is essential for scientific excellence. Build trust among scientists and communities. AAAS builds trust among scientists and engineers and broader communities and is a valued source of accurate scientific information that is foundational to countering misinformation. Catalyze progress where science meets policy. AAAS provides actionable evidence for public policy that serves society and promotes policies that enable quality science. The Opportunity The Chief Government Affairs Officer (CGAO) leads AAAS’ government affairs and advocacy strategies in support of the association’s mission and priorities and to strengthen its role as a trusted, nonpartisan voice for science, research, and evidence-based policymaking. The CGAO is responsible for developing and executing an integrated government affairs strategy across Congress, the Administration, federal agencies, state and local governments, and other relevant policy stakeholders. As a prominent ambassador for the organization and for the American scientific community, the CGAO will build and maintain relationships with policymakers and their staffs, academic organizations, industry partners, professional societies, and others to enhance the visibility and impact of AAAS’ policy and advocacy efforts. The CGAO leads a team of talented government affairs professionals and serves as the principal internal and external advisor on federal legislative and executive branch policy developments affecting science, research, innovation, scientific integrity, research funding, and the broader science and technology ecosystem, as well as science and technology funding and policy at the state and local levels. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer and serving as an important member of the AAAS Leadership Advisory Council and Public Affairs Leadership Team, the CGAO works in close coordination with units across the organization, including Communications; Science, Policy, and Society Programs; Membership; Philanthropy and Strategic Partnerships; Publishing; and others. Key Responsibilities The Chief Government Affairs Officer (CGAO) will provide strategic leadership and oversight of AAAS' government affairs, public policy, and advocacy initiatives, advancing the organization's mission to promote science, innovation, and evidence-based policymaking. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the CGAO will lead and develop a team of government affairs professionals, strengthen relationships with policymakers and key stakeholders, and guide the organization's engagement at the federal, state, and local levels. Working collaboratively with senior leadership and cross-functional teams, the CGAO will be responsible for the following key functions: Enterprise Government Affairs Strategy Conceptualize, develop, and lead implementation of an integrated, organization-wide government affairs and advocacy strategy aligned with AAAS’ mission, goals, and initiatives. Report directly to the COO and partner closely with the COO and CEO in setting government affairs priorities and institutional positioning. Monitor science and technology legislation, policies, rules, and regulations, and identify emerging opportunities and threats affecting science, scientific institutions, research funding, and the broader science and technology ecosystem. Federal Government Affairs Lead AAAS’ federal government affairs strategy and engagement with Congress, the Administration, federal agencies, and other relevant federal stakeholders. Develop strategies to advance AAAS priorities through legislation, appropriations, regulations, executive actions, and other federal policy mechanisms. Build relationships with relevant congressional and Administration officials and their staffs. Oversee AAAS’ engagement on issues affecting federal research and development, scientific institutions, the scientific workforce, and the research ecosystem. Coordinate federal advocacy with communications, R&D budget and policy, and external coalition efforts. Maintain collaboration with other segments of the STEM community, including professional societies, academic institutions, and industry groups. Serve on internal and external advisory committees and represent AAAS on S&T coalitions. Anticipate political and policy developments and advise the COO, CEO, and senior leadership on their implications for AAAS and the broader scientific community. State & Local Government Affairs Establish and lead AAAS’ strategy for engagement with state and local governments on science, research, innovation, education, and related public policy issues. Build relationships with governors’ offices, state legislators, mayors and local officials, state agencies, national state- and local-focused associations, and other relevant stakeholders. Identify opportunities to expand AAAS’ influence beyond Washington and strengthen the organization’s role as a national resource for science-informed policymaking. Coordinate state and local government affairs with federal policy and communications priorities. Develop partnerships and coalitions that amplify AAAS’ impact at the state and local levels. Coordinate with science-for-policy work at the state and local levels in other AAAS units (e.g., AAAS Center for Scientific Evidence in Public Issues). R &D Budget and Policy Provide strategic leadership for AAAS’ work on analyzing federal research and development budgets and related science and technology policy. Oversee analysis and advocacy related to federal R&D funding, agency budgets, appropriations, and broader research policy. Ensure AAAS’ R&D budget and policy work is translated effectively into advocacy and public communications. Partner with scientific societies, research institutions, universities, industry, philanthropy, and other stakeholders to advance effective federal investment in research and innovation. Ensure the COO, CEO, and senior leadership have clear, timely, and credible analysis of developments affecting the federal R&D enterprise. Position AAAS as a leading, trusted voice on the federal research and development landscape. Establish AAAS’ strategy for analyzing state, regional, local, and private research and development budgets and related science and technology policy. Leadership and Management Serve as a leading resource on S&T policy, legislation, and R&D funding for internal (AAAS staff and members) and external (government, peer organizations) audiences. Direct advocacy programs within the Office of Government Affairs, including weekly Policy Alert, congressional briefings, policy briefs, and S&T policy workshops and trainings. Work closely and collaboratively with the Office of Communications to develop and execute a public affairs strategy that advances institutional policy and advocacy priorities. Actively and constructively contribute to AAAS-wide planning and strategy discussions. Supervise Government Affairs staff, projects, and events; plan and oversee staff professional development, vendor management, performance management, and budgeting. Supervisory Responsibilities: Manages 2 direct reports (total staff of 5): Director, Federal Affairs Deputy Director, Federal Affairs Senior Government Affairs Officer Director, R&D Budget and Policy Senior Analyst, State R&D Candidate Profile The ideal candidate will bring a combination of senior-level government affairs leadership; political, policy, and advocacy expertise; and exceptional communications judgment. Required qualifications include: Significant experience (at least 15 years) in government affairs, advocacy, strategic communications, public policy, or a closely related field. At least 5 years of relevant senior leadership experience. Deep understanding of the federal policymaking process and the political environment in Washington, DC. Strong understanding of science, technology, research, higher education, or related policy environments. Demonstrated ability to explain complex policy or technical issues clearly and persuasively to non-technical audiences. Demonstrated success building relationships with senior policymakers, government officials, media, and other influential stakeholders. Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams and in building, coaching, and mentoring a team of government affairs professionals at various career stages. Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. Excellent political judgment and the ability to operate effectively in highly sensitive and rapidly changing environments. Experience advising senior executives on high-stakes public affairs matters. Demonstrated ability to develop and execute organization-wide strategies rather than managing individual functions in isolation. Advanced university-level training leading to a bachelor’s degree in a relevant field; master’s degree preferred Soft Skills Outstanding written and oral communication skills. Highly collaborative, unifying leadership and work style, including experience leading and working as part of diverse, cross-organizational teams with colleagues at all levels. Strong record as an implementer who thrives on managing a variety of key initiatives concurrently. Ability to position government relations and advocacy discussions at both the strategic and tactical level. Self-starter that can work independently and entrepreneur

The incumbent will have primary responsibility for issues related to Medicaid. Providing internal education and policy briefings on government action and policy trends to assist in business decisions across the company. Conducting legislative, regulatory, and policy research and analysis. Developing external communications, written materials, and thought leadership to communicate CareFirsts policy perspective and advance meaningful discussion on pressing health policy issues (e.g., talking points, fact sheets, public comments, blog posts, subject matter expert panels). item.title: Attorney Director I Legislative Counsel Fda Hybrid
item.description: Attorney, Dir I (Legislative Counsel Lifestyle Medicine) - (Hybrid) Washington, D.C. The American Medical Association (AMA) is the nation's largest professional Association of physicians and a non-profit organization. We are a unifying voice and powerful ally for America's physicians, the patients they care for, and the promise of a healthier nation. To be part of the AMA is to be part of our Mission to promote the art and science of medicine and the betterment of public health. At AMA, our mission to improve the health of the nation starts with our people. We foster an inclusive, people-first culture where every employee is empowered to perform at their best. Together, we advance meaningful change in health care and the communities we serve. We encourage and support professional development for our employees, and we are dedicated to social responsibility. We invite you to learn more about us and we look forward to getting to know you. We have an opportunity at our corporate offices in Washington D.C. for an Attorney, Dir I (Legislative Counsel Lifestyle Medicine) - (Hybrid) on our Government Affairs team. This is a hybrid position reporting into our Washington, DC office, requiring 3 days a week in the office. 25 Massachusetts Avenue, NW, Washington, DC 20001-7400 USA As an Attorney, Dir I (Legislative Counsel Lifestyle Medicine), under the supervision of the Director, you will provide legal counsel and support on legislative, regulatory, and advocacy matters impacting the American Medical Association (AMA), with an emphasis on FDA, drugs, lifestyle medicine, and other issues of interest to the AMA. This role involves analyzing and interpreting complex legislation, regulations, and judicial opinions to inform and guide AMA Advocacy staff, Senior Management, Council on Legislation, Board of Trustees, AMA House of Delegates, and other constituencies. Responsible for preparing AMA testimony, brief witnesses, and draft strategic advocacy materials to advance AMA policy objectives. Independently lead an assigned portfolio of significant legislative and regulatory issues, serving as a strategic legal advisor and developing recommended policy and advocacy approaches within the portfolio. RESPONSIBILITIES: Legislative & Regulatory Advocacy Serves as internal expert and provides legal, legislative, and regulatory advice to Advocacy units, as well as other AMA business units on a wide variety of complex AMA issues, focusing on FDA and lifestyle medicine. Advances AMA’s legislative and regulatory agenda by identifying and analyzing emerging federal legislation and regulation, assessing implications for AMA priorities, and developing recommended policy and advocacy approaches on assigned issue. Identifies AMA position on legislation and regulation and/or identifies the need to develop a position in the absence of pertinent policy and prepares/coordinates formal AMA response to proposed regulations. Represents the AMA to external groups and participates in coalition meetings to advocate policy goals of the Organization. Prepares a broad array of persuasive advocacy documents, draft comment letters, and strategic communications on assigned issue areas for Congressional, Administrative, and grassroots operations of the Washington Office. Develops responses to oral and written inquiries from Congress, the Administration, other organizations (i.e. the Federation, member physicians, and others) regarding AMA policy. Develops arguments and “talking points” to assist lobbying and grassroots communication efforts and contributes to direct issue lobbying as necessary and appropriate. Briefs national medical specialty societies, state medical societies, and various AMA Sections or their representatives on request. Prepares AMA written testimony and oral statements on assigned issue areas to be presented by Board of Trustees members before Congress, federal agencies, and boards. Extensively prepares and briefs AMA witnesses for formal appearances in public forums, including preparation of effective responses to anticipated questions. Leads a portfolio based on subject matter expertise, determining the analytical framework and recommended approach, coordinating work across Advocacy and other business unites, and driving execution as issues evolve. Serve as a subject matter expert across business units and is available to guide/mentor junior attorneys as needed. Policy Development & Advisory Advises Council members on legislative and political aspects of top issues, especially the Executive Committee and Workgroup members, and keeps them apprised of the status of key legislative and regulatory issues. Assists the Reference Committee B Secretary at the AMA Annual or Interim meeting as assigned Develops and delivers presentations to specialty and state societies, or other organizations, on relevant legislative or regulatory issues of importance to the House of Medicine. Prepares and presents substantive written and oral issue briefings on assigned issue areas; develops proposed policy and advocacy approaches when existing AMA policy does not clearly address an emerging issue; and provides recommendations to the Council on Legislation at its formal meetings. May include other responsibilities as assigned REQUIREMENTS: J.D. degree and active membership in good standing in at least one state Bar required 10+ years professional experience and 3+ years health law experience required; previous legislative, federal agency, or association experience is highly preferred Subject matter expertise of the U.S. Congressional, legislative, and/or federal regulatory process required Demonstrated strategic judgment and ability to independently lead complex, cross-functional advocacy initiatives Proven experience with physician-related issues in a wide variety of health law subjects such as FDA, lifestyle medicine, and drugs Extensive knowledge of the AMA’s and Federation’s organizational structure and policy development processes highly preferred Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills required Strong verbal communication and presentation skills Strong writing and editing skills to compose and edit polished and persuasive legislative and regulatory advocacy documents to meet short deadlines Strong project leadership and organizational skills to prioritize complex work and coordinate cross-functional activity Interpersonal skills to include persuasiveness and relationship building Political acumen Some travel required This role is an exempt position, and the salary range for this position is $153,355-$207,144. This is the lowest to highest salary we believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s pay within the salary range will be determined by a variety of factors including but not limited to business consideration and geographical location, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience. Employees are also eligible to participate in an incentive plan. To learn more about the American Medical Association’s benefits offerings, please click here . The AMA offers competitive salaries, including an incentive plan and excellent benefits. Our office is a business casual environment, and we respect work-life balance. The American Medical Association is located near Union Station and the Capitol in Washington D.C. We are an equal opportunity employer, committed to diversity in our workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment. As an EOE/AA employer, the American Medical Association will not discriminate in its employment practices due to an applicant’s race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity and veteran or disability status. THE AMA IS COMMITTED TO IMPROVING THE HEALTH OF THE NATION

item.title: Deputy Director Elections
item.description: Summary The Deputy Director of Elections supports the Elections Director in overseeing the daily operations and long-range planning of the Elections Department. This position works closely with all areas of the department and its vendors to ensure continuity of operations and the successful administration of elections throughout Delaware County. The Deputy Director provides strategic leadership, operational oversight, and coordination to support elections that are secure, accurate, transparent, and accessible to Delaware County voters. Essential Duties Support the Elections Director in overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Elections Department. Assist with long-range and strategic planning for election operations. Plan, coordinate, and direct election activities involving more than 2,000 full-time, temporary, and Election Day workers. Support election operations serving approximately 330,000 voters during each election. Coordinate activities across all areas of the Elections Department to ensure continuity of operations. Work closely with departmental staff, County departments, outside vendors, and other stakeholders. Assist with ballot system preparation and testing. Support poll worker recruitment, training, and coordination. Assist with voter registration activities and election-related voter services. Support ballot processing, audits, and election results reporting. Assist with campaign finance activities and other election administration responsibilities. Develop and maintain procedures that support secure, accurate, and transparent election processes. Identify operational needs and assist with implementing improvements to departmental processes. Provide leadership and guidance to staff to ensure deadlines, regulatory requirements, and departmental goals are met. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications High school diploma or equivalent required. Bachelor’s degree preferred. Experience should include a combination of responsibilities in at least two or more of the following areas: Ballot system preparation and testing Poll worker training Voter registration Ballot processing and audits Election results reporting Campaign finance Other related election administration functions Additional Information Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Ability to clearly plan and direct election operations. Ability to work effectively with department staff and vendors. Strong organizational and communication skills. Ability to manage multiple responsibilities related to election operations.

item.title: Project Manager Ppm Tool Selection Implementation
item.description: Our client, a large national accounting and advisory firm, is replacing its enterprise Project & Portfolio Management (PPM) platform. They need an experienced project manager to lead the effort from vendor selection through implementation. You'll help the firm's Enterprise PMO finalize a tool choice by December 2026, then lead implementation from January to a target go-live in March 2027. The role averages about 10 hours per week and flexes to 15–20 hours during peak periods. The flexible, part-time schedule suits an experienced practitioner looking for a meaningful engagement alongside other commitments. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Lead the PPM vendor selection process: refine requirements with the portfolio team, facilitate demos and scoring, and drive to a recommendation by December 2026. Serve as an objective, vendor-neutral advisor, keeping the evaluation grounded in the firm's requirements. Build and manage the implementation plan, schedule, risks/issues log, and status reporting from kickoff through go-live. Coordinate with the selected vendor's implementation team and actively manage resource-availability risk against the timeline. Partner with IT to plan the replacement of data pipelines and system integrations tied to the current platform. Plan and oversee data migration from the legacy tool, including validation and cutover. Lead internal change management and training for product line managers, PMO staff, project managers, and IT. Run a separate workstream for a client-facing user group with a high-touch, white-glove approach. Keep stakeholders, from PMO leadership to individual project managers, informed with clear, timely updates. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 7+ years of project management experience. Led at least one enterprise PPM tool implementation end to end. Experience in a PMO leadership role, such as PMO manager, lead, or director. Experience running a structured software evaluation: requirements gathering, vendor demos, and weighted scoring. Experience coordinating system integrations and data migration with IT teams. Track record driving user adoption and change management for a new enterprise tool. Available roughly 10 hours per week (up to 15–20 in peak weeks) from November 1, 2026 through March 2027. NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS Background in professional services, accounting, or consulting firm environments. Familiarity with enterprise PMO intake, governance, and portfolio prioritization processes. PMP certification and/or a formal change management credential (e.g., Prosci). Experience delivering alongside other large enterprise system rollouts. TOOLS & ENVIRONMENT Enterprise PPM platform (replacement to be selected as part of this engagement). Standard collaboration and reporting tools (e.g., Microsoft 365). IDEAL CANDIDATE PROFILE You treat internal stakeholders as clients, and responsiveness is second nature. You acknowledge requests within one business day, even when the answer is "I'll find out." You're a seasoned practitioner who can step into a part-time role and create momentum quickly. You bring structure while budget and priorities are still taking shape. You stay neutral during vendor selection and earn trust by being candid about tradeoffs. You're comfortable moving between PMO leadership, IT, and end users, and you know that a new tool succeeds only when people actually adopt it. This position requires the successful completion of a criminal background check. No screening will be initiated until an offer has been made. All background checks are consistent with federal and state laws and regulations including applicable second chance hiring laws.

item.title: Government Affairs Regional Manager 0698 Hybrid
item.description: Work for Our Water Resources. Help protect one of Florida’s most vital resources — water — with a career at the Southwest Florida Water Management District (District). The District is a government agency whose mission is to protect water resources, minimize flood risks, and ensure the public’s water needs are met. We serve a population of nearly 6 million people in west-central Florida as directed by state law. Join our Government and Community Affairs Office Here is your opportunity to serve as the District's local liaison for local elected officials, county and municipal utilities, appointed officials, and business and community leaders. This position will be based out of the District's Sarasota office. Geographical coverage includes Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, and Charlotte counties. The mission of this position is to oversee coordinating and implementing the District's intergovernmental strategies for the execution of operational and strategic priorities and to address local water resource issues. To succeed in this position, the successful candidate must possess the following: self motivation and discipline, strong sense of ethics, proven relationship building, conflict management, strong familiarity with local government and community affairs, and consensus building. The District supports employees who prefer a hybrid work schedule so that they can enjoy their time outside of the District through work-life balance. The successful candidate must be a Florida resident and willing to reside or relocate to the Southern Planning Region of the District: Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, and Charlotte counties. District employees are offered an excellent total rewards package that includes : Florida Retirement System (FRS) District Total Contribution 14.03% 9 paid holidays (+ 1 floating holiday) Generous vacation and sick leave Paid Parental Leave, including Maternity, Bonding and Family Supportive Work Program Medical and dental insurance (91- 97% District paid) Vision insurance Deferred Compensation Program Basic and voluntary life and AD&D insurance Long-term disability (District Paid) Prescription drug coverage & mail order program Health savings & flexible spending accounts Flexible schedule for work-life balance Legal and Identity Theft protection Wellness program Public service loan forgiveness qualified employer Tuition reimbursement ($5,250/year) State adoption benefit qualified employer Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Transfer in years of service for other public sector work – towards the FRS program and sick time Starting Compensation : Government Affairs Professional 3 $61,254.00 - $84,422.50 Government Affairs Professional 4 $66,180.00 - $91,203.50 The starting salary ranges are included for the Government Affairs Professional profile which reflects the minimum to approximately 50% of the respective pay grades . The starting salary will be based on the education and experience of the successful candidate. The District conducts annual performance evaluations that may award applicable pay increases based on positive employee performance. Essential Functions Develops and maintains relationships with local, state, and federal government elected officials and staff, key state agency personnel, chambers of commerce, and community-based organizations. Monitors and participates in local commission and council meetings, local and regional community boards, and provides government affairs support to external constituents. Provides internal and external constituent service. Provides support to internal bureaus and represents the District throughout a defined geographical region. Develops, coordinates, and/or administers responses to inquiries regarding the organization. Provides counsel and policy-related assistance to department directors and executive staff. Participates in District emergency management activities and other departmental activities and performs other duties as needed. Provides ability to work with diverse stakeholders, build mutually-beneficial relationships, resolve conflicts and work with little supervision. Participates in District emergency management activities and other departmental activities and performs other duties as needed. Working Conditions Work is performed in a standard office environment with required travel to District service offices and other organizations' work locations. Early morning, holiday, evening, or weekend hours may be required. Will be required to work extended hours and/or on an irregular work schedule, as many local government meetings are held during evening hours. Approximately 60­ to 80 percent of the time may be spent outside the office attending meetings, participating in special events and providing assistance, coordination, and/or support to elected officials, board members, governmental and agency staff, and general public. Considerable travel, including some overnight, is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. During emergency management activities or incidents, employee may be subject to work outside of regularly scheduled work hours, or required to be on call, including nights, weekends or holidays in support of District operations. Required Credentials for Government Affairs Regional Manager Government Affairs Regional Manager 3 Bachelors degree, or higher, in business administration, communications, public relations, or related field and Four (4) years related work experience in public relations, communications, or business related work experience OR Associates degree from an accredited college or university and Six (6) years related work experience in public relations, communications, or business related work experience OR High School diploma or equivalent and Eight (8) years related work experience in public relations, communications. Valid driver’s license Government Affairs Regional Manager 4 Masters degree, or higher, in business administration, communications, public relations, or related field and Six (6) years related work experience in public relations, communications, or business related work experience OR Bachelors degree from an accredited college or university and Eight (8) years related work experience in public relations, communications, or business related work experience OR Associates or equivalent and Ten (10) years related work experience in public relations, communications. Valid driver’s license Preferred Credentials for Government Affairs Regional Manager Experience working with local governments within coverage area (Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, and Charlotte counties) Application Process The District will determine eligibility for employment solely from the information provided on a District employment application. All applicants are required to complete, in full, the District employment application. Incomplete applications will not be considered. A resume will not be considered as a substitute for the required District application for the purpose of qualification. Applicants who are within 30 days of graduation, if selected are not allowed to start until all minimum qualifications are met. Additional Details This position is typically scheduled to work 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday, out of the Sarasota, FL office, and is responsible for coordination activities in Manatee, Sarasota, DeSoto, and Charlotte counties. This position requires flexibility to work frequent evening hours and occasional weekends. This position is eligible for compensatory time for hours worked over 40 hours, in a week. item.title: Coordinator Legal And Public Government Affairs
item.description: At NASCAR, you will work alongside passionate people creating experiences fans feel and helping shape the future of sports and entertainment. NASCAR is seeking a Coordinator, Legal and Public & Government Affairs to: Help shape the initiatives and relationships that support NASCAR's legal, legislative, and public affairs priorities. Drive operational excellence through effective coordination, organization, and administrative support across multiple functions. Create seamless experiences for internal stakeholders, government partners, and guests attending NASCAR events. Advance key business objectives by supporting the processes, communications, and logistics that enable strategic decisions and stakeholder engagement. ...based in Daytona Beach, Florida . What You'll Do Provide administrative support for the Legal and Public & Government Affairs teams, including scheduling meetings, maintaining records, generating reports, and managing departmental workflows. Coordinate guest attendance at NASCAR events, including preparing itineraries, processing guest information, and supporting credentialing requirements. Draft form agreements, including access and license agreements, photography agreements, non-disclosure agreements, and other legal documents under attorney supervision while maintaining accurate records within legal systems. Support department operations through invoice processing, travel coordination, internal communications assistance, and management of sensitive legal, legislative, financial, and executive-level information. Maintain strict confidentiality and exercise sound judgment while supporting legal matters, government affairs initiatives, and executive priorities. Prioritize and manage multiple assignments simultaneously while adapting to changing legislative calendars, race schedules, and departmental needs. Assist with internal communications related to NASCAR's Troops to the Track and Honor and Remember programs. Communicate professionally with internal and external stakeholders via phone, email, and written correspondence. What You'll Bring Associate degree from a two-year college or technical school, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Six months to one year of related administrative, legal, government affairs, or business support experience. Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and the ability to learn new systems and processes quickly. Strong attention to detail with the ability to maintain accuracy in data entry, document preparation, and legal system administration. Excellent organizational, communication, typing, and spelling skills. Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with professionalism and discretion. Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and adapt to shifting business needs with minimal supervision. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment. Commitment to maintaining a positive, collaborative team culture. Why This Role? Help support the work that keeps NASCAR moving forward. In this role, you'll provide critical coordination and administrative support for legal, legislative, and public affairs initiatives, helping ensure key business operations, stakeholder engagements, and executive priorities run smoothly and efficiently. Your attention to detail, discretion, and ability to navigate competing priorities will directly contribute to NASCAR's ability to build meaningful relationships, support strategic initiatives, and strengthen one of the most recognized brands in sports and entertainment. Behind every race weekend are talented people helping shape the future of sports and entertainment. If you are ready to make an impact alongside passionate teammates, we encourage you to apply. Explore this opportunity and apply at www.careers.nascar.com . Our people are the key to our success. That is why we offer competitive compensation, a comprehensive benefits package focused on wellness, and opportunities to grow and develop both personally and professionally. NASCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to conducting recruitment and hiring activities in a fair, ethical, and legally compliant manner . In support of this commitment, all employment decisions are based on job-related qualifications, skills, experience, and performance, and are made without discrimination based on any legally protected characteristic, including but not limited to race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation or gender identity, national origin, age, military or veteran status, disability, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law, including socioeconomic, marital, parental, or caregiving status. Follow us on LinkedIn and X for future opportunities and company news. We are looking for your voice, your ideas, and your perspective. To help us get to know you accurately and keep the process fair for everyone, we ask that interviews and assessments be completed without the support of AI-generated content or automated assistance.
